lines: Speed · 40 ft., fly 80 ft. (hover), swim 40 ft.

gm.title: Description
lines: Gravity bends around this lake-dwelling gem dragon. Its breath can pin opponents in place while it projects itself into two spaces.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Amphibious. Breathe air and water.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). Turn a failed saving throw into a success.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +12 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 18 (2d10 + 7) piercing damage plus 9 (2d8) force damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +12 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 11 (1d8 + 7) slashing damage.
Singularity Breath (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 90-ft. cone makes a DC 20 Strength save. On a failure it takes 45 (10d8) force damage and has speed 0 until the start of the dragon’s next turn. On a success it takes half damage and keeps its speed.

gm.title: Spellcasting (Psionics)
lines:
As an action, cast one of these spells using Intelligence (spell save DC 18). No components are required.
1/day each. Blink, Control Water, Dispel Magic, Protection from Evil and Good, Sending.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines:
Change Shape. Become a Small or Medium creature by magic. Only size changes among the dragon’s statistics. The form ends at 0 HP or when the dragon spends another bonus action to end it.
Psychic Step. Teleport to a visible, unoccupied space within 60 ft.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
The dragon has 3 legendary actions. Use one option at the end of another creature’s turn, then subtract its cost. The dragon regains spent legendary actions at the start of its own turn.
Claw (1 action). Make one Claw attack.
Psionics (2 actions). Use Psychic Step or Spellcasting.
Explosive Crystal (3 actions). Pick a visible point within 60 ft. Each creature in a 20-ft.-radius sphere centered there must pass a DC 20 Dexterity save or take 13 (3d8) force damage and fall prone.

gm.title: Lair actions
lines:
On initiative count 20, losing initiative ties, choose one option. The dragon cannot use the same lair action two rounds in a row.
Beguiling Whisper. Whisper to one creature within telepathy range. On a failed DC 15 Wisdom save, it is charmed until initiative count 20 next round and follows the dragon’s commands as well as it can, except commands that directly harm it.
Imprisoning Force. Cast Forcecage without components (spell save DC 18). That cage ends early if the dragon uses this option again or dies.
Spatial Projection. Choose a space in the lair large enough for the dragon. Until initiative count 20 next round, the dragon occupies its original space and that space at once. When it moves or acts, choose which copy does so. An attack or effect that reaches both copies affects the dragon only once.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:
One or more of these effects can occur near the lair.
Background Check. Once a day the dragon can cast Legend Lore without components about a person, place, or object within 1 mile of the lair.
Crystal Profusion. Amethyst and geodes form on muddy shores and lake beds within 6 miles.
Thriving Wildlife. Fish and other aquatic Beasts flourish in waters within 6 miles. Foraging there produces twice the usual food.
Watery Sight. As an action the dragon can cast Clairvoyance without components on any body of water within 6 miles.
On death, nearby aquatic populations return to normal over 1d10 days. Existing amethysts remain and new crystals form at their ordinary rate.

lines: In its lair, the dragon is CR 17 (18,000 XP).

The dragon regains spent legendary actions at the start of its turn. Detect. The dragon makes a Wisdom (Perception) check. Tail Attack. The dragon makes a tail attack. Wing Attack (Costs 2 Actions). The dragon beats its wings. Each creature within 10 feet of the dragon must succeed on a DC 19 Dexterity saving throw or take 13 (2d6 + 6) bludgeoning damage and be knocked prone. The dragon can then fly up to half its flying speed.

lines: Speed · 40 ft., climb 40 ft., fly 80 ft.

gm.title: Description
lines: An adult copper dragon enjoys riddles and uses false walls and decoy treasures to guard its hoard.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Legendary Resistance (3/day). When the dragon fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. The dragon may use Frightful Presence before making one Bite and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +11 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 17 (2d10 + 6) piercing damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +11 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 13 (2d6 + 6) slashing damage.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +11 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit 15 (2d8 + 6) bludgeoning damage.
Frightful Presence. The dragon chooses creatures within 120 ft. that are aware of it. They must pass a DC 16 Wisdom save or become Frightened for 1 minute, repeating the save at the end of each of their turns to end the effect. A successful initial or repeat save or any other end to the effect grants immunity to this dragon’s Frightful Presence for 24 hours.
Breath Weapons (recharge 5–6). Choose Acid Breath or Slowing Breath.
Acid Breath. Creatures in a 60-ft. line, 5 ft. wide, make a DC 18 Dexterity save. They take 54 (12d8) acid damage on a failure or half on a success.
Slowing Breath. Creatures in a 60-ft. cone must pass a DC 18 Constitution save. On a failure, a creature has half speed, cannot take reactions, and can make at most one attack on its turn. It may take an action or a bonus action on its turn, not both. The effects last 1 minute and end early on a successful repeat save at the end of any of the creature’s turns.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
The dragon has 3 legendary actions. It can use one option at the end of another creature’s turn. Spent actions return at the start of the dragon’s turn. It cannot use these options while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act, or while surprised until it finishes its first turn.
Detect (1 action). Make a Wisdom (Perception) check.
Tail Attack (1 action). Make one Tail attack.
Wing Attack (2 actions). Creatures within 10 ft. must pass a DC 19 Dexterity save or take 13 (2d6 + 6) bludgeoning damage and fall Prone. The dragon can then fly up to half its flying speed.

gm.title: Lair actions
lines:
On initiative count 20, losing ties, choose one effect. The dragon cannot use a lair action while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act, or while surprised until it finishes its first turn.
Stone Spikes. Choose a visible ground point within 120 ft. Spikes appear in a 20-ft. radius and work as Spike Growth. The area is difficult terrain. A creature moving into or within it takes 2d4 piercing damage per 5 ft. traveled. The spikes persist until the dragon uses this option again or dies.
Mud. Choose a visible 10-ft. square of ground within 120 ft. that turns into mud 3 ft. deep. Creatures on that ground when the mud appears must pass a DC 15 Dexterity save or sink and become Restrained. A creature can use its action to make a DC 15 Strength check to free itself or a creature it can reach. Moving 1 ft. through the mud costs 2 ft. of movement. On initiative count 20 next round, the mud hardens and the Strength check DC becomes 20.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines: Choose one or more of these effects around a legendary dragon’s lair. Stone terrain and objects within 6 miles can display magical carvings of the dragon smiling. Within 1 mile, Tiny beasts that cannot normally speak can magically speak and understand Draconic. They praise the dragon and cannot reveal its whereabouts. Intelligent creatures within 1 mile are prone to giggling even at serious things. When the dragon dies, carvings fade over 1d10 days and the other effects end immediately.

gm.title: Variant spellcasting
lines: If using the optional dragon rule, choose 3 spells of level 4 or lower. The dragon can cast each once per day without material components. Its Charisma spell save DC is 16, and its spell attack bonus is +8. The DM chooses the spells.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Monster Manual (2014), pp. 86 and 111–112. Legendary and lair action timing follows the official errata.

lines:

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:

Claw (1 action). Make one Claw attack.
Psionics (2 actions). Use Psychic Step or Spellcasting.
Starlight Strike (3 actions). A visible creature within 60 ft. must pass a DC 17 Dexterity save or take 31 (9d6) radiant damage.

gm.title: Lair actions
lines:
On initiative count 20, losing initiative ties, choose one option. The dragon cannot use the same lair action two rounds in a row.
Beguiling Whisper. Whisper to one creature within telepathy range. On a failed DC 15 Wisdom save, it is charmed until initiative count 20 next round and follows the dragon’s commands as well as it can, except commands that directly harm it.
Ice Passage. Open a passage through up to 5 ft. of ice or snow. The opening can be up to 30 ft. high and wide.
Starlight’s Gleam. Choose a visible point in the lair and fill a 10-ft.-radius sphere with dim light. Each other creature there when the light appears must pass a DC 15 Dexterity save or take 13 (2d12) radiant damage and glow. Attacks against glowing creatures have advantage. Those creatures cannot hide or benefit from invisibility. The light and glow end at initiative count 20 next round.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:
One or more of these effects can occur near the lair.
Clear Skies. Except for magical weather, the lair has clear skies, no precipitation, light winds, and the best visibility the time of day allows.
Crystal Profusion. Quartz forms in natural stone within 6 miles, particularly where natural light reaches it.
Icy Sight. As an action the dragon can cast Clairvoyance without components on ice or quartz within 6 miles.
Positive Energy. A creature finishing a long rest within 6 miles recovers two additional spent Hit Dice.
Thriving Wildlife. Animals flourish within 6 miles. Checks to hunt, fish, or trap for food have advantage.
On death, the extra Hit Dice recovery ends at once and animal populations settle over 1d10 days. Existing quartz remains and new crystals form at their ordinary rate.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
The dragon has 3 legendary actions. Spend them one option at a time at the end of another creature's turn. It regains them at the start of its turn. It can't use them while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act, or while surprised until it finishes its first turn.
Detect (1 action). Make a Wisdom (Perception) check.
Tail Attack (1 action). Make a Tail attack.
Wing Attack (2 actions). Each creature within 10 ft. makes a DC 22 Dexterity save. On a failure it takes 15 (2d6 + 8) bludgeoning damage and falls Prone. The dragon can then fly up to half its flying speed.

gm.title: Lair actions
lines:

Foresight. The dragon has advantage on attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws until the next round's initiative count 20.
Dream Banishment. One creature the dragon can see within 120 ft. makes a DC 15 Charisma save. On a failure it is banished to a dream plane the dragon imagines. The creature can use its action to make a Charisma check contested by the dragon's, escaping if it wins. The banishment also ends on the next round's initiative count 20. The creature returns to the space it left or the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:

Warning Mist. Within 6 miles of the lair, opalescent mist doesn't obscure vision. If evil creatures approach the dragon or non-evil creatures in the mist, the mist takes eerie shapes as a warning.

All these effects end immediately when the dragon dies.

lines: Under the optional dragon spellcasting rule, choose 7 spells of 5th level or lower. The dragon uses Charisma to cast each once per day without material components. Its spell save DC is 21 and its spell attack bonus is +13. The DM chooses the spells.

Within 1 mile, only magic can track the dragon unless it chooses to leave signs. Plants part for it in this area. It ignores obstacles and damage from ordinary plants, including the thickets.
Birds and rodents within 1 mile relay sights and sounds to the dragon. Large game is conspicuously absent.
On the dragon's death, the animals lose their link immediately. Within 1d10 days, the thickets lose their thorns and become ordinary plants and difficult terrain.

lines: Sulfurous Impersonation. The oblex produces a double of a Medium or smaller creature whose memories it stole. It looks, feels, and sounds like that creature but smells faintly of sulfur. The oblex can impersonate 1d4 + 1 distinct creatures. A slime tether up to 120 ft. long links each double to the oblex. The oblex occupies its own space and the doubles' spaces at the same time. The tether is immune to damage. If no opening at least 1 inch wide connects the double to the body, the tether severs and the double disappears.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 198.

gm.title: Skill choice
lines: Choose one of Arcana, History, Nature, or Religion. The oblex has a +7 bonus in that skill.

gm.title: References
lines: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 198 · https://5e.tools/bestiary.html#adult%20oblex_mpmm

gm.title: Description
lines: An oblex steals memories and sends out convincing doubles of its victims. A faint sulfur smell can give a double away.

gm.title: Senses
lines: Blindsight 60 ft. The oblex is blind beyond that range.

gm.title: Condition immunities
lines: Blinded, charmed, deafened, exhaustion and prone.

gm.title: Other skill proficiency
lines: Give the oblex one of Arcana +7, History +7, Nature +7 or Religion +7.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Amorphous. The oblex can pass through openings 1 inch wide without squeezing.
Aversion to Fire. Taking fire damage gives it disadvantage on attacks and ability checks through the end of its next turn.

gm.title: Innate Spellcasting
lines:
The oblex casts with Intelligence (spell save DC 15) and needs no components.
3/day each. Charm Person at 5th level, Color Spray, Detect Thoughts and Hold Person at 3rd level.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Pseudopod attack and use Eat Memories.
Pseudopod. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage plus 5 (2d4) psychic damage.
Eat Memories. Choose one visible creature within 5 ft. It makes a DC 15 Wisdom save. Constructs, oozes, plants and undead automatically succeed. On a failure, the target takes 18 (4d8) psychic damage and is memory drained until it finishes a short or long rest or benefits from Greater Restoration or Heal. While drained, it subtracts 1d4 from every attack roll and ability check. Each further instance of memory drain increases the die by one step, from d4 to d6 to d8 and so on. When the die reaches d20, the creature falls unconscious for 1 hour and the effect ends after that hour. Whenever the oblex drains a creature, it learns that creature’s languages and gains its proficiencies except saving throw proficiencies.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines: Sulfurous Impersonation. Extrude a double of a Medium or smaller creature whose memories the oblex has stolen. It looks, feels and sounds like the original, with a faint smell of sulfur. The oblex can impersonate 1d4 + 1 creatures at a time. Each double shares the oblex’s body and occupies its own space alongside the main body. A slime tether reaches up to 120 ft. from the main body to each double. Damage cannot break the tether. If no path with at least 1 inch of clearance connects the two, the tether breaks and the double disappears.

gm.title: Description
lines: An adult red dragon restored to its own skeleton by the spirit bound to its phylactery gem.

gm.title: Template
lines: Apply the printed dracolich template to the Adult Red Dragon. Change its type to undead and add the listed resistances, immunities and Magic Resistance. The book gives no separate red dracolich stat block or CR or XP adjustment. This profile carries over the base dragon's CR 17 and 18,000 XP.

gm.title: Condition immunities
lines: Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Paralyzed and Poisoned.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Legendary Resistance (3/day). Turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Magic Resistance. Roll saving throws against spells and other magical effects with advantage.
Undead Nature. It needs no air, food, drink or sleep.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. The dracolich may first use Frightful Presence. It then makes one Bite and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +14 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 19 (2d10 + 8) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) fire damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +14 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 15 (2d6 + 8) slashing damage.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +14 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit 17 (2d8 + 8) bludgeoning damage.
Frightful Presence. Choose any creatures within 120 ft. that are aware of the dracolich. Each makes a DC 19 Wisdom save or is Frightened for 1 minute. A target can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. A creature that saves or whose fear ends is immune to this dracolich's Frightful Presence for 24 hours.
Fire Breath (recharge 5–6). Creatures in a 60-ft. cone make a DC 21 Dexterity save. Failure deals 63 (18d6) fire damage. Success halves it.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
The dracolich has 3 legendary actions and spends them one option at a time at the end of another creature's turn. It regains them at the start of its turn. It can't use them while incapacitated or otherwise unable to act, or before its first turn if surprised.
Detect (1 action). Make a Wisdom (Perception) check.
Tail Attack (1 action). Make a Tail attack.
Wing Attack (2 actions). Each creature within 10 ft. makes a DC 22 Dexterity save. On a failure, it takes 15 (2d6 + 8) bludgeoning damage and falls Prone. The dracolich can then fly up to half its flying speed.

gm.title: Phylactery
lines: When the body is destroyed, the spirit returns to its gem if the gem and body are on the same plane. If the gem then touches another dragon's corpse, the spirit can animate that body and return as a dracolich. If the gem is on another plane when the body is destroyed, the spirit passes into the afterlife.

gm.title: Lair actions
lines:
If the DM retains the adult red dragon's lair actions, use these options. The template also allows the DM to remove them or substitute new ones.
On initiative count 20, losing ties, choose one option that was not used the previous round. The creature can't use a lair action while incapacitated or otherwise unable to act, or before its first turn if surprised.
Magma Geyser. Choose a ground point the dracolich can see within 120 ft. Magma erupts in a 5-ft.-radius, 20-ft.-high column. Each creature in it makes a DC 15 Dexterity save. Failure deals 21 (6d6) fire damage. Success halves it.
Tremor. Each other creature on the ground within 60 ft. of the dracolich makes a DC 15 Dexterity save or falls Prone.
Volcanic Gas. Choose a visible point within 120 ft. A 20-ft.-radius sphere of gas spreads around corners and is lightly obscured. It lasts until initiative count 20 of the next round. Each creature starting its turn inside makes a DC 13 Constitution save or is Poisoned until the end of its turn. A creature poisoned this way is also Incapacitated.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines: If using the original lair's regional effects, small earthquakes are common within 6 miles of the lair. Water sources within 1 mile are unnaturally warm and sulfurous. Rocky fissures within 1 mile form portals to the Elemental Plane of Fire and admit creatures from that plane. These effects fade over 1d10 days after the dracolich is destroyed.

gm.title: Variant spellcasting
lines: Under the optional dragon spellcasting rule, choose five spells of 5th level or lower. The dracolich can cast each once per day without material components. Its Charisma spell save DC is 19 and its spell attack bonus is +11. The book leaves the spell choices to the DM.

Add immunity to the charmed, frightened, paralyzed, and poisoned conditions, and to exhaustion. Give it advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Use the dragon’s regular combat actions. The spirit can inhabit another dragon’s corpse if it is brought into contact with the gem on the same plane.

lines:

Claw (1 action). Make one Claw attack.
Psionics (2 actions). Use Psychic Step or Spellcasting.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:

Stony Sight. As an action the dragon can cast Clairvoyance without components on any natural stone formation within 6 miles.
Telepathic Enhancement. A creature’s innate or magical telepathy range doubles while within 1 mile, including telepathy from Rary’s Telepathic Bond.
Thriving Wildlife. Giant Spiders gather within 6 miles.
On death, telepathy returns to normal at once and giant spider populations return to normal over 1d10 days. Existing crystals and sapphires remain and new ones form at their ordinary rate.

gm.title: Description
lines: This dragon's high frill and chin spikes frame a gleaming silver face. Silver dragons befriend humanoids and collect relics of their history.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Legendary Resistance (3/day). The dragon can turn a failed saving throw into a success.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. The dragon may first use Frightful Presence. It then makes one Bite and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +13 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 19 (2d10 + 8) piercing damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +13 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 15 (2d6 + 8) slashing damage.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +13 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit 17 (2d8 + 8) bludgeoning damage.
Frightful Presence. Choose any creatures within 120 ft. that are aware of the dragon. Each makes a DC 18 Wisdom save or becomes Frightened for 1 minute. An affected creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. A creature that saves or whose fear ends gains immunity to this dragon's Frightful Presence for 24 hours.
Breath Weapons (recharge 5–6). Use one of the following breaths.
Cold Breath. Each creature in a 60-ft. cone makes a DC 20 Constitution save. Failure deals 58 (13d8) cold damage. Success halves it.
Paralyzing Breath. Each creature in a 60-ft. cone makes a DC 20 Constitution save or becomes Paralyzed for 1 minute. An affected creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
Change Shape. The dragon magically changes into a humanoid or beast of its CR or lower or returns to dragon form. It returns to dragon form on death. The dragon chooses whether its equipment merges into the form or stays with it. In the new form, it keeps its alignment, hit points, Hit Dice, speech, proficiencies, Legendary Resistance, lair actions, Intelligence, Wisdom, Charisma, and this action. Use the form's other statistics and capabilities. The dragon gains none of the form's class features, legendary actions, lair actions, or regional effects.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
The dragon has 3 legendary actions. Spend them one option at a time at the end of another creature's turn. It regains them at the start of its turn. It can't use them while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act, or while surprised until it finishes its first turn.
Detect (1 action). Make a Wisdom (Perception) check.
Tail Attack (1 action). Make a Tail attack.
Wing Attack (2 actions). Each creature within 10 ft. makes a DC 21 Dexterity save. On a failure it takes 15 (2d6 + 8) bludgeoning damage and falls Prone. The dragon can then fly up to half its flying speed.

gm.title: Lair actions
lines:
While in its lair, the dragon can choose one option on initiative count 20, after other creatures on that count. It can't take a lair action while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. If surprised, it must first finish its first turn.
Fog. Create fog using the Fog Cloud spell's rules. It lasts until the next round's initiative count 20.
Freezing Wind. Each creature within 120 ft. of the dragon makes a DC 15 Constitution save. On a failure it takes 5 (1d10) cold damage. The wind disperses gases and vapors and snuffs exposed flames. Each protected flame, such as a lantern, has a 50 percent chance of going out.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:
Choose one or more of these effects around the lair.
Weather. Once per day the dragon can use the effects of Control Weather within 6 miles of its lair, even indoors.
Buoyant Winds. Within 1 mile of the lair, non-evil creatures that fall through no act of the dragon or its allies descend 60 ft. per round and take no falling damage.
Solid Fog. After days or longer of work, the dragon can make clouds and fog in the lair as solid as stone to form objects or structures.
When the dragon dies, weather changes revert as described in Control Weather. The other effects fade in 1d10 days.

gm.title: Variant spellcasting
lines: Under the optional dragon spellcasting rule, choose 5 spells of 5th level or lower. The dragon uses Charisma to cast each once per day without material components. Its spell save DC is 18 and its spell attack bonus is +10. The DM chooses the spells.

gm.title: Traits

gm.title: Description
lines: A solar dragon patrols its hunting ground on glowing, cloudlike wings. It hunts kindori and scavvers and may approach a distant ship after mistaking it for prey.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Flyby. Leaving an enemy’s reach by flying does not provoke an opportunity attack.
Legendary Resistance (2/day). The dragon can turn a failed save into a success.
Nebulous Thoughts. Magic that attempts to read the dragon’s mind or thoughts fails.
Siege Monster. Double damage against objects and structures.
Unusual Nature. The dragon needs no air.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and one Tail attack.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +12 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 14 (2d6 + 7) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) radiant damage.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +12 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (1d6 + 7) bludgeoning damage.
Photonic Breath (Recharge 5–6). Center a 30-ft.-radius sphere on a point the dragon sees up to 180 ft. away. Each creature in the sphere makes a DC 19 Constitution save, taking 55 (10d10) radiant damage on a failure or half as much on a success.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
The dragon has 3 legendary actions and refreshes them at the start of its turn. Use at most one option at the end of another creature’s turn.
Tail Attack (1 action). Make a Tail attack.
Burst of Light (2 actions). The dragon emits magical light. Each creature in a 20-ft.-radius sphere centered on the dragon makes a DC 19 Wisdom save. On a failure, it is blinded through the end of its next turn.

gm.title: Lair
lines: A solar dragon nests in the core of a star or within an immense hollow rock in its glare. An obsidian-shelled egg turns translucent just before it hatches.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:
Blinding Radiance. A creature inside the star or within 10 miles of it is blinded unless it wears eye protection such as Goggles of Night.
Stellar Incineration. A creature takes 132 (24d10) radiant damage when it enters the star or starts its turn inside it.

lines: A Huge dragon with challenge rating 18. Named abilities include Legendary Resistance (3/Day), Rend, Time Breath (Recharge 5–6).

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A long silver-blue dragon with curling horns traced by branching rainbow veins.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Saves Dex +8, Con +12, Wis +9, Cha +11. Skills Arcana +12, History +18, Perception +15, Stealth +14. Senses: blindsight 60 ft., darkvision 120 ft.. Languages: all. Passive Perception 25.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Legendary Resistance (3/day). Turn a failed save into a success.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three Rend attacks.
Rend. Melee weapon attack +13, reach 10 ft. Hit: 14 (2d6 + 7) slashing plus 7 (2d6) force.
Time Breath (Recharge 5–6). A 60-ft. cone turns nonmagical unattended objects and vegetation to dust. Each creature in range makes a DC 20 Constitution save. On failure it takes 36 (8d8) force damage and is weakened. Attacks against a weakened creature have Advantage, and it is Poisoned. A creature that passes the initial save only takes half damage. A weakened target may repeat the save at each turn end. Its third successful repeat ends the effect.

gm.title: Reactions
lines:
Up to three reactions each round, at most one each turn.
Reactive Rend. After using Legendary Resistance or being hit by an attack roll, make one Rend attack.
Slow Time. Just after a visible creature's turn ends, choose a visible creature within 60 ft. weakened by Time Breath. Its speed is fixed at 0 while it remains weakened.
Time Slip. Halve damage from an attack by a visible attacker, then optionally teleport with all gear to a visible unoccupied space within 30 ft.

gm.title: Lair Actions
lines:
Act on initiative 20, losing ties. Choose one lair action, with no repeat on consecutive rounds.
Temporal Fling. One visible creature within 60 ft. makes a DC 18 Wisdom save. On failure it takes 26 (4d12) psychic damage and disappears for one round, then returns to its space or the nearest available space.
Temporal Lag. Until initiative 20 next round, each creature within 60 ft. can move or take an action on its turn, but not both. It cannot take reactions or bonus actions during that time.
Timeline Divergence. Choose a space in the lair the dragon can fit inside. It exists in both locations until initiative 20 next round. It chooses which self moves or acts each time. An attack or effect covering both spaces affects the dragon once.

gm.title: Regional Effects
lines:
Within 3 miles, one or both effects can apply.
Time Dilations. The DM chooses whether a short rest takes 10 minutes or 2 hours.
Timelessness. Beasts, Humanoids, and Plants age one year per decade.
After the dragon dies, the effects fade over 1d10 days.

gm.title: Description
lines: This coastal gem dragon can drain strength with its breath. Close to its lair, rest may offer less recovery than visitors expect.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Amphibious. Breathe air and water.
Fabricate (1/day). Cast Fabricate without components using Intelligence.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). Turn a failed saving throw into a success.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 15 (2d10 + 4) piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) necrotic damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (1d8 + 4) slashing damage.
Desiccating Breath (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 60-ft. cone makes a DC 17 Constitution save. On a failure it takes 35 (10d6) necrotic damage and is weakened until the end of its next turn. While weakened, it has disadvantage on Strength checks and saves, and its Strength-based weapon attacks deal half damage. On a success it only takes half damage.

gm.title: Spellcasting (Psionics)
lines:
As an action, cast one of these spells using Intelligence (spell save DC 17). No components are required.
1/day each. Bane, Control Water, Create or Destroy Water.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines:
Change Shape. Become a Small or Medium creature by magic. Only size changes among the dragon’s statistics. The form ends at 0 HP or when the dragon spends another bonus action to end it.
Psychic Step. Teleport to a visible, unoccupied space within 60 ft.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
The dragon has 3 legendary actions. Use one option at the end of another creature’s turn, then subtract its cost. The dragon regains spent legendary actions at the start of its own turn.
Claw (1 action). Make one Claw attack.
Psionics (2 actions). Use Psychic Step or Spellcasting.
Essential Reduction (3 actions). Target a visible creature or an unattended object within 60 ft. It must pass a DC 17 Constitution save or take 28 (8d6) necrotic damage. A target reduced to 0 HP by the damage crumbles to dust.

gm.title: Lair actions
lines:
On initiative count 20, losing initiative ties, choose one option. The dragon cannot use the same lair action two rounds in a row.
Beguiling Whisper. Whisper to one creature within telepathy range. On a failed DC 15 Wisdom save, it is charmed until initiative count 20 next round and follows the dragon’s commands as well as it can, except commands that directly harm it.
Cancellation. End one active spell of 5th level or lower the dragon knows is active in the lair.
Negative Energy Infusion. Up to two visible creatures in the lair each make a DC 15 Constitution save, taking 14 (4d6) necrotic damage on a failure. Until initiative count 20 next round, no creature in the lair except the dragon can regain HP.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:
One or more of these effects can occur near the lair.
Crystal Profusion. Natural stone within 6 miles grows crystals and topaz veins, particularly underground.
Negative Energy. A creature finishing a long rest within 6 miles must pass a DC 15 Constitution save to reduce exhaustion or regain spent Hit Dice. Creatures resistant or immune to necrotic damage ignore this effect.
Thriving Wildlife. Giant squid gather and hunt in the sea within 6 miles.
Watery Sight. As an action the dragon can cast Clairvoyance without components on any body of water within 6 miles.
On death, the squid population returns to normal over 1d10 days. Existing crystals and topazes remain and new ones form at their ordinary rate.

lines: Fizban’s p. 34 permits optional languages, skill or tool proficiencies, and tailored traits. Use the stat block’s listed traits and actions as the default.

lines:
On initiative count 20, after other creatures on that count, choose one effect. An effect cannot be chosen in consecutive rounds. Skip this action while the dragon is Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. If surprised, wait until the dragon finishes its first turn.
Freezing fog. Choose a visible point within 120 ft. Fog spreads around corners in a 20-ft.-radius sphere and makes the area heavily obscured. Each creature in the fog when it appears makes a DC 10 Constitution save for 10 (3d6) cold damage, halved on success. A creature that ends its turn there takes 10 (3d6) cold damage. A wind of at least 20 mph disperses the fog. It otherwise lasts until the dragon uses this effect again or dies.
Falling ice. Pick up to three creatures the dragon can see beneath the ceiling within 120 ft. Roll a separate ranged attack at +7 against each. A hit deals 10 (3d6) piercing damage.
Ice wall. Choose a visible solid surface within 120 ft. An opaque ice wall appears, up to 30 ft. long, 30 ft. high, and 1 ft. thick. When it appears, each creature in its space is pushed 5 ft. out of it on the side the dragon chooses. Each 10-ft. section has AC 5, 30 HP, fire vulnerability, and immunity to acid, cold, necrotic, poison, and psychic damage. The wall disappears if the dragon uses the effect again or dies.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:
Choose one or more of these effects around the lair.
Cold fog makes the land within 6 miles lightly obscured. Freezing precipitation falls within the same radius and can turn into a blizzard while the dragon rests.
Ice walls partition the lair. They are 6 inches thick, and each 10-ft. section has AC 5, 15 HP, fire vulnerability, and immunity to acid, cold, necrotic, poison, and psychic damage. The dragon can pass through a wall at full speed, destroying the part it crosses.
After the dragon dies, the fog and precipitation fade within 1 day, and the walls melt over 1d10 days.

gm.title: Variant: innate spellcasting
lines: If using the optional dragon spellcasting rules, choose 1 spell of level 4 or lower. The dragon can cast each once per day without material components using Charisma. Spell save DC 14. Spell attack bonus +6.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Monster Manual (2014), p. 101 for the stat block and p. 86 for optional spellcasting. Lair and regional rules appear on pp. 102–103. The official errata clarifies the legendary and lair action restrictions.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The printed Ice Wall rule is ambiguous about who chooses the side. This profile gives the choice to the dragon.

Legendary Resistance (3/day, or 4/day in its lair). When the dragon fails a save, it can spend a use to succeed instead.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three Rend attacks.
Rend. Melee attack, +11 to hit, reach 10 ft. Hit 13 (2d6 + 6) Slashing damage plus 4 (1d8) Cold damage.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
The dragon has 3 legendary action uses, or 4 in its lair. Immediately after another creature's turn, it can spend one use to take one option below. It regains spent uses at the start of its turn.
Freezing Burst. Center a 30-ft.-radius sphere on a visible point within 120 ft. Each creature in the sphere makes a DC 14 Constitution save. On a failure, it takes 7 (2d6) Cold damage and its Speed is 0 until the end of its next turn. The dragon can use this option again starting on its next turn.
Frightful Presence. The dragon casts Fear without Material components, using Charisma with spell save DC 14. The dragon can use this option again starting on its next turn.
Pounce. The dragon can move up to half its Speed and makes one Rend attack.

gm.title: Lair resources
lines: In the lair, this encounter is worth 11,500 XP. The dragon has 4 daily Legendary Resistance uses and 4 legendary action uses.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:
Frigid Cold. Extreme cold extends 1 mile from the lair, and all water there is frigid water. Use the 2024 Dungeon Master's Guide rules for those hazards.
Glacial Gloom. Cold fog leaves the region within 1 mile Lightly Obscured. Any creature other than the dragon or an ally that finishes a Long Rest in the area makes a DC 15 Constitution save. On a failure, its Speed drops by 10 ft. for 1 hour.
Both effects end immediately if the dragon dies or moves its lair elsewhere.

lines: Dagger. Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage. Archmages are powerful (and usually quite old) spellcasters dedicated to the study of the arcane arts. Benevolent ones counsel kings and queens, while evil ones rule as tyrants and pursue lichdom. An archmage typically has one or more apprentice mages, and an archmage’s abode has numerous magical wards and guardians to discourage interlopers.

gm.title: Description
lines: A boastful harengon brigand with an enchanted blue scarf. Zybilna pinned him to a tree by it. Bavlorna freed him in exchange for the best item taken from each victim.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Evasion. When a Dexterity save would halve damage, Agdon instead takes none on a success or half on a failure. This trait has no effect while he is incapacitated.
Standing Leap. Agdon can long jump up to 20 ft. or high jump up to 10 ft. without needing a running start.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two attacks, choosing Branding Iron or Dagger for each.
Branding Iron. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 10 (3d6) fire damage and magically brand the target. Agdon is invisible to creatures bearing his brand. The mark lasts 24 hours unless removed sooner by a spell that ends a curse. The iron cools when he lets go of it and works only for him.
Dagger. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d4 + 5) piercing damage.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines: Quick Fingers. Target a creature Agdon can see within 5 ft. Roll Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) against DC 1 + its passive Perception. On a success, he steals one object of 1 lb. or less that it carries but does not have in hand. It does not notice the theft.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Uncanny Dodge. When an attack hits Agdon, halve its damage if he can see the attacker.

gm.title: Encounter context
lines: Agdon and his Harengon Brigands ambush travelers at the Brigands’ Tollway, with Harengon Snipers in support. A creature can use an action and succeed on a DC 17 Strength (Athletics) check to catch Agdon’s scarf. While it holds the scarf, his speed is 35 ft. and he cannot move more than 15 ft. from it. He can try once to pull free as an action, resolved by a contested Strength (Athletics) check. If he loses, he surrenders on the spot. The scarf cannot be removed, even if Agdon dies.

lines: Damage resistances: acid, fire, lightning, thunder, and bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks. Damage immunities: cold, necrotic, poison. Condition immunities: charmed, exhaustion, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained. Darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 11. Languages: those it knew in life.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Ethereal Sight. Agony can see 60 ft. between the Material Plane and the Ethereal Plane in either direction.
Incorporeal Movement. Agony treats creatures and objects as Difficult Terrain when passing through them. It takes 5 (1d10) force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.
Bound to the Last Breath. If Agony drops to 0 HP while the ship has at least 1 HP, it returns at full HP in the cargo hold 24 hours later. If it moves more than 100 ft. from the ship, Agony vanishes and immediately reappears in the cargo hold.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Withering Touch. Melee weapon attack +5, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 17 (4d6 + 3) necrotic damage.
Etherealness. Agony crosses between the Material Plane and the Ethereal Plane. Agony remains visible across the boundary while in the Border Ethereal, but effects cannot cross the boundary.
Horrifying Visage. Each non-Undead creature within 60 ft. that can see Agony must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom save or become Frightened for 1 minute. Failing by 5 or more also ages it by 1d4 × 10 years. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the fear on a success. A success or the end of the effect grants 24 hours of immunity to Agony's visage. Greater Restoration reverses the aging if cast within 24 hours of the effect.
Possession (Recharge 6). One visible humanoid within 5 ft. must succeed on a DC 13 Charisma save or Agony disappears into its body. The host is Incapacitated and aware while Agony controls it. Agony can be targeted only by effects that turn undead. Agony retains its alignment, Intelligence, Wisdom, Charisma, and immunity to being Charmed and Frightened. It otherwise uses the host's statistics and gains none of the host's knowledge, class features, or proficiencies.
Possession ends if the host drops to 0 HP, Agony releases it as a bonus action, Agony is turned, or a spell such as Dispel Evil and Good forces it out. Agony reappears in an unoccupied space within 5 ft. of the host. A successful save or the end of possession grants that creature 24 hours of immunity to Agony's Possession.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: Return to Ship. While away from the Last Breath, Agony can magically teleport to the lower cargo hold or another location it can see aboard the ship.

gm.title: Encounters
lines:
Mutiny. Agony possesses the hadozee Flinch on the Second Wind and publicly rebukes Captain Gargenhale before returning to the Last Breath. Flinch remembers none of the incident.
Lower Cargo Hold. If Agony hears someone approach or open the brig door, it tries to possess a character and smash a keg of alchemist’s fire. If the blaze burns for 1 minute, the remaining kegs ignite, destroying the Last Breath and dealing 110 (20d10) fire damage to everything within 100 ft.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

gm.title: Fury shared rules
lines:
Printed source. Furies, pp. 79–80. The sisters appear together and speak all humanoid languages. They try three times to divert a target from atonement before trying to kill them in public.
Defenses. Damage reduction 15/good. Immune to paralysis, polymorph, and mind-affecting effects.
Scourge. The +3 scourge works like a whip that deals 1d4 lethal damage before modifiers. A Fury may substitute it for her claw attacks. Use the attack and ability damage listed for that sister. Rake (Ex) is +9 melee for 1d4 + 1 damage.
Alter Self (Sp). At will as a standard action, a Fury can take the form of an elderly human woman indefinitely. Caster level 10.
Breath Weapon (Su, 3/day). Fill one adjacent square with foul air. Apply stinking cloud as cast by an 8th-level sorcerer, with a DC 16 Fortitude save.
Find Penitent (Su). Furies can locate a target who seeks redemption at the invitation or embrace stage of corruption. The target cannot hide from them, even with magic.
Gaseous Death (Su). At 0 HP, a Fury and her scourge dissolve into smoke. Surviving sisters continue to fight, though the last survivor tries to flee. If a sister survives, the slain Furies return at full HP after 24 hours. To kill them permanently, all three must die within the same 24 hours and an Innocent must deal the killing blows. Their scourges remain after permanent death.
Weaknesses. A good cleric or a paladin can turn each Fury separately by invoking her true name. A turning attempt cannot destroy, rebuke, or command her. A Fury cannot deliberately harm a good creature except with her breath weapon.

gm.title: Periapt of mind trapping
lines: The periapt is a fist-sized container made of silver, emerald, and amethyst. At least three mind flayer arcanists create the periapt and sacrifice an equal number of living victims in a three-day ritual. Each alhoon remains undead for the lifespan remaining to its victim, and the rite can be repeated with new victims. When an alhoon is destroyed, its mind enters the periapt alongside the sacrificed souls. Destroying the periapt destroys the minds and souls trapped inside. Its holder has advantage on attacks, saves, and checks against the associated alhoons, and those alhoons have disadvantage on attacks, saves, and checks against the holder. The holder can speak telepathically with the trapped victims or silence them. Alhoons inside can speak telepathically to the holder without permission.

Abyssal Rift. If the alkilith continuously surrounds a door, window, or similar opening for 6d6 days, the opening becomes a permanent portal to a random layer of the Abyss.
Amorphous. The alkilith passes through openings as narrow as 1 inch without squeezing.
False Appearance. The alkilith has advantage on initiative if motionless at the start of combat. A creature that hasn't seen it move or act needs a successful DC 18 Intelligence (Investigation) check to recognize it as something other than slime or fungus.
Foment Confusion. A creature other than a demon that starts its turn within 30 ft. makes a DC 18 Wisdom save. On a failure, it hears a brief buzz and has disadvantage on its next attack roll, save, or ability check. If it fails by 5 or more, it instead falls under Confusion for 1 minute without requiring the alkilith's concentration. While under that spell, it is immune to Foment Confusion.
Magic Resistance. The alkilith has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
Spider Climb. The alkilith climbs difficult surfaces, including ceilings, without an ability check.
Unusual Nature. The alkilith needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Constitution saves +6. Immune to Charmed, Frightened and Prone. Darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 10. Can speak every language but understands none.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Immutable Form. Powers, spells and other effects cannot change its form.
Lake Rebirth. After being destroyed, it returns at full HP in the Lake of Rot after 24 hours.
Primordial Influence. If a Dazed enemy starts its turn within 20 ft., it attempts a DC 16 Wisdom save. Failure causes a strange physical alteration chosen by the GM without changing its statistics. Cure Ailment of 4th order or higher, Greater Restoration or comparable magic reverses it. The altered creature repeats the save at every long rest. Failure worsens or adds an alteration. Three failures after the first alteration turn the creature into a GM-controlled amalgam. Only Wish restores its original form.
Viscous Vicinity. The space within 20 ft. is difficult terrain for other creatures.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Use Reality Rend twice, with the option to substitute Pull for one attack.
Reality Rend. Melee power attack +7, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit for 15 (2d10 + 4) psychic damage, then the target makes a DC 16 Wisdom save or becomes Dazed until the start of the amalgam’s next turn.
Pull. Select up to three visible creatures within 60 ft. Each makes a DC 16 Strength save. Failure pulls it directly toward the amalgam by up to 30 ft.

gm.title: Psionics
lines:
Power attacks are psionic and deal nonmagical damage. Counterspell, Dispel Magic and Antimagic Field do not stop them. If an enemy provokes an opportunity attack, the amalgam can use Reality Rend as its reaction instead.
MCDM Dazed. On its turn the affected creature chooses only one of movement, an action or a bonus action. Becoming dazed during its turn ends that turn. Additional actions granted by effects such as Haste are still available. Lesser Restoration, Greater Restoration or Cure Ailment can remove Dazed.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Use Contaminating Presence and make three Tentacle attacks. Any of those attacks can be replaced with Fling.
Bite. Melee weapon attack +17, reach 5 ft., one target, 23 (3d8 + 10) piercing. A Large or smaller target already Grappled by the amalgamation is Swallowed, ending that grapple. Inside, it is Blinded and Restrained, has total cover from outside, takes 42 (12d6) acid damage, and gains one level of Contamination at the start of the amalgamation's turns. If the amalgamation takes 50 or more damage in a single turn from a creature inside it, it makes a DC 25 Constitution save at the end of that turn. On a failure all swallowed creatures fall Prone within 10 ft. If it dies, they cease to be Restrained and can spend 15 ft. of movement to exit Prone.
Tentacle. Melee weapon attack +17, reach 50 ft., one target, 20 (3d6 + 10) bludgeoning. Grapple the target (escape DC 18). It is Restrained while grappled. Each of twelve tentacles can hold one target.
Fling. Throw one Large or smaller held object or grappled creature up to 60 ft. A thrown creature lands Prone. Against a solid surface, it takes 3 (1d6) bludgeoning per 10 ft. thrown. A creature the target is thrown at must pass a DC 18 Dexterity save or take the same damage and fall Prone.
Mind-breaking Whispers. One creature within 120 ft. must pass a DC 20 Intelligence save or take 35 (10d6) psychic damage and become insane until it finishes a long rest. It cannot take actions, understand speech, or read, and can only speak gibberish. Greater Restoration ends the effect.
Contaminating Presence. Each humanoid within 120 ft. must pass a DC 20 Constitution save or take 10 (3d6) necrotic damage and gain one level of Contamination.

gm.title: Legendary Actions
lines:
Three legendary actions per round. Use one option after another creature's turn and recover spent actions at the start of this creature's turn.
Tentacle Attack or Fling. Use either option.
Mind-breaking Whispers (2 actions). Use Mind-breaking Whispers.
Piper at the Gate (3 actions). Summon up to five gibbering mouthers into empty spaces within 30 ft. They obey the amalgamation, act immediately after it on the same initiative count, and remain until destroyed. It can have at most ten mouthers summoned by this action.

gm.title: Delerium contamination
lines:
Printed source. Appendix C, pp. 222–223.
Add contamination levels from each exposure. A contaminated character rolls 1d20 at the end of each long rest and gains one level on a 1.
Symptoms are cumulative. Level 1 has no symptom. Level 2 halves healing from Hit Dice. Level 3 prevents HP recovery from a long rest. Level 4 halves damage the creature deals with weapon attacks and spells. Level 5 makes it Incapacitated. Level 6 triggers Monstrous Transformation.
After a character gains a level, roll 1d6. On a result at or below the current level, the GM chooses a new mutation or rolls on the printed mutations table. Replace or reroll duplicate mutations.
Contamination does not wear off. Purge Contamination can remove levels and causes Exhaustion. Heal removes all contamination and mutations. Each level removed also removes one random mutation. At level 0, all symptoms and mutations end.
A contaminated humanoid rises as a Haze Husk 24 hours after death. It rises as a Haze Wight if it had at least six class levels or Hit Dice. Raising a creature from the dead reduces its contamination by one level.
Monstrous Transformation. At level 6 or higher, the creature transforms after one round. Replace its statistics, hit points, and Hit Dice with those of a monster the GM chooses. Contamination resets to 0, and the GM controls the transformed creature.
Wish or similar magic can restore one transformed creature, clearing its madness and contamination. Using Wish this way gives the caster a 33 percent chance of losing the ability to cast it again.

gm.title: Optional dragon customization
lines:
Adjust languages, skills or tool proficiencies to suit the individual dragon. Double selected skill proficiency bonuses where appropriate.
Spellcasting. The Monster Manual's optional innate casting rule grants a number of spells equal to the dragon's Charisma modifier (minimum one). Each is usable once per day without material components. A spell's level cannot exceed one-third of the dragon's challenge rating rounded down. Use Charisma for spell save DC and spell attack rolls. Consider increasing CR for stronger spells that deal damage or impose conditions.
Other traits. Consider giving a younger dragon the Change Shape action, granting Flyby or Mimicry, or binding the dragon's essence to an object so it can return after destruction. You can upgrade blindsight to truesight or grant a burrower tremorsense or Tunneler. One example of damage absorption lets a fire-immune dragon recover HP from fire.

gm.title: Description
lines: Translucent purple crystals hover behind its head. The dragon studies gravity, planes and distant worlds and often makes a lair in flooded caverns.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Amphibious. The dragon breathes air and water.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). The dragon can turn a failed save into a success.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +15 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 19 (2d10 + 8) piercing damage plus 13 (3d8) force damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +15 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 15 (2d6 + 8) slashing damage.
Singularity Breath (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 90-ft. cone makes a DC 23 Strength save. Failure deals 63 (14d8) force damage and sets the creature's speed to 0 until the start of the dragon's next turn. Success halves the damage and preserves movement.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines:
Change Shape. Magically assume any Small or Medium creature's form while keeping all statistics except size. Return to dragon form at 0 HP or by taking a bonus action.
Psychic Step. Magically teleport to a visible unoccupied space within 60 ft.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
The dragon has 3 legendary actions and regains spent actions at the start of its turn. It can use one option at a time at the end of another creature's turn.
Claw (1 action). Make one Claw attack.
Psionics (2 actions). Use Psychic Step or Spellcasting.
Explosive Crystal (3 actions). The dragon detonates an amethyst at a visible point within 60 ft. Each creature in a 20-ft.-radius sphere centered there makes a DC 23 Dexterity save. Failure deals 18 (4d8) force damage and knocks the creature prone.

gm.title: Lair actions
lines:
The dragon is CR 24 (62,000 XP) in its lair.
On initiative count 20, losing ties, choose one option. The same option cannot be used in consecutive rounds.
Beguiling Whisper. One creature within the dragon's telepathy range makes a DC 15 Wisdom save. Failure charms it until initiative count 20 of the next round. It obeys the dragon to the best of its ability, except for directly harmful commands.
Imprisoning Force. Cast Forcecage at the dragon's spell save DC without components. The spell ends early when the dragon uses this action again or dies.
Spatial Projection. Until initiative count 20 next round, the dragon simultaneously occupies its space and one chosen space in the lair large enough to fit it. Choose which body moves or acts each time it moves or acts. An attack or effect that can reach both spaces affects it only once.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:
Use one or more of these effects around the lair.
Background Check. Once per day the dragon can cast Legend Lore without components to learn about a person, place or object within 1 mile.
Crystal Profusion. Amethysts and geodes form in mud on shores and lakebeds within 6 miles.
Thriving Wildlife. Fish and other aquatic Beasts thrive and reproduce quickly within 6 miles. Foraging in these waters yields double the usual food.
Watery Sight. As an action, the dragon can cast Clairvoyance without components targeting any body of water within 6 miles.
At its death, aquatic populations return to normal over 1d10 days. Existing crystals remain and new ones form at the normal rate.

gm.title: Optional dragon customization
lines:
Adjust languages, skills or tool proficiencies to suit the individual dragon. Double selected skill proficiency bonuses where appropriate.
Spellcasting. The Monster Manual's optional innate casting rule grants a number of spells equal to the dragon's Charisma modifier (minimum one). Each is usable once per day without material components. A spell's level cannot exceed one-third of the dragon's challenge rating rounded down. Use Charisma for spell save DC and spell attack rolls. Consider increasing CR for stronger spells that deal damage or impose conditions.
Other traits. Consider giving a younger dragon the Change Shape action, granting Flyby or Mimicry, or binding the dragon's essence to an object so it can return after destruction. You can upgrade blindsight to truesight or grant a burrower tremorsense or Tunneler. One example of damage absorption lets a fire-immune dragon recover HP from fire.

gm.title: Spellcasting (Psionics)
lines:
As an action, the dragon casts one listed spell using Intelligence (save DC 23, +15 to hit with spell attacks) without components.
1/day each. Blink, Control Water, Dispel Magic, Freedom of Movement, Globe of Invulnerability, Plane Shift, Protection from Evil and Good, Sending.

Adjust languages, skills or tool proficiencies to suit the individual dragon. Double selected skill proficiency bonuses where appropriate.
Spellcasting. The Monster Manual's optional innate casting rule grants a number of spells equal to the dragon's Charisma modifier (minimum one). Each is usable once per day without material components. A spell's level cannot exceed one-third of the dragon's challenge rating rounded down. Use Charisma for spell save DC and spell attack rolls. Consider increasing CR for stronger spells that deal damage or impose conditions.
Other traits. Consider giving a younger dragon the Change Shape action, granting Flyby or Mimicry, or binding the dragon's essence to an object so it can return after destruction. You can upgrade blindsight to truesight or grant a burrower tremorsense or Tunneler. One example of damage absorption lets a fire-immune dragon recover HP from fire.

lines: An Underdark dragon that gathers knowledge and uses spores to sow terror, turn foes against one another, or poison prey.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Legendary Resistance (3/day). The dragon can turn a failed save into a success.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +12 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 17 (2d10 + 6) piercing damage plus 11 (2d10) poison damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +12 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 13 (2d6 + 6) slashing damage.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +12 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 10 (1d8 + 6) bludgeoning damage. A creature hit makes a DC 20 Strength save or falls prone.
Change Shape. Magically assume any Small or Medium creature's form while keeping all statistics except size. Return to dragon form at 0 HP or by taking an action.
Nightmare Breath (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 90-ft. cone makes a DC 19 Wisdom save. Failure deals 49 (9d10) psychic damage and frightens the creature of the dragon for 1 minute. gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
The dragon has 3 legendary actions and regains spent actions at the start of its turn. It can use one option at a time at the end of another creature's turn.
Commanding Spores (1 action). A visible creature within 30 ft. makes a DC 19 Wisdom save. On a failure, it must spend its reaction on one melee weapon attack against a random creature in reach. If it cannot take a reaction or has no creature in reach, it takes 11 (2d10) psychic damage instead.
Tail (1 action). Make one Tail attack.
Spore Salvo (2 actions). A visible creature within 30 ft. makes a DC 19 Constitution save. Failure deals 28 (8d6) poison damage and poisons the target for 1 minute. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the condition on a success.

gm.title: Lair actions
lines:
The dragon is CR 19 (22,000 XP) in its lair.
On initiative count 20, losing ties, choose one option. The same option cannot be used in consecutive rounds.
Deep Torpor. Cast Slow without components, using Charisma (save DC 16). The spell ends early when the dragon uses this action again or dies.
Mossy Sludge. Moss makes the lair's floor, walls and ceiling difficult terrain until initiative count 20 next round.
Toxic Spores. Choose a visible 20-ft. cube within 120 ft. Each creature there makes a DC 15 Constitution save. Failure deals 14 (4d6) poison damage and poisons the creature until the end of its next turn.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:

Preservation of Knowledge. Within 6 miles, physical writings become impervious to nonmagical damage.
Restless Sleep. A creature finishing a long rest within 6 miles must succeed on a DC 10 Constitution save to reduce exhaustion. Creatures immune to the poisoned condition are exempt from this effect.
Verdant Growth. Plants and fungi expand and grow rapidly within 6 miles. Foraging yields double the usual food.
At the dragon's death, these effects fade over 1d10 days.

gm.title: Description
lines: A mountainous ocean dragon with a heavy shell and a bite crackling with lightning. Its mythic awakening brings a second surge of vitality.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Amphibious. The dragon breathes air and water.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). The dragon can turn a failed save into a success.
Blessing of the Sea (recharges after a short or long rest). When the turtle would fall to 0 HP, set it to 350 HP instead and recharge Steam Breath. It can use its mythic options for the next hour. Defeating it after this happens awards 62,000 extra XP (124,000 total).
Unusual Nature. The dragon turtle requires no food or drink.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite or Tail attack and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +16 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 15 (1d12 + 9) piercing damage plus 13 (2d12) lightning damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +16 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 18 (2d8 + 9) slashing damage.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +16 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 20 (2d10 + 9) bludgeoning damage. A creature hit makes a DC 24 Strength save or falls prone.
Steam Breath (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 90-ft. cone makes a DC 24 Constitution save. Failure deals 67 (15d8) fire damage, and success halves the damage. Water does not confer resistance to this fire damage.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
The dragon has 3 legendary actions and regains spent actions at the start of its turn. It can use one option at a time at the end of another creature's turn.
Attack (1 action). Make one Claw or Tail attack.
Move (1 action). Move up to speed. Swimming this way does not provoke opportunity attacks.
Boiling Aura (3 actions). Until the start of the turtle's next turn, any creature starting its turn within 20 ft. must succeed on a DC 24 Constitution save or take 40 (9d8) fire damage. Water does not confer resistance to this fire damage.

gm.title: Mythic actions
lines:
For the hour after Blessing of the Sea activates, these options are available as legendary actions.
Bite (1 action). Make one Bite attack.
Armor of Storms (2 actions). Gain 40 temporary HP until the start of the turtle's next turn. While any of these temporary HP remain, a creature that touches the turtle or hits it with a melee attack takes 26 (4d12) lightning damage.

gm.title: Lair actions
lines:
The DM may grant these lair actions to an ancient dragon turtle, raising it to CR 25 (75,000 XP) in its lair.
On initiative count 20, losing ties, choose one option. The same option cannot be used in consecutive rounds.
Blasting Current. Each creature within 30 ft. makes a DC 15 Strength save. The turtle moves each creature 30 ft. in a direction it chooses on a failure, or 10 ft. on a success.
Entangling Kelp. Choose a visible point in the lair. Each creature in a 20-ft.-radius sphere centered there makes a DC 15 Strength save. Failure restrains it until the end of its next turn.
Steam Eruption. Choose a visible point on the ground within 120 ft. Each creature in a 15-ft. cone from that point makes a DC 15 Constitution save. Failure deals 21 (6d6) fire damage, and success halves the damage. Water does not confer resistance to this fire damage.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:
Use one or more of these effects around the lair.
Diverting Currents. Currents steer unwanted visitors away. Each foot swum in them costs 1 extra foot, or 2 extra feet in difficult terrain, even with a swim speed.
Elemental Portals. Seafloor crevasses within 1 mile open two-way portals to the Elemental Plane of Water.
Hot Water. Vents heat the water within 6 miles to 100°F.
At the turtle's death, these effects fade over 1d10 days.

Consider increasing CR for stronger spells that deal damage or impose conditions.
Other traits. Consider giving a younger dragon the Change Shape action, granting Flyby or Mimicry, or binding the dragon's essence to an object so it can return after destruction. You can upgrade blindsight to truesight or grant a burrower tremorsense or Tunneler. One example of damage absorption lets a fire-immune dragon recover HP from fire.

lines: The p. 110 example uses Charisma (save DC 17, +9 to hit with spell attacks). Choose up to two suggested spells: Control Water, Control Weather, or Fog Cloud. The turtle casts each selected spell once per day without material components. Control Weather has a casting time longer than one action.

lines:

Claw (1 action). Make one Claw attack.
Psionics (2 actions). Use Psychic Step or Spellcasting.

gm.title: Lair actions
lines:

Distort Perceptions. Choose one visible creature in the lair. It must succeed on a DC 15 Intelligence save or take 22 (4d10) psychic damage and have disadvantage on saves until its next turn starts.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:
The dragon’s magic causes one or more of these effects around its lair.
Crystal Profusion. Natural stone within 6 miles develops crystals and emerald veins.

Subtle Obstruction. Within 6 miles, rock can shift by itself to block routes, topple markers, or send unwary travelers tumbling.
Thriving Wildlife. Giant Lizards gather within 6 miles.
When the dragon dies, the rock stops moving immediately and the lizard population returns to normal over 1d10 days. Existing crystals and emeralds remain, and new ones form at their usual rate.

lines:

The creature can use its action to make a Charisma check contested by the dragon's, escaping if it wins. The banishment also ends on the next round's initiative count 20. The creature returns to the space it left or the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:

Warning Mist. Within 6 miles of the lair, opalescent mist doesn't obscure vision. If evil creatures approach the dragon or non-evil creatures in the mist, the mist takes eerie shapes as a warning.
Glowing Valuables. Gems and pearls within 1 mile of the lair cast dim light to 5 ft.
All these effects end immediately when the dragon dies.

lines: Speed · 40 ft., fly 80 ft., swim 40 ft.

gm.title: Description
lines: A forest dragon that uses poison, threats, and deception to gain power over its neighbors.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Amphibious. The dragon breathes air and water.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). After failing a save, the dragon can choose to succeed.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. The dragon may use Frightful Presence, then makes one bite attack and two claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack against one target within 15 ft., +15 to hit. Hit for 19 (2d10 + 8) piercing damage plus 10 (3d6) poison damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack against one target within 10 ft., +15 to hit. Hit for 22 (4d6 + 8) slashing damage.
Tail. Melee weapon attack against one target within 20 ft., +15 to hit. Hit for 17 (2d8 + 8) bludgeoning damage.
Frightful Presence. Each creature of the dragon's choice within 120 ft. that is aware of it makes a DC 19 Wisdom save. On failure it is Frightened for 1 minute and can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns to end the effect. A successful save or the end of the effect gives that creature 24 hours of immunity to this dragon's Frightful Presence.
Poison Breath (recharge 5–6). All creatures in a 90-ft. cone make a DC 22 Constitution save. Failure deals 77 (22d6) poison damage. Success halves the damage.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
The dragon has three legendary actions. Spend them on one option at a time at the end of another creature's turn. Spent actions return at the start of the dragon's turn. The dragon can choose to pass. It cannot use these actions while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. If surprised, it must wait until it finishes its first turn. A creature that assumes the dragon's form gains none of its legendary actions, lair actions, or regional effects.
Detect (1 action). Make a Wisdom (Perception) check.
Tail Attack (1 action). Make one tail attack.
Wing Attack (2 actions). Each creature within 15 ft. makes a DC 23 Dexterity save. Failure deals 15 (2d6 + 8) bludgeoning damage and knocks the creature Prone. The dragon may then fly up to half its flying speed (40 ft.).

gm.title: Lair actions
lines:
On initiative count 20, after other creatures on that count, choose one effect. An effect cannot be chosen in consecutive rounds. Skip this action while the dragon is Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. If surprised, wait until the dragon finishes its first turn.
Roots and vines. Choose a visible point on the ground within 120 ft. The ground within 20 ft. becomes difficult terrain. Each creature there must pass a DC 15 Strength save or become Restrained. The creature or another creature can use an action to free it with a DC 15 Strength check. The growth wilts if the dragon chooses this effect again or dies.
Thorn wall. Choose a solid surface within 120 ft. A brush wall up to 60 ft. long, 10 ft. high, and 5 ft. thick blocks sight. When it appears, each creature in its space makes a DC 15 Dexterity save. On failure it takes 18 (4d8) piercing damage and is pushed 5 ft. out of the wall on the side it chooses. Crossing the wall costs 4 ft. of movement per foot traveled. Once per round while in contact with the wall in its space, a creature makes a DC 15 Dexterity save for 18 (4d8) piercing damage, halved on success. Each 10-ft. section has AC 5, 15 HP, fire vulnerability, bludgeoning and piercing resistance, and psychic immunity. The wall sinks into the ground if the dragon chooses this effect again or dies.
Beguiling fog. Choose one visible creature within 120 ft. It makes a DC 15 Wisdom save or is Charmed by the dragon until initiative count 20 of the next round.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:
Choose one or more of these effects around the lair.
Thickets within 1 mile form a maze of walls 10 ft. high and 10 ft. thick that block sight. Moving through them costs 4 ft. per foot traveled. Each round a creature is in contact with them, it must pass a DC 15 Dexterity save or take 3 (1d6) piercing damage. Each 10-ft. cube has AC 5, 30 HP, bludgeoning and piercing resistance, fire vulnerability, and psychic and thunder immunity.
Within 1 mile, only magic can track the dragon unless it chooses to leave signs. Plants part for it in this area. It ignores obstacles and damage from ordinary plants, including the thickets.
Birds and rodents within 1 mile relay sights and sounds to the dragon. Large game is conspicuously absent.
On the dragon's death, the animals lose their link immediately. Within 1d10 days, the thickets lose their thorns and become ordinary plants and difficult terrain.

gm.title: Variant: innate spellcasting
lines: If using the optional dragon spellcasting rules, choose 4 spells of level 7 or lower. The dragon can cast each once per day without material components using Charisma. Spell save DC 19. Spell attack bonus +11.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Monster Manual (2014), p. 93 for the stat block and p. 86 for optional spellcasting. Lair and regional rules appear on pp. 95–96. The official errata clarifies the legendary and lair action restrictions. The official errata corrects XP to 41,000.

lines:

lines:
