gm.title: Description
lines: A foot-tall lizard kin ambusher. Caymas use hidden village entrances and prefer a quick strike followed by retreat.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Temperate to subtropical swamps or forests. Uncommon. Village of 10d6 adults and half as many noncombatants. Active at any time. Omnivore. Intelligence 8–10. Treasure K. Neutral. No magic resistance. Height about 1 foot. Morale 8–10.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack once for 1d3 damage or use a weapon. Bone daggers deal 1d2. A bok deals 1d6. Caymas use it two-handed as a pike and cannot throw it.
Ambush. A concealed cayma imposes a −2 penalty on the target’s surprise roll.

gm.title: Senses and skills
lines: Infravision 90 feet. Hide in Shadows and Move Silently each succeed 40% of the time. Speaks a Shazak dialect. Knowing one lizard kin dialect gives basic comprehension of the other two. A few individuals speak Common.

gm.title: Village shaman
lines: Each village has a shaman equivalent to a 5th- to 7th-level priest. The shaman has AC 6 and raises a party’s morale by one level. XP by Hit Dice, with Legacy value second. 5 HD 420 or 650 XP. 6 HD 650 or 975 XP. 7 HD 975 or 1,400 XP.

gm.title: Red Curse
lines: A cayma entering the cursed lands can acquire a Legacy and needs cinnabryl to prevent Affliction. A standard cayma with a Legacy is worth 120 XP.

gm.title: Cayma grenades
lines:
A Wokan can supply ceramic grenades. On impact against a hard surface, roll 1d20. The grenade breaks and releases its cloud on 1–17.
Sleep. Within 1 foot of the impact, anyone whose head or breathing organ is in the cloud must save vs. breath weapon or sleep for 1d4 turns.
Choke. Same area and save as sleep. Failure leaves the victim unable to attack or defend for 1d6 rounds.
Fog. A 5-foot radius blocks ordinary vision and infravision for 1d6 rounds. Strong wind halves the duration.
Weapon details. Savage Coast Campaign Book, Part 2, pp. 136–137.

gm.title: Description
lines: The camel-headed Abomination looks after the others at camp. In a fight, Ceemal heals allies and draws them back out of danger.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Saves Con +4, Int +5, Wis +6. Skills Medicine +6, Nature +5, Perception +6, Stealth +8, Survival +6. Darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 16. Common.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Octopodan Camouflage. Ceemal can try to Hide while lightly obscured by natural conditions such as foliage, mist, heavy rain, or snow.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Fillet Knife attacks or two Acid Spit attacks.
Fillet Knife. Melee weapon attack +6, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 7 (1d6 + 4) slashing damage. If the target is a creature, another Abomination within 5 ft. of it heals for half the damage dealt.
Acid Spit. Ranged weapon attack +6, range 20/40 ft., one target. Hit 8 (1d8 + 4) acid damage. The target is Poisoned until the start of Ceemal’s next turn.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: To Me, Sweetie (3/day). Choose an ally within 30 ft. who can hear Ceemal. The ally can spend its reaction to move up to its speed toward Ceemal without provoking opportunity attacks.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Wail of Loss. When an enemy within 60 ft. reduces another Abomination Ceemal can see to 0 HP, the enemy makes a DC 14 Constitution save. It takes 7 (2d6) psychic damage on a failure or half on a success.

gm.title: Villain Party Action
lines:
Abominations. Once per encounter for each party action, after an enemy finishes its turn. The party can use the actions in any order, one per round. The creature performing the action must be present and must not be Incapacitated.
Action 3, All You Can Meat. Ceemal throws a piece of meat to every Abomination they can see within 30 ft. Each target that is not Incapacitated can eat the meat without spending an action and regain 8 (1d10 + 3) HP.

gm.title: Description
lines: Owl-eyed celestial bounty hunters judge whether the punishment a petitioner seeks fits the injury. A celebrun that takes a contract pursues its quarry with immortal patience.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Studded leather. Perception 16, Stealth 17. Resistant to radiant damage and bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks. Immune to Blinded. Darkvision 60 ft. Languages Celestial and Common. Telepathy 60 ft.

gm.title: Ability modifiers
lines: Str +3, Dex +7, Con +2, Int +1, Wis +6, Cha +3

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Celestial Resilience. Resistance to radiant damage and bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.
Flyby. Flying out of an enemy’s reach provokes no opportunity attack.
Magic Resistance. Advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Magic Weapons. Its weapon attacks count as magical.
Seekers Sign. On hitting a creature with Talons or Golden Helm, the celebrun can mark it. It knows the target’s exact location whenever they share a plane. The mark ends when either dies or it marks a different creature.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Greatsword and one Talons attack, or two Golden Helm attacks.
Greatsword. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 10 (2d6 + 3) slashing damage.
Talons. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 8 (1d8 + 4) slashing plus 9 (2d8) radiant damage. A creature hit must pass a DC 14 Dexterity save or be Blinded until the end of its next turn.
Golden Helm. Ranged weapon attack, +7 to hit, range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit 9 (2d4 + 4) slashing plus 9 (2d8) radiant damage.
Whirling Wheel (recharge 5–6). Every creature within 10 ft. makes a DC 14 Dexterity save. Failure deals 14 (4d6) slashing plus 18 (4d8) radiant damage. Success halves both.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: Horn of Heaven. Choose a visible non-Celestial creature within 60 ft. that hears the horn. On a failed DC 14 Charisma save, golden light outlines it for 1 minute, negating the benefits of Invisible and granting advantage to attacks against it. Repeat the save at the end of each of its turns to end the effect.

gm.title: Reading Black Flag stat blocks
lines:
Rules source. Black Flag Reference Document, Monsters.
The printed modifiers and fixed HP are ready to use. For a Dexterity (Stealth) check to avoid the creature, use its Perception value as the DC. For a Wisdom (Perception) check to detect it, use its Stealth value as the DC.
Condition resistance gives advantage on checks and saves to avoid or end the named condition. Condition vulnerability gives disadvantage. Apply damage resistance and vulnerability to the amount of damage instead.

gm.title: Description
lines: This vampire drains a pinned victim’s mind and uses the same lunar powers as a nosferatu.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Adapted from the printed fledgling nosferatu. Initiative +8. Touch AC 14, flat-footed AC 22. BAB +3, grapple +4. Space and reach 5 ft. Fort +3, Ref +7, Will +6.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack or full attack. Choose slam +4 melee (1d6 + 1), +1 rapier +8 melee (1d6 + 2, 18–20), or masterwork heavy crossbow +8 ranged (1d10, 19–20/×2).
Domination (Su). Standard action on a target within 30 ft. that the vampire can look at. Will DC 18 or dominate person at caster level 12.
Intelligence Drain (Ex). Pin a living target in a grapple and drain 1d4 Intelligence each round the pin holds. At Intelligence 0 or less the victim becomes catatonic. Use this in place of Blood Drain. The source describes the persistent Domination save as a Blood Drain rider and gives no new rider for this replacement.
Children of the Night (Su, 1/day). Standard action to call 1d6 + 1 rat swarms, 1d4 + 1 bat swarms, or 3d6 wolves. They arrive in 2d6 rounds and serve for up to 1 hour.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
DR 10/silver and magic, cold and electricity resistance 10, turn resistance +4, spider climb, undead traits. Gaseous form as a standard action at will, with indefinite duration and fly speed 20 ft. (perfect). Alternate Form can assume bat, dire bat, wolf, or dire wolf form. As a standard action assume the listed animal form. Lose the slam and domination, gain the animal’s natural weapons and extraordinary attacks, and retain this form until the next sunrise or another change.
Lunar Regeneration. Direct moonlight converts past damage to nonlethal damage even after apparent death. Heal 3, 4, 6, or 8 per round in crescent, half, gibbous, or full moonlight, plus the age bonus. Fire, acid, and blessed or holy weapons deal normal damage. It can reattach severed limbs. It cannot regenerate a lost limb or recover nonlethal damage with its head detached.
Restful Sleep. While at 1 HP or more, heal 1 HP per HD per hour in its coffin. Daylight disables supernatural abilities. After exposure to direct sunlight, it must sleep in its coffin for 8 hours to restore them. Existing domination persists, and an alternate form cannot end until powers return.

gm.title: Spawn
lines: If a victim dies while its Intelligence is 0 or less from the drain, it rises under the creator’s control on the next full moon. A victim with 4 or fewer HD returns as spawn and one with 5 or more HD as a cerebral vampire. The creature regains its original Intelligence in undeath. Cerebral spawn also replace Blood Drain with Intelligence Drain. Nosferatu spawn retain charm, gaseous form, spider climb and daylight powerlessness. They heal 2 HP per hour asleep in their coffins if at 1 HP or more, or 2 HP per round in direct full moonlight.

gm.title: Repelling and slaying
lines: Garlic repels it, and a clearly presented holy symbol or mirror keeps it 5 ft. away. It cannot enter a private home without invitation. A stake through the heart kills it while left in place. At 0 HP it collapses but may return in moonlight. Burn the whole body or scatter the severed limbs beyond its minions’ reach. Running water costs one-third of HP each round and destroys it after 3 rounds of immersion.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Bluff +21, Diplomacy +16, Gather Information +11, Hide +12, Intimidate +12, Listen +12, Move Silently +12, Search +13, Sense Motive +15, Spot +12. Alertness, Combat Reflexes, Dodge, Great Fortitude, Improved Initiative, Lightning Reflexes, Skill Focus (Diplomacy), Weapon Finesse.

gm.title: Encounter adaptation
lines: Apply the strain to the 3.5 vampire template. Retain unmodified abilities, size, BAB, saves and skill points. The base vampire uses undead d12 Hit Dice and has no Constitution score. Keep an existing swim speed and ignore vulnerability to immersion in running water if the base creature can swim. Use save DC 10 + half HD rounded down + Charisma modifier unless specified. Age rows replace one another. Nosferatu lack the base vampire’s Energy Drain. Age DR always requires silver and magic. The cerebral subtype changes the feeding attack only.

gm.title: Age modifiers
lines:
Apply one row to a base creature. The sample already includes its adjustments. Ability scores are listed in Str, Dex, Int, Wis, Cha order.
Fledgling. Abilities 4/4/2/2/6. Speed +0 ft., natural AC +6, turn resistance +4, CR +2. DR 10, lunar healing +0.
Mature. Abilities 4/4/4/2/8. Speed +10 ft., natural AC +6, turn resistance +4, CR +2. DR 15, lunar healing +0.
Old. Abilities 6/6/4/4/8. Speed +10 ft., natural AC +7, turn resistance +5, CR +3. DR 15, lunar healing +1.
Ancient. Abilities 6/6/6/4/10. Speed +20 ft., natural AC +7, turn resistance +6, CR +3. DR 20, lunar healing +1.
Eminent. Abilities 8/8/6/6/10. Speed +20 ft., natural AC +8, turn resistance +7, CR +4. DR 20, lunar healing +2.
Patriarch. Abilities 10/10/8/8/12. Speed +30 ft., natural AC +8, turn resistance +8, CR +5. DR 25, lunar healing +3.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The cerebral subtype has no separate stat block. The header and combat stats use the printed nosferatu sample with the explicit feeding substitution.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Devil’s Sight. Magical darkness doesn’t impede the devil’s darkvision. Magic Resistance. The devil has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Multiattack. The devil makes two attacks with its chains. Chain. Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) slashing damage. The target is grappled (escape DC 14) if the devil isn’t already grappling a creature. Until this grapple ends, the target is restrained and takes 7 (2d6) piercing damage at the start of each of its turns. Animate Chains (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest). Up to four chains the devil can see within 60 feet of it magically sprout razor-edged barbs and animate under the devil’s control, provided that the chains aren’t being worn or carried. Each animated chain is an object with AC 20, 20 hit points, resistance to piercing damage, and immunity to psychic and thunder damage. When the devil uses Multiattack on its turn, it can use each animated chain to make one additional chain attack. An animated chain can grapple one creature of its own but can’t make attacks while grappling. An animated chain reverts to its inanimate state if reduced to 0 hit points or if the devil is incapacitated or dies.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Unnerving Mask. When a creature the devil can see starts its turn within 30 feet of the devil, the devil can create the illusion that it looks like one of the creature’s departed loved ones or bitter enemies. If the creature can see the devil, it must succeed on a DC 14 Wisdom saving throw or be frightened until the end of its turn.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Resistances Bludgeoning, Cold, Piercing, Slashing Immunities Fire, Poison; Poisoned Senses Darkvision 120 ft. (unimpeded by magical Darkness); Passive Perception 11 Languages Infernal; telepathy 120 ft.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Diabolical Restoration. If the devil dies outside the Nine Hells, its body disappears in sulfurous smoke, and it gains a new body instantly, reviving with all its Hit Points somewhere in the Nine Hells. Magic Resistance. The devil has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Multiattack. The devil makes two Chain attacks and uses Conjure Infernal Chain. Chain. Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 10 ft. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) Slashing damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 14) from one of two chains, and it has the Restrained condition until the grapple ends. Conjure Infernal Chain. The devil conjures a fiery chain to bind a creature. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 15, one creature the devil can see within 60 feet. Failure: 9 (2d4 + 4) Fire damage, and the target has the Restrained condition until the end of the devil’s next turn, at which point the chain disappears. If the target is Large or smaller, the devil moves the target up to 30 feet straight toward itself. Success: The chain disappears.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Unnerving Gaze. Trigger: A creature the devil can see starts its turn within 30 feet of the devil and can see the devil. Response—Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 15, the triggering creature. Failure: The target has the Frightened condition until the end of its turn. Success: The target is immune to this devil’s Unnerving Gaze for 24 hours.

gm.title: Description
lines: A jailer of the Nine Hells that binds victims with its own chains and animates loose chains nearby.

gm.title: Damage resistances
lines: Cold. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks that use no silvered weapon.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Devil's Sight. Magical darkness leaves the devil's darkvision unchanged.
Magic Resistance. It has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Chain attacks.
Chain. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 11 (2d6 + 4) slashing damage. If the devil isn't already grappling a creature, a creature hit is Grappled (escape DC 14). While held it is Restrained and takes 7 (2d6) piercing damage at the start of each of its turns.
Animate Chains (recharges after a short or long rest). Magically animate up to four visible chains within 60 ft. that nobody is wearing or carrying. Each chain grows barbs and becomes an object with AC 20, 20 HP, piercing resistance, and psychic and thunder immunity. When the devil uses Multiattack on its turn, each animated chain can make one additional Chain attack. Each chain can hold one creature in its own grapple and cannot attack while it holds that creature. A chain becomes inanimate at 0 HP or if the devil becomes Incapacitated or dies.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Unnerving Mask. When a creature the devil sees starts its turn within 30 ft., the devil can appear to be one of its departed loved ones or bitter enemies. If the creature sees the devil, it must succeed on a DC 14 Wisdom save or be Frightened until the end of that turn.

gm.title: Infernal return
lines: If it dies outside the Nine Hells, its body vanishes in smoke or dissolves into ichor. It returns immediately to its home layer at full strength. Death in the Nine Hells destroys the chain devil permanently.

lines: Darkvision 120 ft. Magical Darkness does not block this vision.

gm.title: Traits
lines:

lines:

lines: Unnerving Gaze. When a creature the devil can see starts its turn within 30 ft. and can see the devil, the devil can force that creature to make a DC 15 Wisdom save. lines: An Arak construct made from a stolen mortal shadow. Its maker assigns it a single task, which it pursues to the exclusion of nearly everything else.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack or full attack. One weapon attack at +2 for weapon damage. Noncombatants do not attack.

lines: Construct traits and darkvision 60 ft. Initiative +0, BAB/grapple +0/+0, space/reach 5 ft./5 ft., Fort +1, Ref +1, Will +1. It knows its former owner's languages and dissolves into shadow when killed. Racial skills count as trained despite having no skill points. Shadow Rift, solitary or pack of 2–12, no treasure. Its alignment follows its maker.

gm.title: Running the encounter
lines: An Arak puts a mortal to sleep with faerie food and lights a magic candle. Over its five-hour burn the mortal cannot wake unless it is extinguished. The Arak uses black dust and a silver sickle to remove the shadow, then must deliver it to the Shadow Rift before the candle goes out. Success creates the changeling and leaves the mortal as an Intelligence-less, shadowless automaton that refuses to defend itself. Wish or miracle restores the mortal. Resurrection cast on the living changeling destroys it and restores the mortal.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: CR is 0 for a noncombatant and 1 for a combatant. The entry prints no separate touch or flat-footed AC, innate poison profile, or poison DC.

gm.title: Setting spell
lines: Purge Contamination (3rd level). Cast for 1 hour and touch one contaminated humanoid. Consume 100 gp of alchemical fluids or holy water. Remove every contamination level and mutation, then give the target one level of Exhaustion for each level removed.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Spear. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit 4 (1d6 + 1) piercing damage, or 5 (1d8 + 1) on a two-handed melee attack.

gm.title: Delerium contamination
lines:
Printed source. Appendix C, pp. 222–223.
Add contamination levels from each exposure. A contaminated character rolls 1d20 at the end of each long rest and gains one level on a 1.
Symptoms are cumulative. Level 1 has no symptom. Level 2 halves healing from Hit Dice. Level 3 prevents HP recovery from a long rest. Level 4 halves damage the creature deals with weapon attacks and spells. Level 5 makes it Incapacitated. Level 6 triggers Monstrous Transformation.
After a character gains a level, roll 1d6. On a result at or below the current level, the GM chooses a new mutation or rolls on the printed mutations table. Replace or reroll duplicate mutations.
Contamination does not wear off. Purge Contamination can remove levels and causes Exhaustion. Heal removes all contamination and mutations. Each level removed also removes one random mutation. At level 0, all symptoms and mutations end.
A contaminated humanoid rises as a Haze Husk 24 hours after death. It rises as a Haze Wight if it had at least six class levels or Hit Dice. Raising a creature from the dead reduces its contamination by one level.
Monstrous Transformation. At level 6 or higher, the creature transforms after one round. Replace its statistics, hit points, and Hit Dice with those of a monster the GM chooses. Contamination resets to 0, and the GM controls the transformed creature.
Wish or similar magic can restore one transformed creature, clearing its madness and contamination. Using Wish this way gives the caster a 33 percent chance of losing the ability to cast it again.

lines: The printing explicitly lists spell save DC 12, +4 to hit with spells, and +3 to hit with the spear. The profile retains those values.

lines: A fly-shaped demon that hunts down deserters. Its drone can leave prey unconscious before it lands.

lines: A fly-like demon with clawed limbs, translucent wings and a stabbing proboscis.

gm.title: Senses
lines: Blindsight 10 ft., darkvision 120 ft., passive Perception 15.

gm.title: Defenses
lines: Resists cold, fire, and lightning. Immune to poison damage and Poisoned.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Drone. Each nondemon starting its turn within 30 ft. makes a DC 12 Constitution save or falls Unconscious for 10 minutes. A creature unable to hear the drone succeeds automatically. Damage ends this effect, as does another creature using an action to splash the target with holy water. A creature that saves or recovers is immune to the drone for 24 hours.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Claw +10 melee for 1d4 + 5 and energy drain, +1 kama +13 melee for 1d6 + 6, or masterwork sling +8 ranged for 1d4.
Full attack. Two of the listed claws, one listed kama attack, or one listed sling attack.
Mesmerism (Su). Standard action against one target within 30 ft. who meets its eyes. Will DC 17 or hold monster at caster level 12.
Energy Drain (Su). Claw hits bestow one negative level on a living target.
Blood Drain (Ex). Pin a living creature in a grapple. Each round the pin is maintained, drain 1d4 Constitution and gain 5 temporary HP.
Spell-like abilities. At will, insect plague and passwall at caster level 12. DC 17 if a save applies.
Children of the Night (Su). Once per day as a standard action, call 4d8 cats or 2d6 panthers using leopard statistics. They arrive after 2d6 rounds and serve for up to 1 hour.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
DR 10/bamboo and magic. Cold and electricity resistance 10. Turn resistance +4. Undead traits. The sample retains evasion, slow fall, stunning attack, and unarmed strike from monk. At 5th monk level, slow fall reduces the effective distance by 20 ft. when a wall is within reach.
Corrosion (Su). A nonmagical weapon that hits must make a DC 14 Fortitude save or take 2d8 acid damage, ignoring hardness.
Invisibility (Su). At will as a standard action, become invisible indefinitely until it makes a direct attack.
Weightless Step (Su). Levitate at will as a free action at caster level 12. The fledgling can also move horizontally up to 10 ft. in this state.
Alternate Form (Su). Assume tiger form as a standard action. It remains in that form until it changes again or until sunrise. Apply the ordinary vampire form rules to its native attacks and the tiger’s extraordinary attacks.

gm.title: Spawn
lines: A humanoid or monstrous humanoid killed by energy drain rises as vampire spawn 1d4 days after burial. One reduced to Constitution 0 by blood drain returns as spawn if it had 4 or fewer HD or as a chiang-shi if it had 5 or more. A creator controls its spawn until it dies.

gm.title: Repelling and slaying
lines:
It avoids smoke made by burning rosemary and myrrh and cannot touch a creature wearing a rosemary and ivy garland. It cannot cross running water on its own. It can be carried over in a coffin or on a conveyance. It rests by day in a coffin lined with native soil. Scattering rosemary and myrrh on that soil bars it permanently from that coffin.
Direct sunlight leaves it with a single move or attack action. It is destroyed in the next round if it cannot escape the light. Immersion in running water takes away one-third of its HP each round and destroys it at the end of round 3. A vampire strain whose base creature has a swim speed retains it and escapes the immersion weakness.
At 1 HP or more it heals 5 HP per round. At 0 HP or less it turns invisible and intangible and flees without attacking. It is destroyed if it misses the 2-hour deadline to reach its coffin. After 1 hour there it reaches 1 HP and resumes healing.
A bamboo shaft through the heart kills it while the shaft remains in place. For permanent destruction, bless a rosemary blossom, put it in the vampire’s mouth, then sew its lips and eyes shut with a silver needle and golden thread.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Balance +12, Bluff +10, Concentration +10, Diplomacy +10, Hide +12, Jump +13, Listen +13, Move Silently +12, Search +9, Sense Motive +11, Spot +13, Tumble +12. Alertness, Combat Reflexes, Deflect Arrows, Dodge, Improved Initiative, Lightning Reflexes, Weapon Focus with kama.

gm.title: Encounter details
lines: Any environment, especially Rokushima Táiyoo. Solitary, pair, or gang of 2–5. An organized group can contain 1–2 full vampires and 2–5 vampire spawn. Speaks languages known in life. Always evil. Double standard treasure. The printed monk has a +1 kama, bracers of armor +1, and two potions of cat’s grace.

gm.title: Template and age
lines: Apply the strain to a humanoid or monstrous humanoid using the 3.5 vampire template as the base. Keep its size, base attack, saves, skill points, d12 HD and applicable original powers. Constitution is absent. These age entries give the changes to Str, Dex, Int, Wis, Cha, speed and natural AC. Speed also specifies maximum horizontal movement while levitating. Damage reduction in every tier requires bamboo and magic to bypass. Apply one age row only. The sample above already incorporates its age. For unlisted save DCs use 10 + half HD, rounded down, + Cha modifier. The two spell-like abilities use 15 + Cha modifier instead. Claw damage follows the size table if the base creature has no claw attack. Where the printed example differs, use its own attack line.

gm.title: Caregiver scaling
lines: PB is the caregiver’s proficiency bonus.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Signature Attack (Bite). Melee weapon attack at +3 + PB, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 1d6 + PB piercing damage.

gm.title: Ferocity actions
lines:
Level 1, Ram’s Defense (2 Ferocity). Make a signature attack. A hit gives the target disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of the chimera’s next turn.
Level 3, Lion’s Leap (5 Ferocity). The chimera moves up to half its speed without provoking opportunity attacks. If it ends on the ground, each creature within 5 ft. makes a Strength save against DC 10 + PB or falls Prone.
Level 5, Volcanic Blow (8 Ferocity). Choose a visible point within 60 ft. Each creature in a 10-ft.-radius sphere around the point makes a Dexterity save against DC 10 + PB. It takes PBd6 fire damage on a failure or half on a success.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Protective Absorption (short or long rest). When the caregiver takes damage within 60 ft. of the chimera, the chimera can use its reaction to take half that damage in the caregiver’s place, rounded up.

gm.title: Mystic connection
lines: Defensive Eruption. At 9th level, a Beastheart with this companion and Mystic Connection can spend a bonus action once per long rest to unleash a burst of energy. Each enemy within 30 ft. makes a Dexterity save against the Beastheart’s exploit save DC. On a failure it takes 4d6 fire damage and falls Prone. On a success it takes half damage. The Beastheart and allies within 30 ft. have advantage on their next attack roll before the start of the Beastheart’s next turn.

gm.title: MCDM companion rules
lines:
Shared turn. The caregiver and companion act on the same turn. The companion moves and uses its reaction and bonus action independently. To do anything with its action besides Dash, Disengage or Dodge, it normally needs a command that costs the caregiver a bonus action. It must see or hear the caregiver. If the caregiver is Incapacitated, it can act without a command. The GM chooses who controls it when the caregiver is Incapacitated or absent.
Ferocity. At the start of their turn, unless Incapacitated, the companion gains 1d4 Ferocity plus one for each enemy it sees or hears within 5 ft. A swarm sharing one stat block counts as one enemy. Spend the listed cost before taking a Ferocity action. It uses the companion’s action, requires the listed caregiver level and is unavailable during a rampage.
Rampage. After rolling Ferocity, a companion with at least 10 Ferocity risks a rampage if it is not Incapacitated. A caregiver who is not Incapacitated and can be seen or heard can prevent it with a Wisdom (Animal Handling) check against DC 5 + Ferocity, without spending an action. If the companion rampages, it immediately moves toward the nearest creature it senses and makes its signature attack, with extra damage equal to half its Ferocity on a hit. If an ally and enemy tie for nearest, roll any die. On an odd roll the caregiver’s player chooses a tied ally. On an even roll they choose a tied enemy. If it cannot reach a target, it Dashes toward it. If it senses none, it moves as far as it can in a random safe direction. Ferocity falls to 0 after this action or at the end of the turn.
Recovery. At 0 HP, a companion makes death saves. After combat, Ferocity resets to 0. A companion that is not dying first regains HP equal to its remaining Ferocity.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A towering demon made from mismatched limbs, a violet crest, angular support legs, and several toothed maws.

gm.title: Classification
lines: Huge Fiend (Demon, Category 5), typically chaotic evil

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Saves Str +11, Dex +5, Cha +5. Intimidation +9, Perception +6. Resists cold, fire, and thunder. Darkvision 120 ft., Soulsight 30 ft., passive Perception 16. Abyssal and Common. Telepathy 120 ft.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Soul Resistance. With at least 2 souls, the chimeron has advantage on saving throws against powers, spells, and other supernatural effects.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make up to three different attacks from Powerful Bite, Scorching Bite, Booming Bite, and Chilling Bite.
Powerful Bite. Melee weapon attack +11, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 25 (4d8 + 7) piercing damage.
Scorching Bite. Melee weapon attack +11, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 11 (1d8 + 7) piercing plus 9 (2d8) fire damage. The target catches fire and takes 7 (2d6) fire damage at the start of each of its turns. The target or a creature that can reach it can use an action to put out the flames. Reigniting the target does not stack the ongoing damage.
Booming Bite (1 soul). Melee weapon attack +11, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 11 (1d8 + 7) piercing plus 9 (2d8) thunder damage. The target falls Prone.
Chilling Bite (1 soul). Melee weapon attack +11, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 11 (1d8 + 7) piercing plus 9 (2d8) cold damage. The target’s speed is halved through the end of its next turn, and it can make only one attack during that turn.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Pain Absorption (1 soul). When it takes damage, the chimeron reduces that damage by 16 (3d10).

gm.title: MCDM demon soul rules
lines:
Soul count. Use the printed starting total or roll the listed dice. Souls spent on a feature are deducted from the total. A demon can accumulate souls without a maximum.
Soul Devourer. When the demon drops a creature other than a Construct or Undead to 0 HP, or deals damage to a dying creature, that creature makes a DC 11 Wisdom save. On a failure, the demon consumes its soul, adds 1 to its soul count, and the creature dies. Only Wish can restore it to life.
Lethe. At 0 souls, the demon has advantage on attacks and disadvantage on saving throws, and its Intelligence is 3. On each turn it must use its movement to get as close as possible to the nearest creature it senses with Soulsight. If able, it must then use its action to attack that creature and attempt to kill it. It can pursue no other goal until its soul count rises.
Soulsight. Within the creature’s listed radius, it perceives creatures other than Constructs and Undead. This counts as seeing them for its features. Physical objects, total cover, and supernatural effects do not block this sense unless a rule says they do.

gm.title: Description
lines: A shy nature spirit about six inches tall. It peers out from rocks, plants, and streams, sometimes following a traveler to see what they do with their tools.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Evasion. When a Dexterity save would halve damage, the chwinga takes none on a success and half on a failure.
Unusual Nature. Chwingas sleep and need no air, food, or drink. When one dies, choose what remains: flower petals, a puff of pollen, a tiny statuette, a smooth stone, or fresh water.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines: Innate Spellcasting. Wisdom is the chwinga’s spellcasting ability. It needs no verbal or material components. At will: Druidcraft, Guidance, Pass without Trace, Resistance.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Magical Gift (1/day). Choose a humanoid the chwinga can see within 5 ft. The DM chooses one supernatural charm for that humanoid.
Natural Shelter. Enter a rock, living plant, or natural source of fresh water in the chwinga’s space. Attacks, spells, and other effects cannot target it while it is sheltered, and its blindsight still works. It can emerge as an action. Destroying the shelter puts the unharmed chwinga in the shelter’s space.

gm.title: Charm of Restoration
lines: The chwinga in Nangalore’s eastern spirit dome can favor the tallest party member with this gift. It has 6 charges. As an action, spend 4 charges to cast Greater Restoration or 2 to cast Lesser Restoration. The charm disappears when its charges are spent.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Tomb of Annihilation, pp. 216–217. See p. 77 for Nangalore’s charm and p. 104 for the wagon encounter. Supernatural charms are in the Dungeon Master’s Guide (2014), chapter 7.

gm.title: Encounter context
lines: In Omu, a chwinga shelters in a mossy disk beneath an overturned wagon. It comes out if travelers leave an offering or follows them secretly if they pass by. It favors curly hair or beards. Vegepygmies flee once they notice it with the party. It stays outside shrines and dungeons.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Evasion. If a Dexterity save normally halves damage, the chwinga takes none on a success and half on a failure. This trait has no effect while the chwinga is incapacitated.
Unusual Nature. The chwinga needs no air, food, or drink. At death, the DM chooses what it becomes: moondust, sparkling spores, a likeness in miniature, a piece of ice, or a twelve-sided sponge.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Magical Gift (1/day). Bestow a supernatural charm of the DM’s choice on a visible Humanoid within 5 ft. See the Spelljammer charms below or the Dungeon Master’s Guide.
Natural Shelter. Enter a rock, bush, tree, or natural freshwater source located in the chwinga’s space. While sheltered, the chwinga retains its blindsight and cannot be targeted by attacks, spells, or other effects. It can emerge as an action. Destroying the shelter places the chwinga unharmed in the shelter’s space.
Spellcasting. Cast Druidcraft, Guidance, Pass without Trace, or Resistance at will using Charisma. The spells require no material or verbal components.

Charm of Instant Tools. The recipient conjures one set of Artisan’s Tools, Navigator’s Tools, or Thieves’ Tools in hand or in their space. The charm ends after one use. The tools stay.

gm.title: Description
lines: A painted clay guardian of Shagambi’s shrine. It bears a bronze spear and a wooden shield, and returns to its cell when destroyed.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Climbing. It can climb difficult surfaces and ceilings without a check.
Steadfast. It cannot be disarmed or make ranged attacks.
Brute. Its melee weapon hits include an extra weapon damage die, already counted below.
Construct Nature. It needs no air, food, drink, or sleep and cannot speak.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three melee attacks.
Spear. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 11 (2d6 + 4) piercing damage, or 13 (2d8 + 4) when wielded with two hands.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Parry. Add 3 to its AC against one melee attack that would hit it. It must see the attacker and hold a melee weapon.

gm.title: Shagambi’s shrine
lines: Four cells hold one guardian apiece. At least 50 lb. on the pit’s pressure plate raises the cell gates and calls the guardians. A gladiator fights if attacked or called to the pit. It cannot leave the shrine. At 0 HP outside the pit, it and its gear disappear and it immediately reforms in its cell at full health with spear and shield. It can then return to the pit. A gladiator destroyed in the pit leaves its spear behind as it reforms. If a spear leaves the shrine, it returns to the gladiator’s hand. When no other creatures remain inside, the gladiators return to their cells and the gates close. Place one spear from each guardian in the four warrior statues to free Shagambi’s puzzle cube.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Tomb of Annihilation, p. 100. The shrine gives changes to the 2014 Gladiator stat block and separate reformation rules.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Acid Absorption. Whenever the golem is subjected to acid damage, it takes no damage and instead regains a number of hit points equal to the acid damage dealt. Berserk. Whenever the golem starts its turn with 60 hit points or fewer, roll a d6. On a 6, the golem goes berserk. On each of its turns while berserk, the golem attacks the nearest creature it can see. If no creature is near enough to move to and attack, the golem attacks an object, with preference for an object smaller than itself. Once the golem goes berserk, it continues to do so until it is destroyed or regains all its hit points. Immutable Form. The golem is immune to any spell or effect that would alter its form. Magic Resistance. The golem has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects. Magic Weapons. The golem’s weapon attacks are magical.

gm.title: Actions

The target dies if this attack reduces its hit point maximum to 0. The reduction lasts until removed by the greater restoration spell or other magic. Haste (Recharge 5–6). Until the end of its next turn, the golem magically gains a +2 bonus to its AC, has advantage on Dexterity saving throws, and can use its slam attack as a bonus action.

While attached, the cloaker can make this attack only against the target and has advantage on the attack roll. The cloaker can detach itself by spending 5 feet of its movement. A creature, including the target, can take its action to detach the cloaker by succeeding on a DC 16 Strength check. Tail. Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 10 ft., one creature. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) slashing damage. Moan. Each creature within 60 feet of the cloaker that can hear its moan and that isn’t an aberration must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw or become frightened until the end of the cloaker’s next turn. If a creature’s saving throw is successful, the creature is immune to the cloaker’s moan for the next 24 hours Phantasms (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest). The cloaker magically creates three illusory duplicates of itself if it isn’t in bright light. The duplicates move with it and mimic its actions, shifting position so as to make it impossible to track which cloaker is the real one. If the cloaker is ever in an area of bright light, the duplicates disappear. Whenever any creature targets the cloaker with an attack or a harmful spell while a duplicate remains, that creature rolls randomly to determine whether it targets the cloaker or one of the duplicates. A creature is unaffected by this magical effect if it can’t see or if it relies on senses other than sight. A duplicate has the cloaker’s AC and uses its saving throws. If an attack hits a duplicate, or if a duplicate fails a saving throw against an effect that deals damage, the duplicate disappears.

lines: A clockwork bodyguard that wants to be human. Its flourishes keep opponents off balance, but each damaging strike spends some of the time left in its springs.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Very rare. Solitary. Active any time. No food. Very to exceptional intelligence (11–16). Fearless morale (19–20). Height 6 feet. No magic resistance. A destroyed automaton yields Q × 2 in gems and 1d4 × 1,000 gp in precious metal.

gm.title: Hit Dice, THAC0 and XP
lines:
5 HD: THAC0 15, 650 XP.
6 HD: THAC0 15, 975 XP.
7 HD: THAC0 13, 1,400 XP.
8 HD: THAC0 13, 2,000 XP.
9–10 HD: THAC0 11, adding 1,000 XP per HD above 8.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Weapons. Two attacks by weapon with +1 to hit and +3 damage for effective Strength 18. It usually carries a rapier and main-gauche or a saber and stiletto. There is a 20% chance it also has a wheellock pistol. Each point of damage it deals costs one hour of activity.
Additional action. Roll d100 each round. 01–25 fancy move, parry as a 10th-level fighter and improve AC by 6. 26–45 amusing quip, same parry and a taunt against one target. 46–60 salute or disarm. The salute gives allies +1 to attack for one round per Hit Die. 61–75 compliment, an opposite-sex target saves vs. spell or comes under charm person. 76–90 embarrassing maneuver, make a called shot at no penalty and follow a success with an amusing quip. 91–100 bold fencing attack, gain +2 to attack this round and force the foe back 1d10 steps. Ignore that last result when fewer than 50 hours remain.

gm.title: Skills and defenses
lines: Use the abilities and nonweapon proficiencies of a swashbuckler of level equal to HD, with no fighting school. Proficiency checks succeed on 18 or less. Immune to mind-influencing magic such as charm person and suggestion. ESP and telepathy can still affect it. If exposed to moisture, save vs. poison or take 6d6 damage 1d4 days later. It fears rust monsters.

gm.title: Winding
lines: Maximum runtime is 10 hours per HP, then it goes dormant. Roll d100 for the percentage remaining when encountered, with a 10% minimum. Below 50%, it heads back to its creator. Rewinding restores one hour per round. Attempting to wind it fully has a 10% chance of destroying it. Only its creator can repair it, and it cannot be raised. It cannot rewind itself. Models of at least 9 HD often need a magical key kept by their maker.

gm.title: Variants
lines: A host to a heroic spirit can rewind itself upon obtaining its key. The spirit can stay until the mechanism rusts. A rogue automaton hosts a legacy leech, can rewind without a key, and uses effective Strength 19. It keeps its swashbuckler abilities and can use Legacies its symbiont shares. Ordinary swordsmen neither gain Legacies nor require cinnabryl.

printings.label: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants

gm.title: Description
lines: A cloud giant lays wagers against rivals across the planes and wears a runic half mask that cuts through magical trickery.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Cloud Rune. A mask in the giant’s possession bears the rune. While holding or wearing it, the giant has truesight out to 30 ft. and can use Thunderous Clap and Negate Spell. The mask has AC 15, 45 HP, and immunity to necrotic, poison, and psychic damage. It recovers all its HP at the end of every turn. It turns to dust at 0 HP or when the giant dies. If the rune is destroyed, the giant can inscribe it on a mask it possesses when it finishes a short or long rest.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three Flying Staff attacks.
Flying Staff. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +14 to hit, reach 10 ft. or range 30/90 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 18 (3d6 + 8) bludgeoning damage plus 16 (3d10) thunder damage. The staff magically returns to the giant’s hand immediately after a ranged attack, hit or miss.
Thunderous Clap (requires Cloud Rune). Magically summon a thundercloud in a 30-ft.-radius sphere around a visible point within 60 ft. It spreads around corners. Each creature in the cloud makes a DC 20 Constitution save. Failure deals 52 (8d12) thunder damage and knocks the creature prone. Success halves the damage and avoids being knocked prone. The clap is audible 300 ft. from the center. The cloud heavily obscures the area until the start of the giant’s next turn or until strong wind disperses it.
Spellcasting. Cast one listed spell without material components, using Charisma (save DC 20).
At will. Detect Magic, Fog Cloud, Light, Minor Illusion.
1/day each. Dream (as an action), Gaseous Form, Major Image.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Negate Spell (requires Cloud Rune). When the giant sees a creature within 60 ft. casting a spell, it can interrupt the casting. A spell cast with a slot of 3rd level or lower fails. For a spell of 4th level or higher, the caster must pass a DC 18 Intelligence save or the spell fails.

gm.title: Optional wager spells
lines: For a giant that has won a wager for spellcasting power, add one or more of Circle of Death, Harm, Otiluke’s Freezing Sphere, and Sunbeam to Spellcasting. Each added spell is usable once per day.

gm.title: Description
lines: A lodestone-powered construct that guards the most restricted archives of the Cobalt Soul.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Immune to fire, lightning, poison and psychic damage. Immune to bludgeoning, piercing and slashing damage from nonmagical weapons that are not adamantine. Immune to Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Paralyzed, Petrified and Poisoned. Darkvision 120 ft., passive Perception 10. Understands its creator’s languages but cannot speak.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Immutable Form. Effects and spells cannot change the golem’s shape.
Magic Resistance. It rolls saves against spells and other magical effects with advantage.
Magic Weapons. Its weapon attacks count as magical.
Conductive Body. Lightning causes no damage. Instead, through the end of the golem’s next turn, its weapon attacks deal an extra 11 (2d10) lightning damage. In that window, a creature takes 11 (2d10) lightning damage if it touches the golem or hits it with a melee attack from within 5 ft.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Use Slam and Sword, or use Magnetic Pulse followed by Spinning Cleave.
Slam. Melee weapon attack +15 within 5 ft. Hit for 25 (3d10 + 9) bludgeoning.
Sword. Melee weapon attack +15 within 10 ft. Hit for 28 (3d12 + 9) slashing.
Spinning Cleave. Make a Sword attack against every creature within 10 ft.
Magnetic Pulse (recharge 6). Unattended metal objects within 30 ft. are pulled into unoccupied spaces within 5 ft. of the golem. A creature within 30 ft. that is made of metal or wearing metal armor must pass a DC 20 Strength save or be pulled into an unoccupied space within 5 ft. of the golem and knocked Prone.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Berserk. At the start of a turn when the cobblefright has 40 HP or fewer, roll a d6. On a 6 it goes berserk. While berserk, it attacks the nearest creature it can see each turn. If it cannot move to and attack a creature, it attacks an object, preferring one smaller than itself. It stays berserk until destroyed or restored to full HP.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three Claw attacks. One may be replaced by Grab.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 8 (1d8 + 4) slashing damage.
Grab. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one creature the cobblefright is not already grappling. On a hit the creature is Grappled (escape DC 15). The cobblefright can hold up to two creatures. At the start of its turn, it can squeeze each creature held, once per target. Each squeezed creature must pass a DC 15 Strength save or take 13 (2d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage.
Soul Siphon. One creature held by the cobblefright makes a DC 14 Constitution save, taking 11 (2d10) necrotic damage on a failure or half on a success. Reduce the target's hit point maximum by the necrotic damage dealt and restore the same number of hit points to the cobblefright. The reduction lasts until the target completes a short or long rest.

gm.title: Reading Black Flag stat blocks
lines:
Rules source. Black Flag Reference Document, Monsters.
The printed modifiers and fixed HP are ready to use. For a Dexterity (Stealth) check to avoid the creature, use its Perception value as the DC. For a Wisdom (Perception) check to detect it, use its Stealth value as the DC.
Condition resistance gives advantage on checks and saves to avoid or end the named condition. Condition vulnerability gives disadvantage. Apply damage resistance and vulnerability to the amount of damage instead.

gm.title: Description
lines: Faithful artisans build these towering figures in honor of their gods. A divine power can awaken the crystal in a colossus's heart and send it to defend the faithful or carry out the deity's will. Many lie dormant in remote places.

gm.title: Languages
lines: Understands Celestial and Common, and can't speak.

gm.title: Condition immunities
lines: Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Stunned, Unconscious.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Immutable Form. The colossus can't shape-shift.
Legendary Resistance (4/day). When it fails a saving throw, the colossus can spend a use to succeed.
Magic Resistance. The colossus has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
Siege Monster. The colossus deals double damage to objects and structures.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three attacks using Slam or Radiant Ray in any combination.
Slam. Melee attack, +18 to hit, reach 20 ft. A hit deals 32 (4d10 + 10) Bludgeoning damage and pushes the target up to 20 ft. directly away from the colossus.
Radiant Ray. Ranged attack, +18 to hit, range 300 ft. A hit deals 22 (4d10) Radiant damage. A Large or smaller creature hit also falls Prone.
Divine Beam (Recharge 5–6). Creatures in a 300-ft.-long, 10-ft.-wide Line make a DC 26 Dexterity save. The beam deals 65 (10d12) Radiant damage on a failure or half as much on a success. If this damage reduces a creature to 0 HP, it disintegrates into dust. The magic items it wore or carried remain.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
3 uses. The colossus can spend one use on an option immediately after another creature's turn. It cannot do so while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. It regains spent uses at the start of its turn.
Smite. Make one Radiant Ray attack.
Stomp. Move up to half its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks. The colossus can make one Slam attack at any point during this move.

Crumbling Destruction. At 0 HP, the colossus crumbles and is destroyed. Each creature on the ground within 30 ft. makes a DC 22 Dexterity save. A creature takes 22 (4d10) bludgeoning plus 22 (4d10) fire damage on a failure, or half as much on a success.
Fire Absorption. When fire would damage the colossus, it instead regains HP equal to that fire damage.
Immutable Form. Spells and effects can't alter its form.
Magic Weapons. The colossus's weapon attacks are magical.
Siege Monster. The colossus deals double damage to objects and structures.

gm.title: Actions

lines: Selesnya dryads advise the Conclave and help design its enclaves. A dryad leading troops may ride an elk-shaped mount made from living branches and vines.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Magic Resistance. The dryad makes saves against spells and other magical effects with advantage.
Speak with Beasts and Plants. The dryad can converse with beasts and plants as though they share a language.

gm.title: Innate Spellcasting
lines:
Charisma sets the dryad's spell save DC to 17. It needs no material components.
At will. Druidcraft.
3/day each. Dispel Magic, Entangle, Plant Growth, Spike Growth.
1/day each. Moonbeam, Grasping Vine, Wall of Thorns.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three attacks in any combination of Vine Staff and Longbow.
Vine Staff. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 12 (2d6 + 5) bludgeoning damage. A creature hit makes a DC 17 Dexterity save. On a failure, vines restrain it for 1 minute. It can use an action to end the effect on itself with a successful DC 17 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check.
Longbow. Ranged weapon attack, +8 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (1d8 + 4) piercing damage.
Summon Mount (1/day). Magically bring forth the mount in an unoccupied space within 60 ft. Use the Elk stat block. The mount is a plant with Intelligence 6 and understands Sylvan but cannot speak. It remains for 8 hours, until it or the dryad dies, or until the dryad spends an action to dismiss it. The dryad can speak with it telepathically within 1 mile.
Suppress Magic (Recharge 5–6). Choose one magic item the dryad can see within 120 ft. If it is an artifact, the effect fails. Otherwise its magic shuts off for 10 minutes, until the dryad becomes incapacitated or dies, or until it uses a bonus action to restore the item's magic.

gm.title: Description
lines: A copper dragon can become a greatwyrm by bringing together counterparts across worlds. It can breathe acid or release a cone of sapping gas.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Metallic Awakening (recharges after a short or long rest). When the creature would drop to 0 HP, set its current HP to 450, recharge Breath Weapon, and restore all spent uses of Legendary Resistance. The creature can take mythic actions for the following hour. Award 120,000 extra XP if defeated after this trait activates (240,000 XP total).
Legendary Resistance (4/day). Turn a failed save into a success.
Unusual Nature. The greatwyrm needs no food or drink.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 21 (2d10 + 10) piercing damage plus 13 (2d12) force damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 19 (2d8 + 10) slashing damage. A Huge or smaller creature hit is grappled (escape DC 20) and restrained until the grapple ends. The greatwyrm can hold only one creature with this attack at a time.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 21 (2d10 + 10) bludgeoning damage. A creature hit must succeed on a DC 26 Strength save or fall prone.
Breath Weapon (recharge 5–6). Choose Elemental Breath or Sapping Breath.
Elemental Breath. Each creature in a 300-ft. cone makes a DC 25 Dexterity save, taking 84 (13d12) acid damage on a failure or half on a success.
Sapping Breath. Each creature in a 300-ft. cone makes a DC 25 Constitution save. A failure leaves the creature unconscious for 1 minute. An unconscious creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. A creature that succeeds on the first save has disadvantage on attack rolls and saving throws until the end of the greatwyrm’s next turn.
Change Shape. Magically take the form of any Medium or Small creature, retaining the greatwyrm’s statistics except size. The form ends if the greatwyrm drops to 0 HP or spends an action to end it.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:

Attack (1 action). Make one Claw or Tail attack.

gm.title: Actions

gm.title: Actions
lines: Bite. Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 8 (1d6 + 5) piercing damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned for 24 hours. The couatl magically polymorphs into a humanoid or beast that has a challenge rating equal to or less than its own, or back into its true form. It reverts to its true form if it dies. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying is absorbed or borne by the new form (the couatl’s choice). In a new form, the couatl retains its game statistics and ability to speak, but its AC, movement modes, Strength, Dexterity, and other actions are replaced by those of the new form, and it gains any statistics and capabilities (except class features, legendary actions, and lair actions) that the new form has but that it lacks. gm.title: Description
lines: This vampire lord pins opponents with spears of darkness and drains their vitality with Sanguinus.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Saving throws Dex +11, Wis +9, Cha +12. Deception +12, History +11, Intimidation +12, Perception +9, Persuasion +12, Stealth +11. Resists necrotic and bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from mundane attacks. Immune to Charmed, Flanked, Frightened, Prone, and Stunned. Blindsight 60 ft., darkvision 120 ft., passive Perception 19. Common.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Vampire lair actions, p. 269. Stat block, p. 272.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Resting Place. If Rhodar drops to 0 HP away from his resting place, he teleports there. At 0 HP there he is stable, and after an hour there at 0 HP he regains 1 HP.
Spear Sacrifice (3/day). Rhodar starts with three floating spears and can call one to a free hand on his turn without an action. When he fails a check or save, he can destroy a spear to succeed. He can use neither Spear Sacrifice nor Spear of the Damned after the last spear is destroyed. Destroyed spears return at dusk.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Sanguinus attacks. Rhodar can also make one Spear of the Damned attack per remaining use of Spear Sacrifice.
Sanguinus. Melee weapon attack +12, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 13 (2d6 + 6) slashing plus 14 (4d6) necrotic damage. A creature's maximum HP falls by the necrotic damage taken and Rhodar heals that amount. The reduction lasts until Cure Ailment of 4th order or higher, Greater Restoration, or a similar supernatural effect removes it. A target whose maximum HP drops to 0 dies. A humanoid killed this way rises as a vampire spawn under Rhodar's control at the following midnight.
Spear of the Damned. Ranged spell attack +12, range 60 ft., one target. Hit 10 (3d6) force damage. A creature hit falls Prone and is Restrained by the spear. It or a creature that can reach it can use an action or a bonus action to attempt a DC 20 Strength (Athletics) check, freeing it on a success. It is also freed if Rhodar summons the spear to attack someone else or destroys it with Spear Sacrifice.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines:
Beguile. Pick one visible creature within 30 ft. that can see Rhodar. On a failed DC 20 Wisdom save, the target spends its reaction, if available, to move up to its speed to a location Rhodar chooses. Rhodar chooses whether it then falls Prone or makes a melee attack against a target he picks.
Inhuman Agility. Move up to speed without provoking opportunity attacks.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Withering Stare. When a visible creature within 60 ft. hits Rhodar, that creature makes a DC 20 Wisdom save or takes 10 (3d6) necrotic damage.

gm.title: Villain Actions
lines:
Use each villain action once per encounter after an enemy's turn. Use at most one per round, in any order.
Action 1, Bloodstained. Center a 20-ft.-radius sphere on a point Rhodar sees within 120 ft. Each creature there other than an Undead makes a DC 20 Dexterity save. On a failure, it is bloodstained until the end of Rhodar's next turn. He has advantage on attacks against it, and it has disadvantage on saves against his Beguile.
Action 2, Fire Drake. Rhodar and his gear turn into a Large dragon of fire. He releases any creature he is grappling and any Grappled or Restrained effect on him ends. He flies up to twice his speed to an unoccupied space, ignoring difficult terrain and opportunity attacks and able to pass through creatures and objects. Each creature he passes through makes a DC 20 Dexterity save, taking 36 (8d8) fire damage on a failure or half on a success. He then returns to his previous form.
Action 3, Mist of Blades. The area within 60 ft. is heavily obscured for other creatures. Rhodar can teleport up to four times to unoccupied spaces in the mist. After each teleport he can make one Sanguinus attack. The mist disappears at the end of the action.

gm.title: Utility Spells
lines: Charisma, save DC 20. At will, 1 action each: Charm Person, Detect Thoughts, Disguise Self, Sending. 3/day each, longer casting times: Clairvoyance, Geas (9th level), Legend Lore.

gm.title: Lair Actions
lines:
When fighting in its lair, a vampire takes one lair action at initiative count 20, losing ties. It cannot repeat the same action in consecutive rounds.
Children of the Night. Bats and insects move with the vampire. The area within 30 ft. of it is heavily obscured for other creatures until the end of initiative count 20 of the next round.
Blood Rain. Choose a visible point within 60 ft. Blood falls there in a 10-ft.-radius, 40-ft.-high cylinder until the end of initiative count 20 of the next round. A creature other than an Undead that takes necrotic damage while inside takes an extra 5 (1d10) necrotic damage.
Obey My Desire. Each creature within 60 ft. that hears the vampire makes a DC 18 Wisdom save or is Charmed until the end of this turn. Each creature Charmed this way immediately spends its reaction, if available, to make a melee attack against another creature, make one against itself, or fall Prone. The vampire picks the effect.

gm.title: Flanked (MCDM)
lines: If using flanking rules, creatures cannot flank Rhodar.

lines: A mundane attack is one that uses neither magic nor psionics.

gm.title: Description
lines: A persistent cloud tower holds a sleeping scion. Disturb it and the cloud takes the shape of a towering wind elemental.

gm.title: Damage resistances
lines: Cold, fire, lightning. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.

gm.title: Condition immunities
lines: Exhaustion, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained, stunned.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Awakening of the Scion. At 0 HP, the cradle dissipates into wisps of cloud. Scion of Memnor immediately appears in the space it occupied and takes its initiative count.
Flyby. Flying out of an enemy’s reach does not provoke an opportunity attack.
Legendary Resistance (5/day). The cradle can turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Magic Resistance. The cradle has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Siege Monster. The cradle deals double damage to objects and structures.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three attacks in any combination of Slam and Wind Javelin.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +17 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 31 (4d10 + 9) bludgeoning damage plus 19 (3d12) thunder damage.
Wind Javelin. Ranged weapon attack, +17 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 27 (4d8 + 9) bludgeoning damage plus 10 (3d6) thunder damage. The target must pass a DC 25 Strength save or fall prone.
Vortex (recharge 5–6). Center a cylinder 30 ft. in radius and 100 ft. high on a visible point within 90 ft. Each creature other than the cradle inside makes a DC 25 Dexterity save. Failure deals 71 (11d12) bludgeoning damage and restrains the creature in the vortex. Success halves the damage and pushes the creature to the nearest unoccupied space outside the cylinder. The vortex lasts until the start of the cradle’s next turn. Creatures still restrained by it fall prone when it ends.
A creature restrained by the vortex can use an action to attempt a DC 19 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check. On success, it escapes and moves 3d6 × 10 ft. away in a random direction.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Thunderclap. Immediately after taking damage, the cradle can force every other creature in a 30-ft.-radius sphere centered on itself to make a DC 25 Constitution save. Failure deals 18 (4d8) thunder damage and deafens the creature for 1 minute.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines: One or more of the regional effects listed under Scion of Memnor can begin while the scion still sleeps inside the cradle.

lines: Cold, fire, lightning. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Awakening of the Scion. At 0 HP, the cradle crumbles into soil and moss. Scion of Grolantor immediately appears in the space it occupied and takes its initiative count.
Legendary Resistance (5/day). The cradle can turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Magic Resistance. The cradle has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Siege Monster. The cradle deals double damage to objects and structures.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three attacks in any combination of Slam and Spit Rock, plus one Grasping Root attack.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +14 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 33 (4d12 + 7) bludgeoning damage.
Spit Rock. Ranged weapon attack, +14 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 25 (4d8 + 7) bludgeoning damage. The target must pass a DC 22 Strength save or fall prone.
Grasping Root. Melee weapon attack, +14 to hit, reach 30 ft., one creature the cradle isn’t already grappling. A hit grapples the target (escape DC 17). While grappled, the target takes 29 (4d10 + 7) bludgeoning damage at the start of each of its turns. The root has AC 19. A single hit that deals at least 15 slashing damage to the root severs it, freeing the target without damaging the cradle.
Rolling Hills (recharge 6). Magically create a wave of dirt from a point on the ground within 120 ft. It can extend up to 30 ft. in length, height, and width. Each creature in the wave makes a DC 22 Strength save. Failure deals 58 (9d12) bludgeoning damage, knocks the creature prone, and buries it. Success halves the damage only.
A buried creature is restrained, has total cover, and can’t breathe. The buried creature or an unburied creature within 5 ft. can use an action to make a DC 17 Strength (Athletics) check. Success ends the prone and restrained conditions from the burial.

gm.title: Delerium contamination
lines:
Printed source. Appendix C, pp. 222–223.
Add contamination levels from each exposure. A contaminated character rolls 1d20 at the end of each long rest and gains one level on a 1.
Symptoms are cumulative. Level 1 has no symptom. Level 2 halves healing from Hit Dice. Level 3 prevents HP recovery from a long rest. Level 4 halves damage the creature deals with weapon attacks and spells. Level 5 makes it Incapacitated. Level 6 triggers Monstrous Transformation.
After a character gains a level, roll 1d6. On a result at or below the current level, the GM chooses a new mutation or rolls on the printed mutations table. Replace or reroll duplicate mutations.
Contamination does not wear off. Purge Contamination can remove levels and causes Exhaustion. Heal removes all contamination and mutations. Each level removed also removes one random mutation. At level 0, all symptoms and mutations end.
A contaminated humanoid rises as a Haze Husk 24 hours after death. It rises as a Haze Wight if it had at least six class levels or Hit Dice. Raising a creature from the dead reduces its contamination by one level.
Monstrous Transformation. At level 6 or higher, the creature transforms after one round. Replace its statistics, hit points, and Hit Dice with those of a monster the GM chooses. Contamination resets to 0, and the GM controls the transformed creature.
Wish or similar magic can restore one transformed creature, clearing its madness and contamination. Using Wish this way gives the caster a 33 percent chance of losing the ability to cast it again.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

Dispersed Vines (Ex). Cover one 5-by-5-ft. square per HD, on the ground or on a wall. Track each die’s HP separately. A section at 0 HP or with a comparable loss such as a negative level cannot act. At −10 HP it is destroyed. An area attack deals full damage to every section it reaches.

gm.title: Description
lines: A crimson dragon stalks the cursed lands for cinnabryl. It often feints or puts on a display of Legacies before committing to a fight.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Solitary. Very rare in cursed lands. Active by day. Carnivore. Genius intelligence (17–18). Fanatic morale (17–18). All speak a dragon dialect other crimson and evil dragons understand. The chance of communicating with any intelligent creature starts at 15% for a hatchling and rises 5 percentage points per later age category.

gm.title: Age tiers
lines:
1. Hatchling, 0–5 years. 7 HD, AC 0, THAC0 13, combat modifier +1. Fear none. Magic resistance 0. Spells none. Treasure none, 2,000 XP. Body 2–16 ft., tail 4–16 ft.
2. Very Young, 6–15 years. 9 HD, AC -1, THAC0 11, combat modifier +2. Fear none. Magic resistance 0. Spells none. Treasure none, 3,000 XP. Body 16–27 ft., tail 16–25 ft.
3. Young, 16–25 years. 11 HD, AC -2, THAC0 9, combat modifier +3. Fear none. Magic resistance 0. Spells none. Treasure B, 5,000 XP. Body 27–42 ft., tail 25–34 ft.
4. Juvenile, 26–50 years. 13 HD, AC -3, THAC0 7, combat modifier +4. Fear none. Magic resistance 0. Spells none. Treasure BI, 8,000 XP. Body 42–61 ft., tail 34–53 ft.
5. Young Adult, 51–100 years. 14 HD, AC -4, THAC0 7, combat modifier +5. Fear 15 yd., save +3. Magic resistance 20%. Spells none. Treasure BI, 10,000 XP. Body 61–80 ft., tail 53–72 ft.
6. Adult, 101–200 years. 15 HD, AC -5, THAC0 5, combat modifier +6. Fear 20 yd., save +2. Magic resistance 25%. Spells 1 wizard. Treasure BH, 12,000 XP. Body 80–99 ft., tail 72–91 ft.
7. Mature Adult, 201–400 years. 16 HD, AC -6, THAC0 5, combat modifier +7. Fear 25 yd., save +1. Magic resistance 30%. Spells 2 wizard. Treasure BH, 13,000 XP. Body 99–118 ft., tail 91–110 ft.
8. Old, 401–600 years. 17 HD, AC -7, THAC0 5, combat modifier +8. Fear 30 yd., save +0. Magic resistance 35%. Spells 2/1 wizard. Treasure BHU, 14,000 XP. Body 118–137 ft., tail 110–129 ft.
9. Very Old, 601–800 years. 18 HD, AC -8, THAC0 5, combat modifier +9. Fear 35 yd., save −1. Magic resistance 40%. Spells 2/2 wizard. Treasure BHU, 15,000 XP. Body 137–157 ft., tail 129–148 ft.
10. Venerable, 801–1,000 years. 19 HD, AC -9, THAC0 5, combat modifier +10. Fear 40 yd., save −2. Magic resistance 45%. Spells 2/2/1 wizard, 1 priest. Treasure BH + U × 2, 16,000 XP. Body 157–177 ft., tail 148–168 ft.
11. Wyrm, 1,001–2,000 years. 20 HD, AC -10, THAC0 5, combat modifier +11. Fear 45 yd., save −3. Magic resistance 50%. Spells 2/2/2 wizard, 2 priest. Treasure BH + U × 2, 18,000 XP. Body 177–197 ft., tail 168–188 ft.
12. Great Wyrm, 1,200+ years. 21 HD, AC -11, THAC0 5, combat modifier +12. Fear 50 yd., save −4. Magic resistance 55%. Spells 3/2/2/1 wizard, 2/1 priest. Treasure BH + U × 3, 20,000 XP. Body 197–217 ft., tail 188–208 ft.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Claws and bite. Two claws at 1d8 each and a bite at 4d6. Add the age tier’s combat modifier to each physical damage roll. Claws can strike the front and sides, and the bite also reaches behind. The dragon saves as a fighter of level equal to HD.
Cinnabryl breath. From Juvenile onward, the dragon can breathe once every three rounds, giving up its other attacks that round. It produces a 100-foot cone measuring 5 feet wide at its mouth and 50 feet across at the far end. It depletes all cinnabryl and ruins crimson essence in the cone. The dragon has a cumulative 3% chance per ounce depleted to gain one new Legacy. The cone does not increase with age.

gm.title: Other dragon attacks
lines:
Kick. Against a target behind it, deal claw damage. The target rolls Dexterity or lower on 1d20 or is pushed 1d6 feet plus 1 foot per age tier. A pushed target saves vs. petrification with the combat modifier as a penalty or falls. Use one hind leg if also attacking with a claw. No tail slap in the same round.
Snatch. From Young Adult, dive to grab a target at least two sizes smaller. On a hit there is a 50% chance of pinning its arms. The dragon can drop it, deal automatic claw damage each round, or transfer it to its jaws with another successful attack roll for automatic bite damage each round. Old dragons can snatch two targets. Wyrms and Great Wyrms can carry three by transferring one to the mouth.
Wing buffet. From Young Adult, deal claw damage against a target at either side. It falls unless it rolls at or below Dexterity on 1d20.
Tail slap. From Adult, attack up to the age-tier number of targets at the rear and sides, rolling separately. Each hit deals twice claw damage, and the target saves vs. petrification at a penalty equal to the combat modifier or is stunned for 1d4 + 1 minutes. It can smash light wood or drain a cube of force by one charge per two points of combat modifier, rounded down.
Stall. Hover one round near the ground, then land. During the stall, the dragon can attack with all four legs and its bite, or breathe instead. Debris creates a dust cloud out to the fear radius for one round in suitable terrain. Anyone in it is blinded and cannot cast.
Optional plummet. From at least 30 feet above the target, land on up to the combat-modifier number of targets, rolling separately for bite damage. Each hit target saves vs. petrification at a penalty equal to the modifier or is pinned and takes the damage again on the next round if the dragon holds it down. It must save again to escape an ongoing pin. The dragon cannot do anything else while plummeting or holding the pin.

gm.title: Fear and spellcasting
lines:
From Young Adult, seeing it causes targets under 1 HD and nonaggressive noncarnivores below the dragon’s HD to panic for 4d6 rounds. Other creatures below its HD in a charging dragon’s fear radius or under its flight path at up to 250 feet altitude save vs. petrification with the listed modifier. Failure gives −2 to attack and damage. Creatures at least equal to its HD are immune.
Determine its spells from the age tier. A dragon generally casts each spell once per day or more if rolled more than once. Casting is verbal only with casting time 1. It cannot attack, breathe, use innate magic, or do more than glide while casting.

gm.title: Red Curse
lines: The first Legacy requires the dragon to drain at least 1 ounce of cinnabryl with its breath. Juvenile and older dragons are assumed to have 1d4 − 1 random Legacies for each age category from Juvenile onward. Duplicate Legacies stack if possible. Otherwise roll again. Add 1,000 XP per Legacy. A new Legacy costs no ability points. Physical changes appear over a few days, and the dragon can reverse them over the following week.

gm.title: Harvested scales
lines: One hide yields enough cinnabryl-bearing scales for at most one set of armor. A crimson essence alchemist must treat the scales into scale mail using at least one potion of crimson essence. It protects only the wearer. A slashing, piercing, or magical hit dealing more than 15 damage calls for an appropriate item saving throw. On failure the scales lose their protection in a smokepowder-like detonation.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: Choose an age tier before play. The printed Wyrm and Great Wyrm age ranges overlap.

The spell totals list slots by spell level. The appendix gives no direct HP damage for the cinnabryl breath. General dragon attacks, fear, and casting follow the Monstrous Manual, Dragons, General. THAC0 uses Dungeon Master Guide Table 39.
