gm.title: Description
lines: An elder brain lives in a brine pool at the heart of a mind flayer colony. It coordinates the colony and reaches other minds across great distances.

gm.title: Languages
lines: Understands Common, Deep Speech, and Undercommon. It communicates through telepathy with a range of 5 miles and cannot speak aloud.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Creature Sense. Detect creatures within 5 miles whose Intelligence is at least 4. The elder brain knows their direction, distance, and Intelligence score. Mind Blank, Nondetection, and similar magic defeat this sense.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). The elder brain can turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Magic Resistance. The elder brain has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Telepathic Hub. The elder brain can hold up to ten simultaneous telepathic conversations. It may let the connected creatures hear one another telepathically.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Tentacle. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. A hit deals 20 (4d8 + 2) bludgeoning damage. A creature of Huge size or smaller is grappled (escape DC 15) and takes 9 (1d8 + 5) psychic damage at the start of each of its turns until the grapple ends. The elder brain can grapple up to four targets.
Mind Blast (Recharge 5–6). Release magical psychic energy and choose creatures within 60 ft. Each must succeed on a DC 18 Intelligence save or take 32 (5d10 + 5) psychic damage and be stunned for 1 minute. A stunned target can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
Psychic Link. Link with one incapacitated creature detected by Creature Sense. The elder brain perceives what the target senses until the link ends. The target notices the link once it is no longer incapacitated. It can use an action on its turn to make a DC 18 Charisma save, breaking the link and taking 10 (3d6) psychic damage on a success. The brain can end the link without an action. Separation of more than 5 miles ends the link with no consequences for the target. The elder brain can maintain up to ten psychic links.
Sense Thoughts. Read a linked creature's reasoning, emotions, and foremost thoughts. The elder brain can plant a false belief or feeling by making a Charisma (Deception) check with advantage, contested by the target's Wisdom (Insight). If the elder brain wins, the target believes the deception for 1 hour or until presented with evidence of the lie.

gm.title: Innate spellcasting (psionics)
lines:
Use Intelligence (spell save DC 18). These spells require no components.
At will. Detect Thoughts, Levitate.
1/day each. Dominate Monster, Plane Shift (self only).

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
The elder brain has 3 legendary actions. It can spend one to use one option at the end of another creature's turn. Spent uses return at the start of its turn. It cannot use legendary actions while incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. If surprised, it must finish its first turn before using one.
Tentacle (1 action). Make one Tentacle attack.
Break Concentration (1 action). Choose a linked creature within 120 ft. End its concentration on a spell it cast. It takes 1d4 psychic damage per level of the spell.
Psychic Pulse (1 action). Choose a linked creature within 120 ft. Each enemy of the elder brain within 10 ft. of that target takes 10 (3d6) psychic damage.
Sever Psychic Link (1 action). End a psychic link with a creature within 120 ft. The creature has disadvantage on ability checks, attack rolls, and saving throws until the end of its next turn.

gm.title: Lair actions
lines:
While fighting in its lair, the elder brain can use one option at initiative count 20, losing ties. It cannot use the same option in consecutive rounds. It must be able to act. If surprised, it must finish its first turn before using a lair action.
Force Wall. Cast Wall of Force.
Psychic Inspiration. Pick a friendly creature the elder brain can sense within 120 ft. It gains advantage on one attack roll, ability check, or saving throw it makes by the end of its next turn. The benefit expires if unused.
Psionic Anchor. Pick a creature the elder brain can sense within 120 ft. On a failed DC 18 Charisma save, the target is unable to leave its current space. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:
Choose one or more effects around the lair. All end immediately when the elder brain dies.
Paranoia. Creatures within 5 miles feel that someone is following them.
Telepathic Eavesdropping. The elder brain can overhear any telepathic conversation within 5 miles. When contact first begins, the creature that initiated it makes a DC 18 Wisdom (Insight) check. A success reveals an eavesdropper without identifying it. The elder brain can join only if it has a psychic link with the initiator.
Psychic Whispers. Creatures linked to the elder brain hear faint, incomprehensible traces of its thoughts and the thoughts of others in the link.

gm.title: Description
lines: An elder brain takes control of a captive dragon and uses the host’s mobility to lead an illithid army. Its brine breath can turn victims into mind flayers.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Legendary Resistance (4/day). The dragon can turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Siege Monster. The dragon deals double damage to objects and structures.
Unusual Nature. The dragon needs neither air nor sleep.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite, two Claw attacks, and one Tentacle attack.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +15 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 19 (2d10 + 8) piercing damage plus 11 (2d10) psychic damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +15 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 11 (1d6 + 8) slashing damage.
Tentacle. Melee weapon attack, +15 to hit, reach 15 ft., one creature. A hit deals 12 (1d8 + 8) psychic damage. A Huge or smaller target is also grappled (escape DC 18). The dragon can grapple up to four creatures with its tentacles at once.
Tadpole Brine Breath (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in a line 120 ft. long and 15 ft. wide makes a DC 22 Constitution save. Failure deals 55 (10d10) psychic damage. Success halves the damage. Either result infests the creature with illithid tadpoles unless it is a Construct or an Undead.
Infestation. An infested creature starts each of its turns by taking 16 (3d10) psychic damage. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, clearing the infestation after three successes. Magic that ends a curse or restores at least 40 hit points to the creature kills the tadpoles and ends the infestation immediately.
Ceremorphosis. If an infested Humanoid drops to 0 hit points, it is stable and remains unconscious for 6d12 hours. It then becomes a Mind Flayer with full hit points. Casting Wish on it while unconscious ends the infestation and prevents the transformation.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
The dragon has three legendary actions and regains spent actions at the start of its turn. It can use one option at the end of another creature’s turn.
Tentacle (1 action). Make one Tentacle attack.
Shatter Concentration (2 actions). Choose a creature the dragon has grappled. Its concentration on a spell or ability ends, and it takes 19 (3d12) psychic damage.

gm.title: Description
lines: An oblex steals memories and uses them to imitate people. Its doubles can pass for their originals, apart from a faint sulfur smell.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Amorphous. The oblex can move through a gap as narrow as 1 inch without squeezing.
Aversion to Fire. After taking fire damage, it has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks until the end of its next turn.
Unusual Nature. The oblex does not need sleep.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Pseudopod attacks and use Eat Memories.
Pseudopod. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 17 (4d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage plus 14 (4d6) psychic damage.
Eat Memories. Choose one visible creature within 5 ft. It makes a DC 18 Wisdom save. Constructs, Oozes, Plants, and Undead succeed automatically. On a failure, the target takes 44 (8d10) psychic damage and is memory drained. A short or long rest, Greater Restoration, or Heal ends the drain. While drained, the target subtracts a d4 roll from each ability check and attack roll. Each further drain increases the die by one size through d6, d8, d10, d12, then d20. When the die reaches d20, the target falls unconscious for 1 hour, then the effect ends. The oblex learns all the drained creature’s languages and gains all its skill proficiencies.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
Spellcasting (Psionics). As an action, cast one listed spell using Intelligence (spell save DC 18). No components are required.
At will. Charm Person (cast at 5th level), Detect Thoughts.
3/day each. Dimension Door, Dominate Person, Hypnotic Pattern, Telekinesis.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines: Sulfurous Impersonation. Form a double of a Medium or smaller creature whose memories the oblex stole. The double looks, sounds, and feels like the original but smells faintly of sulfur. The oblex can imitate 2d6 + 1 different creatures. Each double is part of the oblex, which occupies both its own space and the double’s space. A strand up to 120 ft. long connects each double to the body. The strand is immune to damage. The strand severs if no opening at least 1 inch wide connects the double and the body. The double then disappears.

gm.title: Condition immunities

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Air Form. The tempest can enter and stop in a hostile creature’s space. It can move through a gap as narrow as 1 inch without squeezing.
Flyby. Flying out of an enemy’s reach provokes no opportunity attack.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). When the tempest fails a saving throw, it can succeed instead.
Living Storm. A storm 1d6 + 4 miles across stays centered on the tempest. Heavy rain or snow lightly obscures the area. Heavy rain puts out open flames and imposes disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing. Strong winds throughout the storm impose disadvantage on ranged attack rolls, put out open flames, and disperse fog.
Siege Monster. The tempest deals double damage to objects and structures.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Thunderous Slam attacks.
Thunderous Slam. Melee weapon attack, +16 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 23 (4d6 + 9) thunder damage.
Lightning Storm (Recharge 6). Each creature within 120 ft. makes a DC 21 Dexterity save, taking 27 (6d8) lightning damage on a failure or half on a success. A creature that fails by 5 or more is also stunned until the end of its next turn.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
The tempest has 3 legendary actions. Spend the listed cost immediately after another creature’s turn. It regains spent actions at the start of its turn. It can use these actions only when able to act. If surprised, it must finish its first turn before using one.
Move (1 action). Move up to its speed.
Lightning Strike (2 actions). Strike a point on the ground anywhere under the storm. Each creature within 5 ft. of that point makes a DC 21 Dexterity save, taking 16 (3d10) lightning damage on a failure or half on a success.
Screaming Gale (3 actions). Blast a 300-ft. line, 20 ft. wide. Objects in the line take 22 (4d10) thunder damage. Each creature in the line makes a DC 21 Dexterity save. On a failure, it takes 22 (4d10) thunder damage and is thrown up to 60 ft. away from the line. Hitting an immovable object or another creature deals the thrown creature 3 (1d6) bludgeoning damage for every 10 ft. traveled before impact. A creature struck by the thrown creature makes a DC 19 Dexterity save. On a failure, it takes the same impact damage and falls prone.

lines: A titan of the Elemental Chaos. It moves through earth, air, and water and can set off a different disaster each time it attacks with Cataclysmic Event.

gm.title: Damage immunities
lines: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Poison, Thunder.

gm.title: Condition immunities
lines: Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Exhaustion, Frightened, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained, Stunned, Unconscious.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Earth Glide. The cataclysm can burrow through unworked, nonmagical earth and stone without disturbing the material.
Legendary Resistance (4/day). On a failed saving throw, the cataclysm can spend one use to succeed.
Siege Monster. The cataclysm deals double damage to objects and structures.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Elemental Burst attacks.
Elemental Burst. Melee or ranged attack, +15 to hit, reach 30 ft. or range 150 ft. A hit deals 25 (5d6 + 8) damage. The cataclysm chooses Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder for that hit.
Control Weather. Cast Control Weather using Constitution and no spell components.
Cataclysmic Event (recharge 4–6). Roll 1d4 for one effect.
1. Clinging Flames. Center a 60-ft.-radius sphere on a visible point within 150 ft. Each creature inside makes a DC 23 Dexterity save. Failure deals 45 (13d6) Fire damage. Success halves the damage. The creature starts Burning either way.
2. Freezing Waves. Each creature in a 90-ft. cone makes a DC 23 Strength save. Failure deals 22 (5d8) Bludgeoning plus 22 (5d8) Cold damage and knocks it Prone. Success halves the damage and avoids the fall. Either way, the creature's Speed becomes 0 until the end of its next turn.
3. Raging Storm. Center a 60-ft.-radius sphere of storm cloud on a visible point within 150 ft. It lasts for 1 minute or until the cataclysm uses Cataclysmic Event again. Creatures wholly inside are Blinded and Deafened and cannot cast spells with Verbal components. A creature that first enters the cloud on a turn or starts its turn there makes a DC 23 Dexterity save. Failure deals 18 (4d8) Lightning plus 18 (4d8) Thunder damage. Success halves the damage.
4. Swallowing Earth. Choose a point on the ground within 150 ft. Each creature in a 90-ft. cube originating there makes a DC 23 Strength save. Failure deals 18 (4d8) Bludgeoning plus 18 (4d8) Acid damage, knocks it Prone, and buries it under rubble. Success halves the damage and avoids the fall and burial. A buried creature is Restrained and suffocating and has Total Cover. The buried creature or another creature within 5 ft. of it can take an action to free it with a successful DC 18 Strength (Athletics) check.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
3 uses. Spend one immediately after another creature's turn to select one option. The cataclysm recovers spent uses at the start of its turn and cannot use them while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act.
Eruption. Make one Elemental Burst attack.
Rumbling Movement. Move up to the cataclysm's Speed, Fly Speed, or Swim Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks. Each creature it comes within 5 ft. of during the move makes one DC 23 Constitution save or falls Prone. The cataclysm cannot use this option again until the start of its next turn.

gm.title: Description
lines: An elemental lich fights up close to channel Ravenloft’s fire, mist, grave earth and blood. Its phylactery lies hidden beneath a mist-shrouded grave.

gm.title: Classification
lines: Medium undead (augmented humanoid), 10th-level human wizard example

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack or full attack. Touch +5 melee (see powers below), dagger +5 melee for 1d4/19–20, or dart +3 ranged for 1d4/×2. The touch and other natural weapons count as magical.
Conjure Dread Elemental (Su). Each day it may call one 8 HD blood, grave, mist and pyre elemental. Each serves willingly.
Fear Aura (Su). A creature under 5 HD that looks at it within 60 ft. must make a DC 18 Will save against fear. Success gives immunity to this aura for 24 hours. Caster level equals the lich's level.
Touch of Blood (Su). A hit deals 1d8 + 5 HP damage. DC 18 Fortitude or permanent paralysis and 1d4 damage each round. Remove paralysis or curse removal ends paralysis. DC 20 Spot or DC 15 Heal reveals the paralyzed victim is alive.
Touch of the Grave (Su). DC 18 Fortitude. Success means 1d8 + 5 HP damage. Failure means death unless heal is cast on the victim within one round.
Touch of the Pyre (Su). Hit for 1d10 damage, then clothing and armor save or ignite. The magic fire deals 1d10 each round until dispelled or the victim is burned to ash, typically within 1d4 rounds.
Touch of Mist (Su). No HP damage. DC 18 Will or the victim becomes chaotic evil and serves the lich, which can contact it telepathically up to 10 miles away. Remove curse cast by someone of the victim’s former alignment frees it and restores that alignment.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Sample DR 15/bludgeoning and magic. Immune to elemental attacks, electricity, involuntary polymorph, and mind-affecting effects. Undead traits and +3 turn resistance. It cannot control undead.

gm.title: Combat statistics
lines: Initiative +6. AC +2 Dex, +5 natural, +3 bracers, +2 protection ring. Touch 17, flat-footed 10 as printed. BAB/grapple +5/+5, space/reach 5 ft./5 ft., Fort +3, Ref +5, Will +11.

gm.title: Spells prepared
lines: DC 15 + spell level. 0: detect magic, flare, ray of frost, read magic. 1st: burning hands, chill touch, comprehend languages, expeditious retreat, magic missile, true strike. 2nd: continual flame, flaming sphere, fog cloud, gust of wind, whispering wind. 3rd: dispel magic, explosive runes, fireball, slow. 4th: fire trap, remove curse, wall of fire, wall of ice. 5th: cone of cold, passwall.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Concentration +15, Decipher Script +10, Hide +18, Knowledge (arcana) +15, Knowledge (engineering) +10, Listen +18, Move Silently +26, Spellcraft +15, Spot +12. Combat Casting, Craft Wondrous Item, Improved Initiative, Scribe Scroll, Still Spell, Toughness.

gm.title: Phylactery encounter
lines: The lich buries its phylactery in a grave near the lair, where a rite calls mist over the site. Approaching creatures make a DC 18 Will save or wander away in confusion. Digging above it alerts the lich, which usually arrives in 1d10 rounds.

gm.title: Applying the encounter template
lines: Use a humanoid able to create the phylactery. Type becomes undead; keep size, BAB, saves and skill points. HD becomes d12, natural AC becomes +5 or remains higher, and Int, Wis and Cha increase by 2. Add one touch per round and the listed powers. Add +8 racial on Hide, Listen, Move Silently, Search, Sense Motive and Spot. CR increases by 2; save DC is 10 + half HD + Cha modifier. The sample carries +3 bracers, potions of invisibility and gaseous form, and a brooch of shielding.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: Roll 10d12 + 3 because the sample does not print a fixed HP total. Keep sample touch and flat-footed AC despite the printed breakdown. The sample’s DR includes magic, but the template lists only bludgeoning. Pyre does not specify the item save category.

lines: Elok seized command of the Dragonfang in a mutiny. He now wants the pirate captains to stop paying Fort Beluarian and has support among their crews.

lines: AC 10 in human form. AC 11 from natural armor in boar and hybrid forms.

gm.title: Description

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Fledgling sample, 5th-level elf ranger. Initiative +12. Touch AC 18, flat-footed AC 15. BAB +5, grapple +9. Space and reach 5 ft. Fort +5, Ref +12, Will +5.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack or full attack. Choose slam +9 melee (1d6 + 4 and 1d4 Charisma drain to a living creature), +1 longsword +10 melee (1d8 + 4, 18–20), or +1 mighty composite longbow +14 ranged (1d8 + 4, ×3). A target below Charisma 3 gains the book’s lost-one madness effect. At Charisma 0 or less the victim dies within 2d6 hours.
Wretched Gaze (Su). Anyone within 30 ft. who sees its face makes a DC 11 Will Horror save or freezes. The victim is flat-footed and unable to act until 1d4 rounds after losing sight of its face.
Black Thumb (Su). A plant touched by its bare skin makes a DC 11 Fortitude save or takes 1d4 HP damage per minute until it dies. This cannot be suppressed. Destroying the vampire ends the effect.
Spell-like abilities. At caster level 12, 3/day each entangle, snare, spike growth and warp wood. 1/day each antilife shell, giant vermin and wall of thorns. Save DC 9 + spell level.
Children of the Night (Su, 1/day). Call 5d10 hawks, 3d10 eagles, 3d6 wolves, or 6d10 HD of Tiny or Diminutive mammals. They arrive in 2d6 rounds and serve up to 1 hour.

gm.title: Traits
lines: DR 10/cold iron and magic, cold and electricity resistance 20, turn resistance +2, fast healing 4, undead traits, favored enemy (goblinoids +2, elves +1), Track. Plantwalk uses tree stride at will as a standard action and exposes both trees to Black Thumb. Alternate Form uses an eagle or giant eagle. As a standard action assume the listed animal form. Lose the slam and domination, gain the animal’s natural weapons and extraordinary attacks, and retain this form until the next sunrise or another change.

gm.title: Spawn
lines: An elf or half-elf who dies from the madness caused by the drain rises as spawn 1d4 days after burial. A victim killed by draining Charisma to 0 or less rises as spawn at 4 HD or fewer and as an elven vampire at 5 HD or more. The creator controls them until it dies. Elven spawn retain 1d4 Charisma drain, Plantwalk, 2 HP fast healing, DC 14 Horror gaze, and DC 14 Black Thumb limited to 10 rounds.

gm.title: Repelling and slaying
lines: An unbroken line of fragrant petals plucked within 1 day stops it. Music forces a Will save matching the Perform check or it stops to listen, with another save each minute. An attack ends the effect. Underground it takes 1d4 damage per round and loses fast healing and supernatural and spell-like powers. Between sunset and sunrise it must be in its coffin or can take only standard actions before being destroyed on the next round. Running water has no power over it. Fresh sap burns like holy water. A charcoal stake kills it while left through its heart. For permanent destruction, the book has its severed head burned with flowers and flowering shrubs for at least 24 hours. At 0 HP it retreats via Plantwalk and is destroyed if caught outside a tree for more than 2 consecutive rounds before reaching its coffin. After 1 hour in the coffin it reaches 1 HP and resumes healing.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Bluff +10, Hide +20, Handle Animal +7, Knowledge (nature) +9, Listen +15, Move Silently +20, Search +11, Sense Motive +11, Spot +15, Survival +11. Alertness, Combat Reflexes, Dodge, Improved Initiative, Lightning Reflexes, Point-Blank Shot, Precise Shot.

gm.title: Encounter adaptation
lines: Apply the strain to the 3.5 vampire template. Retain unmodified abilities, size, BAB, saves and skill points. The base vampire uses undead d12 Hit Dice and has no Constitution score. Keep an existing swim speed and ignore vulnerability to immersion in running water if the base creature can swim. Use save DC 10 + half HD rounded down + Charisma modifier unless specified. Age rows replace one another. Apply only to an elf. Age DR requires cold iron and magic. The Outcast Rating (OR) adjustment applies when dealing with non-elven vampires.

gm.title: Age modifiers
lines:
Apply one row to a base creature. The sample already includes its adjustments. Ability scores are listed in Str, Dex, Int, Wis, Cha order.
Fledgling. Abilities 4/8/2/4/0. Speed +0 ft., natural AC +4, turn resistance +2, CR +2. DR 10, fast healing 4, OR +2.
Mature. Abilities 4/10/4/4/0. Speed +10 ft., natural AC +4, turn resistance +2, CR +2. DR 15, fast healing 4, OR +2.

gm.title: Description
lines: An emerald dragon whose crystalline form and vast psionic reach reflect centuries of merging with its echoes. Smargad is the emerald thane named in the book’s sidebar on Sardior.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Gem Awakening (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest). When the greatwyrm would drop to 0 hit points, it instead resets to 400 hit points, recharges Breath Weapon and recovers all spent Legendary Resistance uses. It can use Mass Telekinesis for the next hour. Defeating it after Gem Awakening grants an extra 90,000 XP, for 180,000 XP total.
Legendary Resistance (4/day). The greatwyrm can turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Unusual Nature. The greatwyrm needs no food or drink.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +17 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 20 (2d10 + 9) piercing damage plus 16 (3d10) force damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +17 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 18 (2d8 + 9) slashing damage. A Huge or smaller creature hit is grappled (escape DC 19) and restrained while grappled. The greatwyrm can hold only one creature with its Claw.
Breath Weapon (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 300-ft. cone makes a DC 25 Dexterity save. A failure deals 71 (11d12) force damage and knocks the creature prone. Success halves the damage and prevents the knockdown. On either result its speed becomes 0 until the end of its next turn.
Mass Telekinesis (Gem Awakening Only, Recharges after a Short or Long Rest). Choose any number of visible creatures or objects within 120 ft., each weighing up to 4,000 lb. Worn or carried objects are ineligible. Each chosen creature must pass a DC 26 Strength save or be restrained by the grip. It can repeat this save at the end of each of its turns to escape. At the end of each of the greatwyrm’s turns, it can move each creature or object still in the grip up to 60 ft. in any direction, within 120 ft. of itself. It can also deal 45 (7d12) force damage to each creature it chooses that remains restrained by the grip.
Spellcasting (Psionics). As an action, cast a listed spell using Intelligence (spell save DC 26, +18 to hit with spell attacks) and no components. Dispel Magic, Forcecage, Plane Shift, Reverse Gravity, and Time Stop are each usable once per day.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines:
Change Shape. Magically take the shape of a Small or Medium creature. The greatwyrm retains its game statistics apart from size. The change ends at 0 hit points or when the greatwyrm spends a bonus action to end it.
Psychic Step. Magically teleport to a visible unoccupied space within 60 ft.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
The greatwyrm has three legendary actions and regains spent actions at the start of its turn. Use one option at a time at the end of another creature’s turn.
Claw (1 action). Make one Claw attack.
Psionics (2 actions). Use Psychic Step or Spellcasting.
Psychic Beam (3 actions). Each creature in a line 90 ft. long and 10 ft. wide makes a DC 26 Intelligence save. Failure deals 27 (5d10) psychic damage. Success halves the damage.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Legendary Resistance (3/Day). If the tarrasque fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead. Magic Resistance. The tarrasque has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects. Reflective Carapace. Any time the tarrasque is targeted by a magic missile spell, a line spell, or a spell that requires a ranged attack roll, roll a d6. On a 1 to 5, the tarrasque is unaffected. On a 6, the tarrasque is unaffected, and the effect is reflected back at the caster as though it originated from the tarrasque, turning the caster into the target. Siege Monster. The tarrasque deals double damage to objects and structures.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Multiattack. The tarrasque can use its Frightful Presence. It then makes five attacks: one with its bite, two with its claws, one with its horns, and one with its tail. It can use its Swallow instead of its bite. Bite. Melee Weapon Attack: +19 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 36 (4d12 + 10) piercing damage. If the target is a creature, it is grappled (escape DC 20). Until this grapple ends, the target is restrained, and the tarrasque can’t bite another target. Claw. Melee Weapon Attack: +19 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 28 (4d8 + 10) slashing damage. Horns. Melee Weapon Attack: +19 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 32 (4d10 + 10) piercing damage. Tail. Melee Weapon Attack: +19 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. Hit: 24 (4d6 + 10) bludgeoning damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 20 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone. Frightful Presence. Each creature of the tarrasque’s choice within 120 feet of it and aware of it must succeed on a DC 17 Wisdom saving throw or become frightened for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, with disadvantage if the tarrasque is within line of sight, ending the effect on itself on a success. If a creature’s saving throw is successful or the effect ends for it, the creature is immune to the tarrasque’s Frightful Presence for the next 24 hours. Swallow. The tarrasque makes one bite attack against a Large or smaller creature it is grappling. If the attack hits, the target takes the bite’s damage, the target is swallowed, and the grapple ends. While swallowed, the creature is blinded and restrained, it has total cover against attacks and other effects outside the tarrasque, and it takes 56 (16d6) acid damage at the start of each of the tarrasque’s turns. If the tarrasque takes 60 damage or more on a single turn from a creature inside it, the tarrasque must succeed on a DC 20 Constitution saving throw at the end of that turn or regurgitate all swallowed creatures, which fall prone in a space within 10 feet of the tarrasque. If the tarrasque dies, a swallowed creature is no longer restrained by it and can escape from the corpse by using 30 feet of movement, exiting prone.

gm.title: Legendary Actions
lines: The tarrasque can take 3 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature’s turn. The tarrasque regains spent legendary actions at the start of its turn. Attack. The tarrasque makes one claw attack or tail attack. Move. The tarrasque moves up to half its speed. Chomp (Costs 2 Actions). The tarrasque makes one bite attack or uses its Swallow.

gm.title: Description
lines: The youngest Hourglass Coven hag rules Yon from her mountaintop theater. She shows visitors terrible futures in exchange for a piece of their free will and believes she will die during a solar eclipse.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Boon of Immortality. Endelyn cannot age through any effect or die of old age.
Eclipsed Doom. Endelyn dies at 0 hit points only during a solar eclipse or within 60 ft. of a symbolic solar eclipse. Otherwise, at 0 hit points she vanishes in inky smoke with all worn and carried items, then returns 24 hours later at the same spot or the nearest open space.
Uncanny Awareness. Endelyn cannot be surprised.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Puppeteer’s Lash attacks.
Puppeteer’s Lash. Melee or ranged spell attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft., one creature. On a hit, deal 17 (4d6 + 3) psychic damage. If the target is Large or smaller, Endelyn telekinetically moves it up to 10 ft. in any horizontal direction.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
As an action, cast one listed spell with Charisma (save DC 14) and no material components.
At will. Detect Magic, Mage Hand.
2/day each. Augury, Polymorph.
1/day. Plane Shift (self only).

gm.title: Hourglass Coven
lines: While Endelyn, Bavlorna Blightstraw, and Skabatha Nightshade are all within 30 ft. of one another, any of them can spend an action to cast Detect Thoughts, Dispel Magic, Finger of Death, Glibness, Locate Creature, or Mass Suggestion without material components (save DC 14). Each spell has one shared use until the next dawn.

gm.title: Motherhorn
lines: Glister of the Selenelion Twin act can stage a symbolic eclipse by standing behind the theater’s wooden moon prop while wearing her sun mask. The twins can also embody the sun and moon together. When threatened, Endelyn can flee on her Ornithopter of Flying. If the coven has regrouped and risks capture or death, the hags flee for the Palace of Heart’s Desire.

gm.title: Orrery of Tragedies (M14)
lines:
Creatures on the balcony and on the floor below have three-quarters cover against attacks from the other level. Touching the central lightning rod, entering the device’s space for the first time on a turn, or starting a turn there triggers a DC 15 Dexterity save. Take 44 (8d10) lightning damage on a failed save or half on a success. Make the save with disadvantage in metal armor.
At least eight components must be destroyed to wreck the device. Each is a Large object with AC 19, 27 HP, and immunity to lightning, poison, and psychic damage. The central rod has eight segments, each AC 17 and 25 HP with the same immunities. Destroying a segment drops the ones above it. If at least three are lost, the orrery shuts down after 1 minute until the rod is rebuilt. Antimagic Field suppresses the device while in contact. Dispel Magic (DC 19) shuts it down for 1 minute, but it stays charged.

lines: Three treants defend Eoghan if he is attacked. gm.title: Delerium contamination
lines:
Printed source. Appendix C, pp. 222–223.
Add contamination levels from each exposure. A contaminated character rolls 1d20 at the end of each long rest and gains one level on a 1.
Symptoms are cumulative. Level 1 has no symptom. Level 2 halves healing from Hit Dice. Level 3 prevents HP recovery from a long rest. Level 4 halves damage the creature deals with weapon attacks and spells. Level 5 makes it Incapacitated. Level 6 triggers Monstrous Transformation.
After a character gains a level, roll 1d6. On a result at or below the current level, the GM chooses a new mutation or rolls on the printed mutations table. Replace or reroll duplicate mutations.
Contamination does not wear off. Purge Contamination can remove levels and causes Exhaustion. Heal removes all contamination and mutations. Each level removed also removes one random mutation. At level 0, all symptoms and mutations end.
A contaminated humanoid rises as a Haze Husk 24 hours after death. It rises as a Haze Wight if it had at least six class levels or Hit Dice. Raising a creature from the dead reduces its contamination by one level.
Monstrous Transformation. At level 6 or higher, the creature transforms after one round. Replace its statistics, hit points, and Hit Dice with those of a monster the GM chooses. Contamination resets to 0, and the GM controls the transformed creature.
Wish or similar magic can restore one transformed creature, clearing its madness and contamination. Using Wish this way gives the caster a 33 percent chance of losing the ability to cast it again.

gm.title: Description
lines: An organic warship grown by a Reigar, usually resembling a vast jellyfish or cephalopod. Without its creator, its actions are driven by self-preservation.

gm.title: Condition immunities
lines: Blinded, charmed, deafened, exhaustion, frightened, petrified, prone.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Bioluminescence. With at least 1 HP, the esthetic lights the area within 30 ft. brightly and the next 30 ft. dimly. Its compartments have dim light.
Spelljamming. The esthetic has the properties of a Spelljamming Helm. Its Reigar creator is the only creature that can attune to it.
Unusual Nature. The esthetic needs no air, food, or drink.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Tentacle attacks.
Tentacle. Melee weapon attack, +11 to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. A hit deals 17 (3d6 + 7) force damage. A creature hit is grappled (escape DC 17) and takes 18 (4d8) acid damage at the start of each of its turns while held. The esthetic has 1d4 × 2 tentacles. Each can grapple one target and cannot attack a different target until it releases the creature.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines: Jammerscream (recharge 6). Choose one spelljamming ship within 300 ft. If it has several helms, randomly select one. Its helm’s magic shuts down for 2d10 days unless a creature attuned to it opts to make a DC 17 Charisma save. On a failed save, that creature takes 42 (12d6) psychic damage and the shutdown lasts 2d10 hours. On a successful save, the creature takes half damage and the shutdown lasts 2d10 minutes.

gm.title: Passengers and creator
lines: There is room for the Reigar and up to six Medium passengers. The Reigar can open or close the hatch by touching it. The esthetic can live indefinitely on the Astral Plane while its creator lives. If its creator dies, the esthetic sickens and dies after 1d12 days.

Bite. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing plus 4 (1d8) poison damage. The target makes a DC 11 Constitution save. On failure it is Poisoned for 1 minute. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the condition on a success.
Web Garrote. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. The target must be a Small or Medium creature against which the ettercap has advantage on the attack. Hit 4 (1d4 + 2) bludgeoning damage and the target is Grappled (escape DC 12). While grappled this way, the target cannot breathe and the ettercap has advantage on attacks against it.
Web (Recharge 5–6). Ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, range 30/60 ft., one Large or smaller creature. On a hit, the target is Restrained. The target can spend an action on a DC 11 Strength check to break free. Destroying the web also frees it. The web has AC 10 and 5 HP. It is vulnerable to fire and immune to bludgeoning, poison, and psychic damage.

gm.title: Legendary Actions
lines:
Three legendary actions per round. Use one option after another creature's turn and recover spent actions at the start of this creature's turn.
Lumber Forward (2 actions). Move up to half speed.
Attack (2 actions). Make a melee or ranged Guillotine Blade attack.
Summon Shadows (3 actions). Up to six visible humanoid corpses within 60 ft. that died violently each produce a shadow in their space or the nearest empty one. They obey the Executioner and act after it on the same initiative count. They disappear after 1 minute or if the Executioner is destroyed, and can be destroyed earlier.

gm.title: Delerium contamination
lines:
Printed source. Appendix C, pp. 222–223.
Add contamination levels from each exposure. A contaminated character rolls 1d20 at the end of each long rest and gains one level on a 1.
Symptoms are cumulative. Level 1 has no symptom. Level 2 halves healing from Hit Dice. Level 3 prevents HP recovery from a long rest. Level 4 halves damage the creature deals with weapon attacks and spells. Level 5 makes it Incapacitated. Level 6 triggers Monstrous Transformation.
After a character gains a level, roll 1d6. On a result at or below the current level, the GM chooses a new mutation or rolls on the printed mutations table. Replace or reroll duplicate mutations.
Contamination does not wear off. Purge Contamination can remove levels and causes Exhaustion. Heal removes all contamination and mutations. Each level removed also removes one random mutation. At level 0, all symptoms and mutations end.
A contaminated humanoid rises as a Haze Husk 24 hours after death. It rises as a Haze Wight if it had at least six class levels or Hit Dice. Raising a creature from the dead reduces its contamination by one level.
Monstrous Transformation. At level 6 or higher, the creature transforms after one round. Replace its statistics, hit points, and Hit Dice with those of a monster the GM chooses. Contamination resets to 0, and the GM controls the transformed creature.
Wish or similar magic can restore one transformed creature, clearing its madness and contamination. Using Wish this way gives the caster a 33 percent chance of losing the ability to cast it again.

gm.title: Description
lines: With mouth and eye shut, this ambusher resembles a twelve-foot asteroid. It opens its eye when it senses vibrations. Coins, metal weapons, gems, and magic items can remain in the gullet after a meal.

gm.title: Senses
lines: Darkvision 120 ft., blindsight 120 ft. while the eye monger's eye is closed.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Antimagic Gullet. The gullet suppresses magic, including spells and magic items. Magic from artifacts or deities is exempt. Slots or item charges spent inside on suppressed magic are wasted. Suppression counts against an effect’s duration. Outside magic cannot affect creatures or objects inside unless it comes from an artifact or deity.
False Appearance. If it starts combat motionless with both mouth and eye closed, it has advantage on initiative. A creature that has never seen it move or act needs a successful DC 18 Intelligence (Investigation) check to recognize it as animate.
Unusual Nature. The eye monger needs no air.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 12 (2d6 + 5) piercing damage. A Medium or smaller creature hit must pass a DC 18 Dexterity save or be swallowed into the antimagic gullet. The eye monger can hold one swallowed creature at a time.
A swallowed creature is blinded and restrained. It has total cover from attacks and other effects originating outside the eye monger. It takes 35 (10d6) acid damage at the start of each of its own turns.
If a creature in the gullet deals at least 25 damage to the eye monger in one turn, the monster regurgitates it. The creature lands prone within 10 ft. If the eye monger dies, the swallowed creature is freed from restraint and can spend 10 ft. of movement to exit prone.

gm.title: Printing note
lines: The updated printing uses blindsight while the eye is closed. The original printing listed tremorsense.

gm.title: Description
lines: A beholder’s dreams of a dragon rival can give rise to this limbless flying aberration. A large eye in its mouth projects antimagic, and the eyestalks in its wings fire rays.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Unusual Nature. The eyedrake needs no food or drink.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 13 (3d6 + 3) piercing damage.
Antimagic Breath (Recharge 6). Each creature in a 30-ft. cone makes a DC 14 Constitution save. Failure deals 39 (6d12) force damage. Success halves the damage. Every spell of 3rd level or lower ends on creatures or objects of the eyedrake’s choice in the cone.
Eye Rays. Roll three different rays at random, rerolling duplicates. For each ray, choose one creature the eyedrake can see within 60 ft.
1. Freezing Ray. DC 14 Constitution save. On a failure, take 17 (5d6) cold damage and halve speed until the end of the target’s next turn. Success halves the damage without reducing speed.
2. Debilitating Ray. DC 14 Constitution save. On a failure, take 7 (2d6) thunder damage and become incapacitated until the end of the target’s next turn.
3. Repulsion Ray. DC 14 Strength save. On a failure, take 14 (4d6) force damage and be pushed up to 60 ft. away from the eyedrake.
4. Fire Ray. DC 14 Dexterity save. On a failure, take 21 (6d6) fire damage. Success halves the damage.
5. Paralyzing Ray. DC 14 Constitution save. On a failure, become paralyzed for 1 minute. The target can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
6. Death Ray. DC 14 Dexterity save. On a failure, take 28 (8d6) necrotic damage. Success halves the damage. The target dies if the ray reduces it to 0 hit points.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A gigantic burrowing stalk tipped with a single red eye.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Saves Con +11, Wis +4. Senses: blindsight 30 ft., tremorsense 60 ft.. No languages. Passive Perception 9.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Tunneler. Burrowing through solid rock costs twice as much movement, and leaves a tunnel 10 ft. wide.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Use Bite once and use Eradication Gaze when available.
Bite. Melee weapon attack +14, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 22 (3d8 + 9) piercing. A Large or smaller creature must pass a DC 19 Dexterity save or be swallowed. Inside, it is Blinded and Restrained and has Total Cover against attacks and effects from outside. At the start of each eyestalk turn it takes 21 (6d6) acid damage. When one creature inside deals at least 30 damage on a turn, the eyestalk must pass a DC 21 Constitution save at that turn's end or vomit all swallowed creatures out Prone within 10 ft. If the eyestalk dies, swallowed creatures are no longer Restrained by it and can spend 20 ft. of movement to exit Prone.
Eradication Gaze (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 150-ft. cone makes a DC 16 Dexterity save. Failure deals 55 (10d10) necrotic damage. A creature reduced to 0 HP by that damage turns into fine violet dust.

gm.title: Description
lines: A fleshy mass disguised as algae or seaweed. Its feelers look like stalks with eyes until the mouths at their tips open.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Aquatic, usually along coasts or in rivers. Rare, solitary, active at any time. Carnivore. Intelligence 1. No treasure or magic resistance. Neutral. Appearing 1. Body 10 feet across. Steady morale 11–12.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Feelers. Attack with 2d4 feelers, each dealing 1d3 damage on a hit. They can extend up to 100 feet to find and bite prey. Eyeweed hunts by touch and smell.

gm.title: Defenses
lines: Each feeler takes 6 damage to sever. Damage to a feeler does not reduce the plant’s HP. Kill the central body to destroy the eyeweed. Lost feelers grow back in a week.

gm.title: Description
lines: A green, blue, indigo, or violet faerie dragon. These older butterfly-winged dragons build on the magic they learned in earlier colors.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A cat-sized dragon with butterfly wings. Older forms range from green through blue and indigo to violet.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Arcana +4, Perception +3, Stealth +7. Darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 13. Draconic and Sylvan.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Superior Invisibility. As a bonus action, the dragon can turn itself and its worn or carried gear Invisible. It maintains Concentration as it would on a spell. The effect ends when its concentration ends.
Limited Telepathy. The dragon can communicate magically with any other faerie dragon within 60 ft.
Magic Resistance. The dragon has advantage on saves against spells and other magic.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
Innate Spellcasting. Charisma is the spellcasting ability (save DC 13). The dragon needs no material components. Each color adds its spells to those of all younger colors.
Red (5 years or less), 1/day each. Dancing Lights, Mage Hand, Minor Illusion.
Orange (6–10 years), 1/day. Color Spray.
Yellow (11–20 years), 1/day. Mirror Image.
Green (21–30 years), 1/day. Suggestion.
Blue (31–40 years), 1/day. Major Image.
Indigo (41–50 years), 1/day. Hallucinatory Terrain.
Violet (51 years or more), 1/day. Polymorph.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit 1 piercing damage.
Euphoria Breath (Recharge 5–6). Exhale a puff of gas at one creature within 5 ft. It must succeed on a DC 11 Wisdom save or lose its reactions for 1 minute. At the start of each affected turn, roll 1d6. On 1–4, it takes no action or bonus action and spends all its movement moving in a random direction. On 5–6, it stays put and can only repeat the DC 11 Wisdom save, ending the effect on a success.

gm.title: Variant rules
lines: Superior Invisibility is a bonus action and requires Concentration. Worn and carried gear also becomes Invisible.

Euphoria Breath (Recharge 5–6) targets one creature within 5 ft. It must pass a DC 11 Wisdom save or lose reactions for 1 minute. At each turn start roll a d6. On 1–4 it takes no action or bonus action and uses all its movement in a random direction. On 5–6 it stays still and can only repeat the save to end the effect.

gm.title: Faerie Dragon Color and Age
lines: Age by color. Red up to 5 years, orange 6–10, yellow 11–20, green 21–30, blue 31–40, indigo 41–50, and violet 51 or more.

Each spell is usable once per day. Red gains Dancing Lights, Mage Hand and Minor Illusion. Orange adds Color Spray and yellow adds Mirror Image. Green adds Suggestion, blue Major Image, indigo Hallucinatory Terrain and violet Polymorph. Each color keeps all spells of younger colors.
Red through yellow are CR 1. Green through violet are CR 2. Innate spell save DC 13.

gm.title: Description
lines: Far traders sail the Astral Sea to sell luxury goods and magic-infused stones. Their hidden home port is the black-rock city of Far Spire.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Studded leather. Perception 15, Stealth 12. Vulnerable to radiant damage and resistant to necrotic damage. Darkvision 120 ft. Speaks all languages.

gm.title: Ability modifiers
lines: Str +1, Dex +2, Con +4, Int +3, Wis +5, Cha +6

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Astral Seafarer. Proficient with airships and waterborne vessels. Add its proficiency bonus to checks to control such a vessel and grant advantage on saves made aboard.
Ethereal Sight. See 60 ft. across the boundary between the Material and Ethereal Planes from either side.
Far Traveler. Advantage on saves against environmental dangers such as Void terrain and infernal gases.
Phrenic Weapons. Its weapon attacks are magical and add 2d4 psychic damage on a hit, included below.
Regeneration. Regain 2 HP at the start of each turn. Fire or radiant damage disables this trait at the start of its next turn. The trader dies only if it starts a turn at 0 HP and fails to regenerate.
Trader’s Eye. Advantage on Intelligence (Investigation) checks to spot defective or counterfeit goods and on Wisdom (Insight) checks to catch someone trying to sell those goods.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Scimitar or Psychic Bolt attacks. The trader can replace one with Spellcasting.
Scimitar. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 5 (1d6 + 2) slashing damage plus 5 (2d4) psychic damage.
Psychic Bolt. Ranged spell attack, +6 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. Hit 9 (2d4 + 4) psychic damage.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines: Charisma, save DC 14. At will: Message, Minor Illusion. Three times per day each: Disguise Self, Suggestion.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines:
Etherealness. Switch between the Material and Ethereal Planes. The trader remains visible from the other plane, but cannot affect or be affected by anything there.
Trader’s Jargon. One creature the trader can see within 30 ft. makes a DC 14 Charisma save. On a failure, it is vulnerable to psychic damage until the end of its next turn.

gm.title: Reading Black Flag stat blocks
lines:
Rules source. Black Flag Reference Document, Monsters.
The printed modifiers and fixed HP are ready to use. For a Dexterity (Stealth) check to avoid the creature, use its Perception value as the DC. For a Wisdom (Perception) check to detect it, use its Stealth value as the DC.
Condition resistance gives advantage on checks and saves to avoid or end the named condition. Condition vulnerability gives disadvantage. Apply damage resistance and vulnerability to the amount of damage instead.

gm.title: Description
lines: A Carceri fiend coated in sticky tar. Farastus are cruel trackers sometimes charged with hunting down escaped prisoners.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A lanky climbing fiend with long claws, a biting maw, and a sticky hide.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Boundless Movement. Ignore difficult terrain and any magical reduction in speed. The farastu can spend 5 ft. of movement to end the grappled condition on itself automatically.
Magic Resistance. The farastu has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Spider Climb. Traverse hard-to-climb surfaces, including ceilings, without an ability check.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Claw attacks and one Bite attack.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 16 (2d10 + 5) slashing damage. A Large or smaller creature hit is grappled (escape DC 15, with disadvantage on the escape check). The farastu can hold one creature in each claw.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Roll with advantage against a creature the farastu is grappling. A hit deals 12 (2d6 + 5) piercing plus 24 (7d6) acid damage.
Summon Demodand (1/day). There is a 40 percent chance another farastu appears in an unoccupied space within 60 ft. It fights as an ally and cannot summon other demodands. It stays up to 1 minute and disappears sooner if either farastu dies or the summoner dismisses it as an action.

gm.title: Spellcasting

Charisma, no material components. At will: Invisibility (self only). 1/day each: Dispel Magic and Fog Cloud.

lines:
Bonding. The felidar can form a magical bond with a creature it can see immediately after observing it for at least 1 hour within 30 ft. On the same plane the felidar can sense how far away its partner is and in which direction. Either partner can take an action to see and hear through the other's senses until the start of its next turn. While doing so, it loses its own sight and hearing.

gm.title: The hunt
lines: A deed requiring a powers check in a swamp or moor draws at least two hounds on the next full moon. They track the quarry unerringly, fight anyone who interferes, and vanish at dawn. They return on the three nights of a full moon while the quarry survives and the curse remains. A slain hound dissolves into luminous vapor. Recurrence (Su). Killing a fenhound makes the killer the target of a pack at each full moon. Atonement ends the pursuit.

gm.title: Ravenloft Fear
lines: When using the Ravenloft Fear rules, roll a Will save. Apply modifiers to saves against fear. Failure by 1–5 makes the target shaken, 6–10 frightened, and 11–15 panicked. Failure by 16 or more makes it panicked and calls for an immediate Horror save at the Fear DC minus 5. Fear lasts 5d6 rounds. A second failure escalates shaken to frightened or frightened to panicked. Creatures without Intelligence scores are immune. See Ravenloft Player’s Handbook, pp. 77–79.

Rules source. Black Flag Reference Document, Monsters.

gm.title: Description
lines: After a thousand years or more in Ysgard, some fensirs grow to about 25 feet tall and develop a hunger they cannot satisfy. A devourer can curse nearby creatures as it dies.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Death Curse. If the fensir starts its turn at 0 HP and fails to regenerate, each creature within 30 ft. of it when it dies must make a DC 13 Charisma save. A creature that fails is cursed for 24 hours. It gains no benefit from a short or long rest and must make a DC 13 Charisma save at the end of every hour or take 11 (2d10) psychic damage.
Regeneration. The fensir regains 10 HP at the start of its turn if outside sunlight. Taking acid or fire damage suppresses regeneration at the start of its next turn. The fensir dies only if it starts its turn at 0 HP and fails to regenerate.
Sunlight Hypersensitivity. If the fensir starts its turn in sunlight, it must pass a DC 15 Constitution save or be petrified until it is out of the sunlight.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two attacks in any combination of Rend and Boulder.
Rend. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 21 (3d10 + 5) slashing damage.
Boulder. Ranged weapon attack, +8 to hit, range 60/240 ft., one target. A hit deals 18 (2d12 + 5) bludgeoning damage. A Large or smaller creature hit must succeed on a DC 16 Strength save or fall prone. Roll a d6 after each throw. On a 4 or lower, the fensir runs out of boulders.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, p. 135.

gm.title: Description
lines: Years of fighting in Ysgard teach skirmishers to wield earth as a weapon. They can hurl a fleck of gravel that grows into a boulder on its way to the target.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Regeneration. The fensir regains 10 HP at the start of its turn if outside sunlight. Taking acid or fire damage suppresses regeneration at the start of its next turn. The fensir dies only if it starts its turn at 0 HP and fails to regenerate.
Sunlight Hypersensitivity. If the fensir starts its turn in sunlight, it must pass a DC 15 Constitution save or be petrified until it is out of the sunlight.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three Battleaxe attacks or two Magic Stone attacks.
Battleaxe. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 13 (2d8 + 4) slashing damage, or 15 (2d10 + 4) slashing damage if used with two hands.
Magic Stone. Ranged spell attack, +5 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. A hit deals 15 (2d12 + 2) bludgeoning damage. A Large or smaller creature hit must succeed on a DC 13 Strength save or fall prone.
Mud to Stone (Recharge 6). Choose a point the fensir can see within 60 ft. Magical mud fills a 30-ft.-radius sphere centered there. Each creature other than a fensir in the sphere must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity save or take 13 (3d8) bludgeoning damage and become restrained. The creature must roll the save again at the end of its next turn. A success ends the effect, while a failure petrifies it for 24 hours.
Spellcasting. The fensir uses Intelligence to cast Create or Destroy Water, Detect Magic, or Pass without Trace. It can cast each spell once per day.

gm.title: Description
lines: The high priest of Dendar in Omu. A vision of the Black Opal Crown convinced her to plot a coup against Ras Nsi.

gm.title: Senses
lines: Darkvision 120 ft., including in magical darkness.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Death Fangs (2/day). The first time Fenthaza hits with a melee attack on her turn, she can add 16 (3d10) necrotic damage.
Magic Resistance. She has advantage on saves against spells and other magic.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Shapechanger. Change into a Medium snake or back into yuan-ti form. Her equipment and statistics stay the same. She keeps her current form on death.
Multiattack (yuan-ti form only). Make one Constrict and one Scimitar attack.
Constrict. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (2d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage. A Large or smaller target is grappled (escape DC 14) and restrained until the grapple ends. Fenthaza can constrict only one creature at a time.
Scimitar (yuan-ti form only). Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) slashing damage.
Invoke Nightmare (short or long rest). Choose a visible creature within 60 ft. It makes a DC 13 Intelligence save. On a failure, it takes 11 (2d10) psychic damage and is frightened of an immobile, indestructible illusion visible only to it. Fenthaza maintains Concentration for up to 1 minute. The target can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the illusion on a success or taking another 11 (2d10) psychic damage on a failure.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
Only in yuan-ti form. Innate magic uses Charisma (save DC 13) and requires no material components. Animal Friendship is at will and works only on snakes. Suggestion is 3/day.
6th-level warlock. Spellcasting uses Charisma (save DC 13, +5 to hit). Recover both 3rd-level slots after a short or long rest.
Cantrips: Chill Touch, Eldritch Blast (300 ft., +3 damage per hit), Mage Hand, Message, Poison Spray, Prestidigitation.
3rd-level slots: Arms of Hadar, Darkness, Fear, Hex, Hold Person, Hunger of Hadar, Witch Bolt.

gm.title: Encounter context
lines:
Two type 2 Yuan-ti Malisons guard area 5. Fighting in the hall brings the broodguards from area 6 in 1 round. Fenthaza’s stone urn contains an Air Elemental that obeys her. Anyone else removing the lid releases it to attack. After an alarm, the guards cover Fenthaza while she releases the elemental. She tries to capture intruders alive for area 8 and may send a particularly troublesome captive to the altar in area 6. She carries keys to area 8’s restraints. If the party leaves before the coup, she can send the elemental after them. It returns when the pursuit ends.
If prisoners serve a day of labor without incident, she offers freedom and any of Ras Nsi’s puzzle cubes in exchange for taking him down. The agreement can open the armory and start an uprising. She means to betray the party if she can.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Tomb of Annihilation, pp. 111–114 and 117 (Fenthaza, temple roster, and area 5). Uses the Yuan-ti Nightmare Speaker reprinted on p. 239, originally from Volo's Guide to Monsters, p. 205.

gm.title: Description
lines: A hovering tentacled horror that feeds on strong emotions. It avoids confrontation by hiding aboard spelljamming ships and feeding on the nightmares of sleeping crew.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Unusual Nature. The feyr has no need to breathe.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Frightful Bite attack and one Tentacle attack.
Frightful Bite. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Deal 8 (1d10 + 3) piercing damage on a hit. After the hit, every creature within 10 ft. that can see the feyr must pass a DC 13 Wisdom save or be frightened of it until the end of the feyr's next turn.
Tentacle. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 10 ft., one creature. On a hit, the target takes 17 (4d6 + 3) psychic damage and is grappled (escape DC 13). Each of the feyr's two tentacles can hold one creature and cannot attack a different target while holding one.
Invisibility. The feyr turns invisible. An attack or use of Nightmare Fuel ends the effect. It can also end it as a bonus action.
Nightmare Fuel (1/day). Choose an unconscious creature the feyr can see within 10 ft. The target must pass a DC 13 Wisdom save or take 27 (5d10) psychic damage. The feyr gains as many temporary hit points as the damage it actually deals.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

gm.title: Description
lines: An earth elemental with club-tipped tentacles and a colorful shell. The mineral trail it leaves hardens into glass thin enough to cut into window panes.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Antimagic Shell. The snail has advantage on saves against spells, and spell attacks against it have disadvantage. If the snail saves successfully against a spell of 1st level or higher or that spell's attack misses it, its shell releases stored force. Every creature within 30 ft. makes a DC 15 Constitution save, taking 3 (1d6) force damage per spell level on a failure or half as much on a success.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make five Flail Tentacle attacks.
Flail Tentacle. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d4 + 3) bludgeoning damage.
Scintillating Shell (Recharges after a short or long rest). The shell casts bright light for 30 ft. and dim light for another 30 ft. through the end of the snail's next turn. While the light lasts, creatures that can see the snail have disadvantage on attacks against it. When the light first appears, each creature in the bright area that can see the snail must pass a DC 15 Wisdom save or remain stunned until the light ends.
Shell Defense. The snail retreats into its shell. It gains +4 AC and is restrained until it emerges.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines: Emerge. On its turn, the snail can leave its shell to end Shell Defense.

gm.title: Using the shell
lines: An intact shell weighs about 250 pounds and can sell for 5,000 gp. A skilled armorer can cut it into three shields. For 1 month, each shield grants its wielder Antimagic Shell. A shield whose magic has faded can form the base for a Spellguard Shield. Ground shell can also go into the dye and serve as a ritual component for a Robe of Scintillating Colors.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 126.

gm.title: References

gm.title: Description
lines: A slow earth elemental with a brightly colored shell and five mace-tipped tentacles.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Antimagic Shell. The snail saves against spells with advantage. Spell attacks against it have disadvantage. Roll a d6 when the snail succeeds on a saving throw against a spell or a spell attack misses it.
1–2. An area or multitarget spell fails entirely. A spell aimed solely at the snail leaves it unharmed and rebounds at the caster with the original slot level, save DC, spell attack bonus, and spellcasting ability.
3–4. Nothing else happens.
5–6. Each creature within 30 ft. of the snail makes a DC 15 Constitution save. It takes 1d6 force damage per level of the spell on a failure or half as much on a success.
Flail Tentacles. The snail starts with five. Every turn on which it takes at least 10 damage costs it one tentacle. As long as one remains, all dead tentacles grow back in 1d4 days. Losing the last tentacle sends the snail into its shell with total cover. It wails audibly out to 600 ft. until it dies 5d6 minutes later. Regenerate or other limb-restoring magic can stop it from dying.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Flail Tentacle attack per surviving tentacle, all against the same target.
Flail Tentacle. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage.
Scintillating Shell (recharges after a short or long rest). Until the end of the snail’s next turn its shell casts bright light for 30 ft. and dim light for another 30 ft. Creatures that can see the snail attack it with disadvantage during that time. Any creature in the bright light that can see the snail when it activates this effect must pass a DC 15 Wisdom save or become stunned until the light goes out.
Shell Defense. The snail retracts into its shell, raising AC by 4 until it comes out. Emerging takes a bonus action on its turn.

gm.title: Encounter context
lines: Unkh takes the form of a flail snail in Omuan stories (pp. 92, 102–103). A DC 10 Wisdom (Survival) check determines which way a snail was traveling from its slime trail (p. 199). An intact shell weighs about 250 lb. and is worth 2,500 gp.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Tomb of Annihilation, Appendix D, p. 220.

gm.title: Description
lines: The snail grazes on stone and mineral deposits. It leaves a glassy trail that can be harvested and worked into panes or other glassware.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Antimagic Shell. The snail has advantage on saves against spells. Spell attacks against it have disadvantage. When it succeeds on a spell save or a spell attack misses it, roll a d6 for the shell effect below.
Flail Tentacles. The snail starts with five flail tentacles. Whenever it takes at least 10 damage during a single turn, one tentacle dies. If at least one survives, the dead tentacles regrow in 1d4 days. If all five die, the snail withdraws for total cover and wails audibly out to 600 ft. until it dies 5d6 minutes later. Limb-restoring magic such as Regenerate can stop the dying process.

gm.title: Antimagic Shell mechanics
lines:
1–2. An area or multitarget spell fails entirely. A spell targeting only the snail leaves it unaffected and rebounds on the caster, using that caster's slot level, spell save DC, spell attack bonus, and casting ability.
3–4. No further effect.
5–6. Each creature within 30 ft. of the snail makes a DC 15 Constitution save. On a failure it takes 1d6 force damage per level of the spell. On a success it takes half as much.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Flail Tentacle attack per surviving tentacle, all against the same target.
Flail Tentacle. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage.
Scintillating Shell (recharges after a short or long rest). Until the end of the snail's next turn, the shell sheds bright light out to 30 ft. and dim light another 30 ft. Creatures that see the snail have disadvantage on attacks against it while the light lasts. A creature in the bright light that can see it when the effect begins must pass a DC 15 Wisdom save or be stunned until the light ends.
Shell Defense. Withdraw into the shell to gain +4 AC until it emerges.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines: Emerge. The snail can emerge from Shell Defense on its turn.

gm.title: Shell harvesting
lines: An intact shell weighs about 250 lb. and can sell for 5,000 gp. A skilled armorer can make three shields from it. Each shield grants the wielder Antimagic Shell for one month. Once that magic fades, the shield can be used to craft a Spellguard Shield. Ground shell can instead be mixed into dye for a Robe of Scintillating Colors and used in its enchanting ritual.

gm.title: Description
lines: The floating skull of a dead wizard. It obeys its creator’s orders literally and can reform after it is destroyed.

gm.title: Condition immunities
lines: Charmed, Frightened, Paralyzed, Poisoned, and Prone.

Rejuvenation. One hour after its destruction, it reforms at full HP. Sprinkling Holy Water on the remains or casting Dispel Magic or Remove Curse on them prevents its return. If it reforms but can no longer carry out its orders, it acts independently.
Undead Nature. It needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.

gm.title: Skeleton pantomimes
lines:
Roll 1d6 or choose what the skeleton does when left alone.
1. Takes a meal or old letters to its former master’s tomb.
2. Keeps drilling with other skeletons, even after they hack it to pieces.
3. Repeats an old pastime such as dancing, acting, or reading.
4. Returns to familiar work such as cleaning, cooking, mining, or praying.
5. Reenacts its final moments.
6. Guards the post it held in life.

gm.title: Description
lines: A burning skeleton found where Thordak’s fire scarred the land.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Vulnerable to bludgeoning. Immune to fire damage, poison damage, Exhaustion and Poisoned. Darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 9. Understands its languages from life but cannot speak.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Undead Nature. It needs no air, food, water or sleep.
Heated Weapons. A hit with a metal melee weapon deals an extra 3 (1d6) fire damage. The Shortsword damage already includes it.
Illumination. Bright light extends 10 ft., followed by 10 ft. of dim light.

gm.title: Actions
lines:

Ignite. Choose a Large or smaller creature within 5 ft. It makes a DC 12 Dexterity save. On failure it is Grappled (escape DC 12) and catches fire. It takes 3 (1d6) fire damage at the start of each of its turns, even if the grapple ends. The target or a creature within 5 ft. can spend an action to put out the flames. Another effect that quenches them, such as submersion in water, also stops the damage.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A floating, lavender flumph with eyestalks, trailing tentacles, and an oversized feathered hat.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Skills Arcana +4, History +4, Religion +4. Psychic vulnerability. Darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 12. Understands Undercommon without speaking. Telepathy 60 ft.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Advanced Telepathy. Flapjack perceives the content of any telepathic communication within 60 ft. and cannot be Surprised by telepathic creatures.
Prone Deficiency. When knocked Prone, roll a die. On an odd result, Flapjack lands upside down and becomes Incapacitated. At the end of each of its turns it can make a DC 10 Dexterity save to right itself and end that condition.
Telepathic Shroud. Flapjack is immune to divination spells and effects that would sense its emotions or read its thoughts.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Tendrils. Melee weapon attack +4, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing plus 2 (1d4) acid damage. At the end of each of the target's turns, it makes a DC 10 Constitution save. It takes 2 (1d4) acid damage on a failure. A success or Lesser Restoration ends the recurring acid damage.
Stench Spray (1/day). Each creature in a 15-ft. cone must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity save or be coated in a foul liquid for 1d4 hours. A coated creature is Poisoned for the duration. Other creatures are Poisoned while within 5 ft. of it. A creature can remove the stench from itself by bathing in water, alcohol, or vinegar during a short rest.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
As an action, Flapjack can cast one of these spells using Intelligence, save DC 12, with no material components.
At will · Mage Hand, Minor Illusion.
1/day each · Magic Missile, Unseen Servant.

gm.title: Encounters
lines:
Flapjack pilots Captain Sartell's Moondancer and can teach spellcasters the basics of spelljamming.
The Moondancer's helm lets Flapjack sense telepathic activity aboard nearby ships while piloting. The Lucent Edict's psurlons obscure their presence with Aberrant Mind. Flapjack senses something aboard and shares that with Sartell and close companions.

Shortbow. Ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage.

gm.title: Encounter context
lines: Flask and River Mist quietly hire out in Malar’s Throat and Tiryki Anchorage. They can guide travelers to Firefinger or Dungrunglung. The Zhentarim pay attention to what the two learn about Artus Cimber, and the pair report back unless given a reason to keep quiet.

lines: Tomb of Annihilation, p. 35 (River Mist and Flask of Wine) and p. 232 (Tabaxi Hunter).

lines:

lines: An adamantine skeleton supports the bodies of fallen giants. An elemental core inside the chest powers the construct and keeps it under control.

lines:
Berserk. Destroying the core makes the colossus berserk until it is destroyed. On each of its turns it attacks the nearest creature it can see. If no creature is close enough to reach and attack, it attacks an object.
Immutable Form. Spells and other effects cannot change its form.

gm.title: Actions

A Large or smaller creature hit is pulled up to 15 ft. toward the colossus and becomes grappled (escape DC 17). It is restrained until this grapple ends. The colossus can hold up to two creatures this way.
Elemental Breath (Recharge 5–6). Choose acid, cold, fire, or lightning. Each creature in a 90-ft. cone makes a DC 21 Dexterity saving throw, taking 40 (9d8) damage of the chosen type on a failure or half as much on a success. When it exhales, creatures inside its chest cavity also take 40 (9d8) force damage.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines: Bite. Melee weapon attack, +13 to hit, reach 5 ft., one Large or smaller creature grappled by the colossus. A hit deals 20 (3d8 + 7) bludgeoning damage and swallows the creature. The chest cavity can hold up to two swallowed creatures. A swallowed creature is restrained, has total cover against attacks and effects outside the colossus, and takes 10 (3d6) force damage at the start of each of the colossus’s turns.

gm.title: Elemental core
lines: The core is a Large object within the chest cavity with AC 16, 140 HP, and immunity to lightning, poison, and psychic damage. It sheds dim light in a 10-ft. radius. Destroying it makes the colossus berserk and prevents further swallowing. The colossus ejects all swallowed creatures, which land prone in spaces within 10 ft. If the colossus dies, swallowed creatures lose the restrained condition and can spend 10 ft. of movement to leave the corpse, exiting prone.

lines: Berserk. Whenever the golem starts its turn with 40 hit points or fewer, roll a d6. On a 6, the golem goes berserk. gm.title: Description
lines: Dimir agents send these winged horrors after targets who would ordinarily be safe behind walls or on rooftops.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Fear Frenzy. The horror has advantage on attack rolls against frightened creatures.
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight, the horror has disadvantage on attacks and Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 8 (1d6 + 5) slashing damage plus 14 (4d6) psychic damage.
Frightening Screech (Recharge 5–6). Each creature within 30 ft. that can hear the screech must pass a DC 13 Wisdom save or become frightened of the horror for 1 minute. The creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. Once it succeeds on the save or the effect ends, it is immune to this horror’s screech for 24 hours.

gm.title: Customizing a Horror
lines:
For a customized Flying Horror, choose or roll one primary and one secondary feature on two d4s.
Primary 1. Avoidance. If a successful save would halve damage, take no damage on a success and half as much on a failure.
Primary 2. Damage Resistances. Gain resistance to necrotic and psychic damage.
Primary 3. Innate Spellcasting. Cast Darkness three times per day using Charisma (spell save DC 13), without material components.
Primary 4. Psychic Rebuke. When a melee attack deals damage to the horror, it can use its reaction to deal 3 (1d6) psychic damage to each creature within 5 ft.
Secondary 1. Grasping Tendrils. The horror has four tendrils (AC 12 and 10 HP each). Destroying one deals no damage to the horror. As a bonus action, choose a creature it can see within 10 ft. The target makes a DC 9 Dexterity save or is grappled (escape DC 9). Each tendril can hold only one target at a time.
Secondary 2. Indomitable Mind. Gain immunity to being charmed.
Secondary 3. Keen Senses. Gain advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight, hearing, or smell.
Secondary 4. Mind Sight. Magical darkness does not impede the horror’s darkvision.

gm.title: Horrors and Madness
lines: If you use the book’s optional madness rule, track each failed save against a Flying Horror’s Frightening Screech, a Shadow Horror’s claw attack, or a Skittering Horror’s Maddening Presence. After the encounter, each character with any such failures makes a DC 13 Wisdom save. Failure causes short-term madness after one tracked failure, long-term madness after two or three, or indefinite madness after four or more. Consult the Dungeon Master’s Guide for the corresponding madness rules.

lines: Guildmasters’ Guide to Ravnica, p. 203. The optional customization rules appear on p. 204.
