Shortbow. Ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Reversal of Fortune. When another creature deals damage to the nilbog, the nilbog can reduce that damage to 0 and regain 1d6 hit points.

gm.title: Nilbog spirit (possession)
lines: Without a host, the invisible spirit has a flying speed of 30 ft., cannot speak or be attacked, and can take only one kind of action: attempt to possess a goblin within 5 ft. The goblin makes a DC 15 Charisma save. On a failure, its alignment becomes chaotic evil, its Charisma rises to 15 if lower, and it gains Innate Spellcasting, Nilbogism, and Reversal of Fortune from the nilbog stat block. A success prevents this spirit from possessing that goblin for 24 hours. If the host dies or magic ends the possession (such as Hallow, Magic Circle, or Protection from Evil and Good), the spirit looks for another goblin. The spirit can leave at any time but leaves willingly only if it knows of another potential host nearby. A former host reverts to its usual statistics and loses the features granted by the spirit.

gm.title: Camp Vengeance
lines: Parties arriving by boat are ordered to ferry messages and seven sick soldiers downriver to Port Nyanzaru. The soldiers have Blue Mist Fever, Shivering Sickness, or Throat Leeches. Parties arriving over land are ordered to lead four Guards and four Tribal Warriors on a two-week undead patrol back the way they came. Refusal brings arrest and trial. A guilty verdict means confiscation of gear and abandonment in the jungle. Undril Silvertusk can intercede for a party that earned her respect. Otherwise, a sound argument and a successful DC 15 Charisma (Persuasion) check with each of Ord Firebeard and Perne Salhana can prevent judgment.

lines: Rare in tropical and subtropical deserts or caves. Squad or city, usually 8 or more. Carnivore. Intelligence 5–18. Morale 15–18. Treasure J, K, M, Q, with F and U × 10 listed parenthetically. No magic resistance. 60-foot infravision. Stands 6 feet tall, with a 4-foot body and 10-foot tail.

lines:
6 HD: THAC0 15, 975 XP (1,400 with a Legacy).
7 HD: THAC0 13, 1,400 XP (2,000 with a Legacy).
8 HD: THAC0 13, 2,000 XP (3,000 with a Legacy).

11–12 HD: THAC0 9.
Add 1,000 XP for each HD above 8.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Claws and sting. Two front-facing claws deal 1d4 + 1 apiece. The tail can strike to any side and deals 1d4 plus poison on a hit. The stat line also allows weapon damage without specifying a weapon routine.
Sting poison. At 6–8 HD, a failed save vs. poison puts the victim to sleep for 2d8 rounds. At 9–10 HD it deals 3d8 damage on failure. At 11–12 HD, save vs. poison at −2 or die immediately.

gm.title: Sunlight and armor
lines:
Armor rated AC 7 or worse improves its AC by only 1. It cannot swim, and water washes off its makeup in 1d4 rounds.
Direct sun with no makeup deals 1d6 + 2 damage per round until the creature gets underground or reapplies all makeup. Dexterity and morale drop to 3, movement is halved, and it automatically loses initiative. A full turn of continuous exposure kills it in flames. Reflected sunlight, including moonlight or a mirror reflection, deals 1d3 damage without makeup and halves Dexterity and morale. Direct sunlight with 50–99% makeup coverage has the same effects as reflected sunlight.

gm.title: Description
lines: The ancient dragon who founded the Izzet League. From a private laboratory at the top of its guildhall, he coordinates research and gathers secrets in place of a conventional hoard.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Legendary Resistance (3/day). Niv-Mizzet can choose to succeed on a saving throw he failed.
Locus of the Firemind. Niv-Mizzet can concentrate on two different spells at once. He has advantage on saving throws to maintain concentration.
Magic Resistance. Niv-Mizzet has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Master Chemister. When Niv-Mizzet casts a damaging spell, he can change its damage type to cold, fire, force, lightning, or thunder.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
Niv-Mizzet is a 20th-level Izzet wizard. Intelligence is his spellcasting ability (DC 26, +18 to hit with spell attacks).
Cantrips (at will). Fire Bolt, Light, Prestidigitation, Ray of Frost, Shocking Grasp.
1st level (4 slots). Detect Magic, Magic Missile, Shield, Thunderwave, Unseen Servant.
2nd level (3 slots). Blur, Enlarge/Reduce, Flaming Sphere, Scorching Ray.
3rd level (3 slots). Counterspell, Fireball, Hold Person, Lightning Bolt, Slow.
4th level (3 slots). Confusion, Dimension Door, Fabricate.
5th level (2 slots). Conjure Elemental, Polymorph, Wall of Fire, Wall of Force.
6th level (1 slot). Chain Lightning, Disintegrate, True Seeing.
7th level (1 slot). Project Image, Reverse Gravity, Teleport.
8th level (1 slot). Control Weather, Maze, Power Word Stun.
9th level (1 slot). Prismatic Wall.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +17 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 18 (2d8 + 9) piercing damage and 14 (4d6) fire damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +17 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 14 (2d4 + 9) slashing damage.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +17 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 16 (2d6 + 9) bludgeoning damage.
Fire Breath (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in the 90-ft. cone makes a DC 25 Dexterity save, taking 91 (26d6) fire damage on a failure or half as much on a success.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
Niv-Mizzet has three legendary actions and regains spent actions at the start of his turn. He can use one option at a time, at the end of another creature’s turn.
Cantrip (1 action). Cast a cantrip from his spell list.
Tail Attack (1 action). Make a Tail attack.
Wing Attack (2 actions). Each creature within 15 ft. must pass a DC 25 Dexterity save or take 14 (2d4 + 9) bludgeoning damage and fall prone. Niv-Mizzet can then fly up to half his flying speed.
Dracogenius (3 actions). Regain one expended spell slot of 3rd level or lower.

gm.title: Roleplaying
lines: Niv-Mizzet values invention, has spent more than ten thousand years studying the world, and quickly loses patience with people he thinks lack imagination.

gm.title: Source notes
lines: The printed spell list places Hold Person at 3rd level, using a 3rd-level slot. The indexed reference places it at 2nd level.

gm.title: Description
lines: A nosferatu can return from apparent death in direct moonlight. By day, it relies on servants already under its control.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Fledgling sample, 5th-level human aristocrat. Initiative +8. Touch AC 14, flat-footed AC 22. BAB +3, grapple +4. Space and reach 5 ft. Fort +3, Ref +7, Will +6.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack or full attack. Choose slam +4 melee (1d6 + 1), +1 rapier +8 melee (1d6 + 2, 18–20), or masterwork heavy crossbow +8 ranged (1d10, 19–20/×2).
Domination (Su). Standard action on a target within 30 ft. that the vampire can look at. Will DC 18 or dominate person at caster level 12.
Blood Drain (Ex). Pin a living target in a grapple. Each round the pin holds, drain 1d4 Constitution and gain 5 temporary HP. Each victim of Blood Drain must also make a DC 18 Will save or be dominated until break enchantment succeeds or the vampire dies.
Children of the Night (Su, 1/day). Standard action to call 1d6 + 1 rat swarms, 1d4 + 1 bat swarms, or 3d6 wolves. They arrive in 2d6 rounds and serve for up to 1 hour.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
DR 10/silver and magic, cold and electricity resistance 10, turn resistance +4, spider climb, undead traits. Gaseous form as a standard action at will, with indefinite duration and fly speed 20 ft. (perfect). Alternate Form can assume bat, dire bat, wolf, or dire wolf form. As a standard action assume the listed animal form. Lose the slam and domination, gain the animal’s natural weapons and extraordinary attacks, and retain this form until the next sunrise or another change.
Lunar Regeneration. Direct moonlight converts past damage to nonlethal damage even after apparent death. Heal 3, 4, 6, or 8 per round in crescent, half, gibbous, or full moonlight, plus the age bonus. Fire, acid, and blessed or holy weapons deal normal damage. It can reattach severed limbs. It cannot regenerate a lost limb or recover nonlethal damage with its head detached.
Restful Sleep. While at 1 HP or more, heal 1 HP per HD per hour in its coffin. Daylight disables supernatural abilities. After exposure to direct sunlight, it must sleep in its coffin for 8 hours to restore them. Existing domination persists, and an alternate form cannot end until powers return.

gm.title: Spawn
lines: A humanoid or monstrous humanoid drained to Constitution 0 or less rises on the next full moon. At 4 HD or fewer it becomes spawn, otherwise a nosferatu. Spawn remain controlled until the creator dies. Nosferatu spawn retain charm, gaseous form, spider climb and daylight powerlessness. They heal 2 HP per hour asleep in their coffins if at 1 HP or more, or 2 HP per round in direct full moonlight.

gm.title: Repelling and slaying
lines: Garlic repels it, and a clearly presented holy symbol or mirror keeps it 5 ft. away. It cannot enter a private home without invitation. A stake through the heart kills it while left in place. At 0 HP it collapses but may return in moonlight. Burn the whole body or scatter the severed limbs beyond its minions’ reach. Running water costs one-third of HP each round and destroys it after 3 rounds of immersion.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Bluff +21, Diplomacy +16, Gather Information +11, Hide +12, Intimidate +12, Listen +12, Move Silently +12, Search +13, Sense Motive +15, Spot +12. Alertness, Combat Reflexes, Dodge, Great Fortitude, Improved Initiative, Lightning Reflexes, Skill Focus (Diplomacy), Weapon Finesse.

gm.title: Encounter adaptation
lines: Apply the strain to the 3.5 vampire template. Retain unmodified abilities, size, BAB, saves and skill points. The base vampire uses undead d12 Hit Dice and has no Constitution score. Keep an existing swim speed and ignore vulnerability to immersion in running water if the base creature can swim. Use save DC 10 + half HD rounded down + Charisma modifier unless specified. Age rows replace one another. Nosferatu lack the base vampire’s Energy Drain. Age DR always requires silver and magic. The cerebral subtype changes the feeding attack only.

gm.title: Age modifiers
lines:
Apply one row to a base creature. The sample already includes its adjustments. Ability scores are listed in Str, Dex, Int, Wis, Cha order.
Fledgling. Abilities 4/4/2/2/6. Speed +0 ft., natural AC +6, turn resistance +4, CR +2. DR 10, lunar healing +0.
Mature. Abilities 4/4/4/2/8. Speed +10 ft., natural AC +6, turn resistance +4, CR +2. DR 15, lunar healing +0.
Old. Abilities 6/6/4/4/8. Speed +10 ft., natural AC +7, turn resistance +5, CR +3. DR 15, lunar healing +1.
Ancient. Abilities 6/6/6/4/10. Speed +20 ft., natural AC +7, turn resistance +6, CR +3. DR 20, lunar healing +1.
Eminent. Abilities 8/8/6/6/10. Speed +20 ft., natural AC +8, turn resistance +7, CR +4. DR 20, lunar healing +2.
Patriarch. Abilities 10/10/8/8/12. Speed +30 ft., natural AC +8, turn resistance +8, CR +5. DR 25, lunar healing +3.

gm.title: Description
lines: This blood-drinking undead keeps the skills and spells of its former life. It can pass for a living person in daylight, though it casts no shadow and has no reflection.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Any terrain. Very rare, solitary, and active at any time. Drinks blood. Intelligence 8–18. Treasure F. Any alignment, usually evil. Appearing 1. No magic resistance. Height 5–7 feet. Morale 15–16. The XP listed is the minimum.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Bite or weapon. One bite deals 1d4 damage. It can instead use a weapon or cast a spell from its former class. Use the THAC0 of the equivalent class and level. Strength is at least 16.
Charm. A creature that meets its gaze saves at −2 or is affected as by charm person. The nosferatu can then use suggestion on that victim.
Change form. It can become gaseous at will and is immune to physical attacks in that form. At night it can become a large bat. By day it can become a raven. It can also use spider climb.
Summon animals. Call 1d100 rats or bats underground, or 3d6 wolves in the wilderness. They arrive in 2d6 rounds.

gm.title: Defenses and defeat
lines:
Only +1 or better magical weapons can harm it. It regains 1 HP each round. Sleep, charm, hold, poison, and paralysis fail against it. Cold and electricity spells deal half damage. At 0 HP it turns gaseous and flees to its coffin. If it fails to reach the coffin within 12 turns, it dies. After eight hours inside, it regains corporeal form.
Garlic repels it. Clerical symbols and holy water are harmless to it. A cleric of opposing alignment or a cleric specialized in hunting undead can turn it. Immersion in running water for three consecutive rounds destroys it. A wooden stake through the heart stops it, but it resumes healing if the stake is removed. To destroy a staked nosferatu permanently, behead it and fill its mouth with earth consecrated to a good deity.

gm.title: Invitation and spawn
lines: A resident must invite it into a private home. Charm or deception can secure the invitation. Once invited, it can come and go. If it chooses to create spawn, a drained human or humanoid rises after three days unless the body is burned or destroyed. The spawn obeys its creator until the creator dies.

gm.title: Former class
lines: Keep the original class’s memories, abilities, skills, and restrictions. Set class level to at least 7 and at most 9 when it becomes a nosferatu. It can advance thereafter at triple the usual XP. Keep ability scores except that Strength is at least 16 and Constitution is no longer required. Warriors and clerics can wear armor without improving AC. Clerics retain spells from their original Immortal patron only if their alignment still matches.

gm.title: Hunger and Red Curse
lines: It must drink at least 9 HP worth of mortal blood per week. After a week of fasting, its ability scores fall by 1 each day to a minimum of 9. An extra 1d4 HP worth of fresh blood restores lost scores. Nonhumanoid blood dulls the pain for one day without restoring scores. It never acquires Legacies and needs no cinnabryl.

lines:

lines:
Multiattack. Make two Lancing Bolt attacks or one Lancing Bolt attack and one Harpoon attack.
Lancing Bolt. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 100/400 ft., one target. A hit deals 15 (2d10 + 4) piercing damage.
Harpoon. Ranged weapon attack, +7 to hit, range 50/200 ft., one target. A hit deals 9 (1d10 + 4) piercing damage and grapples the target (escape DC 12). Its speed is unchanged, but its own movement must take it closer to the oaken bolter. An escape attempt deals 5 (1d10) slashing damage to the creature whether or not it succeeds. The oaken bolter can hold only one target in this grapple at a time.
Explosive Bolt (Recharge 5–6). Choose a point within 120 ft. Creatures within 20 ft. of it make a DC 15 Dexterity save, taking 17 (5d6) fire damage on a failure or half as much on a success.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines: Reel In. Pull a creature held by Harpoon 20 ft. closer.

gm.title: Clockwork enhancements
lines:
For an individual clockwork, choose or roll one enhancement and one potential malfunction, both on d10.
1. Camouflaged. Gain Stealth proficiency if needed. While still, the clockwork passes for an inactive machine.
2. Sensors. Raise darkvision to at least 120 ft. and add Perception proficiency if needed.
3. Improved Armor. Increase AC by 2.
4. Increased Speed. Increase speed by 10 ft.
5. Reinforced Construction. Gain resistance to force, lightning and thunder damage.
6. Self-Repairing. At the start of its turn, recover 5 HP if it has at least 1 HP. Lightning damage skips the next recovery.
7. Sturdy Frame. Add its number of Hit Dice to its maximum HP.
8. Suction. Gain a 30-ft. climbing speed.
9. Vocal Resonator. It speaks rudimentary Common or Gnomish, as its maker decides.
10. Water Propulsion. Gain a 30-ft. swimming speed.

gm.title: Clockwork malfunctions
lines:
1. Faulty Sensors. Roll a d6 at turn start. On a 1, the clockwork is blinded until turn end.
2. Flawed Targeting. Roll a d6 at turn start. On a 1, its attack rolls have disadvantage until turn end.
3. Ground Fault. Gain vulnerability to lightning damage.
4. Imprinting Loop. Roll a d6 at turn start. On a 1, it mistakes a visible creature within 30 ft. for its maker. It avoids harming that creature for 1 minute or until the creature attacks or damages it.
5. Leaking Lubricant. Roll a d6 at turn start. On a 1, it gains one level of exhaustion despite immunity.
6. Limited Steering. It moves in straight lines, turning up to 90 degrees before moving and once at the halfway point. It can rotate freely on a turn when it uses none of its speeds.
7. Overactive Sense of Self-Preservation. At the start of a combat turn while at half HP or less, roll a d6. On a 1, the clockwork retreats if it can. If it cannot retreat, it keeps fighting.
8. Overheats. Roll a d6 at turn start. On a 1, it is incapacitated until turn end.
9. Rusty Gears. It has disadvantage on initiative rolls and its speed drops by 10 ft.
10. Weak Armor. Remove its immunity to bludgeoning, piercing and slashing damage from nonmagical, non-adamantine attacks.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

gm.title: Description
lines: An army may hire this yugoloth to break a siege by spreading plague. The oinoloth can remove disease too, at lasting cost to the patient.

gm.title: Damage resistances
lines: Cold, fire, lightning, and bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Magic Resistance. The oinoloth has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Claw attacks and use either Spellcasting or Teleport.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 14 (3d6 + 4) slashing damage plus 22 (4d10) necrotic damage.
Corrupted Healing (Recharge 6). Touch one willing creature within 5 ft. It regains all its hit points. The oinoloth can also end one disease or remove one condition from the target. The eligible conditions are blinded, deafened, paralyzed, and poisoned. The target then gains 1 level of exhaustion and loses 7 (2d6) from its hit point maximum. It dies if its maximum drops to 0. Only Wish or three castings of Greater Restoration on the target within the same hour can remove this reduction.
Teleport. Teleport up to 60 ft. to a visible, unoccupied space, taking any worn or carried equipment along.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
As an action, cast a listed spell using Charisma (save DC 16). No material components are required.
At will. Darkness, Detect Magic, Dispel Magic, Hold Monster, Invisibility (self only).
1/day each. Feeblemind, Globe of Invulnerability.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines:
Bringer of Plagues (Recharge 5–6). Blight a 30-ft.-radius sphere centered on the oinoloth for 24 hours. Normal plants in the area wither and die.
A creature that enters the area or starts its turn there makes a DC 16 Constitution save. On a failure, it takes 14 (4d6) poison damage and is poisoned. On a success, it gains immunity to this oinoloth's Bringer of Plagues for 24 hours.
A creature poisoned this way cannot regain hit points. Every 24 hours, it can repeat the save. Each failure reduces its hit point maximum by 5 (1d10) until the poison ends. The creature dies if its maximum drops to 0. Three successful saves end the poison.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Amphibious. The olothec breathes air and water.
Immutable Form. Powers, spells, and other effects cannot change its form.
Supernatural Resistance. It has advantage on saving throws against powers, spells, and other supernatural effects.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make six Devolving Tentacle attacks and use Piscine Transformation.
Devolving Tentacle. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. Hit 12 (2d6 + 5) piercing damage. The first time a creature is hit by this attack on a turn, it must succeed on a DC 17 Constitution save or be slimed. While slimed it subtracts 1d4 from each attack roll and ability check. After each of its turns, the penalty die steps up from d4 to d6, d8, d10, then d12. A successful repeat save at the end of its turn ends the effect, as do Cure Ailment and Lesser Restoration.
Piscine Transformation (3rd-order power). Choose a visible Humanoid within 60 ft. On a failed DC 17 Wisdom save, change one part of its body. A fish head prevents speech. Fins in place of legs limit walking speed to 10 ft. if it was higher and give a 30-ft. swim speed. A fish torso lets the target breathe only water and hold its breath for 1 hour. If it gains the torso out of water, it starts suffocating. A 4th-order or higher Cure Ailment or Greater Restoration ends a transformation. With all three changes at once, the target permanently becomes a fishlike hybrid. Only Wish or similar magic can restore it then.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: Jaunt (3rd-order power). Teleport 30 ft. to a visible, unoccupied space.

gm.title: Lair Actions
lines:
In its lair, take one action from the list on initiative count 20 after any ties. Use a different option from the previous round.
Baleful Teleport. Choose up to two visible creatures within 60 ft. Each that fails a DC 15 Charisma save teleports up to 60 ft. to a visible, unoccupied space of the olothec’s choice.
Psychic Shock. Choose up to two creatures within 30 ft. slimed by Devolving Tentacle. Each takes 9 (2d8) psychic damage. The olothec heals for the total damage dealt.
Slime Eruption. Choose up to three creatures within 120 ft. On a failed DC 15 Constitution save, the target is Poisoned until the end of its next turn.

gm.title: Slime Servant Template
lines: After 1 continuous minute slimed by Devolving Tentacle, the slime ends and the creature loses its memories and becomes an NPC loyal to the olothec. It keeps its statistics and gains amphibious breathing and a swim speed at least equal to its walking speed. It cannot be Charmed or Frightened. The olothec can use its senses and speak through it if it can speak. Only Wish restores its memories and original state.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

gm.title: Description
lines: The Demon Prince of Undeath rules Thanatos from the fortress city of Naratyr. He wants to extinguish all life and rule the Undead that remain.

gm.title: Armor
lines: Natural armor. AC 20 while holding the Wand of Orcus.

gm.title: Damage immunities
lines: Necrotic and poison. Nonmagical bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Legendary Resistance (3/day). When Orcus fails a save, he can spend a use to succeed.
Magic Resistance. Orcus has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Master of Undeath. Orcus can cast Animate Dead at will and Create Undead three times per day. He chooses the level for each casting. The resulting Undead obey him indefinitely. He can cast Create Undead at any time of day.
Special Equipment. Orcus carries the Wand of Orcus.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three attacks in any combination of Wand of Orcus, Tail, or Necrotic Bolt.
Wand of Orcus. Melee weapon attack, +19 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 24 (3d8 + 11) bludgeoning damage plus 13 (2d12) necrotic damage.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +16 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 21 (3d8 + 8) force damage plus 9 (2d8) poison damage.
Necrotic Bolt. Ranged spell attack, +15 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. A hit deals 29 (5d8 + 7) necrotic damage.
Conjure Undead (1/day). While holding the Wand of Orcus, summon any combination of Undead with a total of up to 500 average hit points. They appear in unoccupied spaces within 300 ft. and obey Orcus until destroyed or dismissed by him as an action.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
As an action, cast a listed spell using Charisma (save DC 23). No material components are required.
At will. Detect Magic.
3/day. Dispel Magic.
1/day. Time Stop.
Wand Spellcasting. While holding the Wand of Orcus, use an action to cast a listed spell (save DC 18). The wand holds up to 7 charges and regains 1d4 + 3 charges each dawn.
At will from the wand. Animate Dead, Blight, Speak with Dead.
1 charge each. Circle of Death or Finger of Death.
2 charges. Power Word Kill.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
Orcus has 3 legendary actions and regains them at the start of his turn. Spend the stated cost on one option immediately after another creature's turn. He cannot use them while incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. If surprised, he must finish his first turn before using one.
Attack (1 action). Make one Tail or Necrotic Bolt attack.
Creeping Death (2 actions). Choose a point on the ground that Orcus can see within 100 ft. A cylinder 60 ft. high and 10 ft. in radius rises from that point until the end of his next turn. Creatures inside have vulnerability to necrotic damage.

gm.title: Lair actions
lines:
At initiative count 20, after any creature tied at that count, Orcus can use one option while in his lair and able to act. He cannot repeat the same option two rounds in a row. If surprised, he must finish his first turn before using one.
Deadly Utterance. Subject one creature Orcus knows is in his lair to Power Word Kill. He can target a creature he cannot see.
Grasp of the Dead. Conjure skeletal arms in a visible 20-ft. square of ground until the next initiative count 20. Each creature in the square when the arms appear makes a DC 23 Strength save. On a failure, it is restrained until the arms vanish or Orcus releases it, which requires no action.
Undead Servants. Animate up to six corpses in the lair as skeletons, zombies, or ghouls. They obey Orcus's telepathic commands anywhere in the lair.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:
One or both effects can occur in the region around the lair.
Charnel Realm. The region smells of rotting flesh and fills with swarms of flies.
Undead Beasts. Some dead Beasts rise as skeletons or zombies. Undead versions of local wildlife are common.
These effects fade over 1d10 days after Orcus dies.

lines: Necrotic, poison. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical sources.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Wand of Orcus. The wand holds up to 7 charges and regains 1d4 + 3 at dawn. Its abilities that call for a save use DC 18. While holding it, Orcus can use an action to cast Animate Dead, Blight, or Speak with Dead. He can also cast Circle of Death or Finger of Death for 1 charge each, or Power Word Kill for 2 charges.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). If Orcus fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed.
Magic Resistance. Orcus has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Magic Weapons. Orcus’s weapon attacks are magical.
Master of Undeath. Orcus chooses the spell level when he casts Animate Dead or Create Undead. The creatures they create remain under his control indefinitely. He can cast Create Undead at any time of day.

gm.title: Innate Spellcasting
lines:
Orcus uses Charisma (spell save DC 23, +15 to hit with spell attacks). He needs no material components.
At will. Chill Touch (17th level), Detect Magic.
3/day each. Create Undead, Dispel Magic.
1/day. Time Stop.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Wand of Orcus attacks.
Wand of Orcus. Melee weapon attack, +19 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 21 (3d8 + 8) bludgeoning damage plus 13 (2d12) necrotic damage.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +16 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 21 (3d8 + 8) piercing damage plus 9 (2d8) poison damage.
Conjure Undead (Wand of Orcus, once per dawn). While holding the wand, Orcus creates undead creatures with no more than 500 combined average hit points. They appear in unoccupied spaces within 300 ft. and obey him until destroyed or dismissed. Dismissing them takes an action.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
Orcus has 3 legendary actions and regains spent actions at the start of his turn. He can use one option at the end of another creature’s turn.
Tail (1 action). Make one Tail attack.
A Taste of Undeath (1 action). Cast Chill Touch at 17th level.
Creeping Death (2 actions). Choose a point on the ground Orcus can see within 100 ft. A cylinder 60 ft. high with a 10-ft. radius appears there until the end of Orcus’s next turn. Creatures inside have vulnerability to necrotic damage.

gm.title: Lair actions
lines:
On initiative count 20, losing initiative ties, Orcus can use one option. He cannot pick the same option two rounds in a row.
Power Word Kill. One creature Orcus knows is in the lair is subject to Power Word Kill. He can choose it without seeing it. The spell uses its normal hit-point threshold.
Animate Corpses. Raise up to six corpses in the lair as skeletons, zombies, or ghouls. They obey Orcus by telepathy from anywhere in the lair.
Skeletal Arms. Choose a 20-ft. square on the ground Orcus can see. Each creature in the square when the arms appear must succeed on a DC 23 Strength save or be restrained. The arms vanish at the next initiative count 20. Orcus can release their grasp before then without taking an action.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:
Dead beasts sometimes animate, and skeletal or zombified local wildlife roam the area.
The air reeks of decay and swarms with flies, even without carrion.
A humanoid who spends at least 1 hour within 1 mile of the lair must make a DC 23 Wisdom save. On a failure, roll on the Madness of Orcus table. A success grants immunity to this regional effect for 24 hours.
After Orcus dies, these effects fade over 1d10 days.

gm.title: Madness of Orcus
lines:
Roll d100 when a creature succumbs to this madness in the lair or within Orcus’s sight. The resulting flaw lasts until cured.
01–20. Withdraws into bitter thoughts about living.
21–40. Feels driven to torment the weak.
41–60. Disturbs the dead freely while trying to understand death.
61–80. Seeks to become undead and endure forever.
81–100. Dwells on the futility of life.

gm.title: Description
lines: An infernal bounty hunter that tracks quarry across the planes. An orthon between assignments may work for anyone who offers it a difficult hunt.

gm.title: Damage resistances
lines: Cold. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks made without silvered weapons.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Magic Resistance. The orthon has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Infernal Dagger. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 11 (2d4 + 6) force damage. The target makes a DC 17 Constitution save, taking 22 (4d10) poison damage on a failure or half on a success. On a failure, it is also poisoned for 1 minute. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns to end the condition.
Brass Crossbow. Ranged weapon attack, +7 to hit, range 100/400 ft., one target. A hit deals 14 (2d10 + 3) force damage and applies one of the rider effects below. The orthon cannot choose the same effect two rounds in a row.
Acid. The target makes a DC 17 Constitution save, taking an extra 17 (5d6) acid damage on a failure or half on a success.
Blindness. The target takes 5 (1d10) extra radiant damage. The target and every other creature within 20 ft. of it must pass a DC 17 Dexterity save or be blinded until the end of the orthon's next turn.
Concussion. The target and every other creature within 20 ft. of it must make a DC 17 Constitution save, taking 13 (2d12) thunder damage on a failure or half on a success.
Entanglement. The target makes a DC 17 Dexterity save or is restrained by sticky webs for 1 hour. It can use an action to make a DC 17 Strength or Dexterity check, escaping on a success.
Paralysis. The target takes 22 (4d10) lightning damage and makes a DC 17 Constitution save. On a failure, it is paralyzed for 1 minute and can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns to end the condition.
Tracking. For 24 hours, the orthon knows the target's direction and distance while they share a plane. If the target is on another plane, the orthon knows which plane it is on without learning its exact location.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines: Invisibility Field (Recharge 4–6). The orthon becomes invisible. Its gear remains invisible while it wears or carries it. The effect ends immediately after it makes an attack roll or an attack roll hits it.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Explosive Retribution. When the orthon drops to 15 hit points or fewer, it explodes. Every other creature within 30 ft. makes a DC 17 Dexterity save, taking 9 (2d8) fire damage plus 9 (2d8) thunder damage on a failure or half on a success. The explosion destroys the orthon, its infernal dagger, and its brass crossbow.

lines: Parry. The captain adds 2 to its AC against one melee attack that would hit it. To do so, the captain must see the attacker and be wielding a melee weapon. It takes a strong personality, ruthless cunning, and a silver tongue to keep a gang of bandits in line. The bandit captain has these qualities in spades. In addition to managing a crew of selfish malcontents, the pirate captain is a variation of the bandit captain, with a ship to protect and command. gm.title: Delerium contamination
lines:
Printed source. Appendix C, pp. 222–223.
Add contamination levels from each exposure. A contaminated character rolls 1d20 at the end of each long rest and gains one level on a 1.
Symptoms are cumulative. Level 1 has no symptom. Level 2 halves healing from Hit Dice. Level 3 prevents HP recovery from a long rest. Level 4 halves damage the creature deals with weapon attacks and spells. Level 5 makes it Incapacitated. Level 6 triggers Monstrous Transformation.
After a character gains a level, roll 1d6. On a result at or below the current level, the GM chooses a new mutation or rolls on the printed mutations table. Replace or reroll duplicate mutations.
Contamination does not wear off. Purge Contamination can remove levels and causes Exhaustion. Heal removes all contamination and mutations. Each level removed also removes one random mutation. At level 0, all symptoms and mutations end.
A contaminated humanoid rises as a Haze Husk 24 hours after death. It rises as a Haze Wight if it had at least six class levels or Hit Dice. Raising a creature from the dead reduces its contamination by one level.
Monstrous Transformation. At level 6 or higher, the creature transforms after one round. Replace its statistics, hit points, and Hit Dice with those of a monster the GM chooses. Contamination resets to 0, and the GM controls the transformed creature.
Wish or similar magic can restore one transformed creature, clearing its madness and contamination. Using Wish this way gives the caster a 33 percent chance of losing the ability to cast it again.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Detached Eyes. Six floating eyes function as objects, each with AC 24 and 1 HP. An eye's shield makes it immune to damage until it uses a psionic effect. The shield returns at the start of the overmind's next turn. Destroyed eyes are replaced at the end of its next turn.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Bite. Melee weapon attack +4, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 14 (4d6) piercing damage.
Eye Psionics. Use three different effects through the detached eyes. Unless specified, each targets a creature the overmind can see within 120 ft.
Charm Beam. DC 16 Wisdom save or Charmed by the overmind for 1 hour. The charm ends if the overmind harms the target or an ally of the target.
Compulsion Beam. DC 16 Intelligence save or the target uses its reaction, if available, to move up to its speed toward the closest ally it can see and make a weapon attack against that ally. Creatures immune to Charmed are unaffected.
Toxic Vapors. Choose a visible point within 120 ft. Each creature within 10 ft. of it makes a DC 16 Constitution save or is Poisoned for 1 minute. A creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on success.
Telekinetic Beam. DC 16 Strength save or the overmind moves the target up to 30 ft. in any direction and deals 7 (2d6) force damage at the end of the movement. Alternatively, it can move a visible unworn, uncarried object within 120 ft., weighing up to 300 pounds, up to 30 ft. and manipulate it precisely.
Lightning Bolt. Each creature in a 60-ft. line, 5 ft. wide, makes a DC 16 Dexterity save, taking 21 (6d6) lightning damage on a failure or half on a success.
Fire Beam. The target makes a DC 16 Dexterity save. On a failure it takes 36 (8d8) fire damage and burns for 1 minute, taking 9 (2d8) fire damage at the start of each turn. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the burning on a success. Any creature can use an action to put out the flames.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: The Great Eye (Recharge 6). The overmind projects a 150-ft. cone. For the overmind and each creature in the cone affected by a spell, that spell’s effects end immediately for that creature.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Away with You! When a creature within 5 ft. hits the overmind with a melee attack, it can use Telekinetic Beam against that attacker.

gm.title: Lair Actions
lines:
On initiative count 20, losing ties, the overmind can choose one effect. It can't choose the same effect two rounds in a row.
Gas Belch. The ceiling, floor, or wall within 60 ft. gives off gas in a 20-ft. sphere through the end of initiative count 20 in the next round. A creature that enters the gas for the first time or starts its turn there makes a DC 15 Constitution save or is Poisoned until the start of its next turn.

gm.title: MCDM companion rules
lines:
Shared turn. The caregiver and companion act on the same turn. The companion moves and uses its reaction and bonus action independently. To do anything with its action besides Dash, Disengage or Dodge, it normally needs a command that costs the caregiver a bonus action. It must see or hear the caregiver. If the caregiver is Incapacitated, it can act without a command. The GM chooses who controls it when the caregiver is Incapacitated or absent.
Ferocity. At the start of their turn, unless Incapacitated, the companion gains 1d4 Ferocity plus one for each enemy it sees or hears within 5 ft. A swarm sharing one stat block counts as one enemy. Spend the listed cost before taking a Ferocity action. It uses the companion’s action, requires the listed caregiver level and is unavailable during a rampage.
Rampage. After rolling Ferocity, a companion with at least 10 Ferocity risks a rampage if it is not Incapacitated. A caregiver who is not Incapacitated and can be seen or heard can prevent it with a Wisdom (Animal Handling) check against DC 5 + Ferocity, without spending an action. If the companion rampages, it immediately moves toward the nearest creature it senses and makes its signature attack, with extra damage equal to half its Ferocity on a hit. If an ally and enemy tie for nearest, roll any die. On an odd roll the caregiver’s player chooses a tied ally. On an even roll they choose a tied enemy. If it cannot reach a target, it Dashes toward it. If it senses none, it moves as far as it can in a random safe direction. Ferocity falls to 0 after this action or at the end of the turn.
Recovery. At 0 HP, a companion makes death saves. After combat, Ferocity resets to 0. A companion that is not dying first regains HP equal to its remaining Ferocity.

gm.title: Setting Spells
lines:
Delerium Orb. Action, 120 ft. One visible creature makes a save using an ability chosen by the caster. Choose cold, fire, lightning, necrotic, psychic, or radiant damage. Deal 6d6 on failure or half on success, plus 2d6 per slot level above 1st.
Warp Bolt. Action, 60 ft., concentrate up to 1 minute. Automatically hit a contaminated target, or make a ranged spell attack against an uncontaminated one. A hit deals 6d6 necrotic and one level of Contamination. On later turns, use an action for a new bolt. Each slot level above 2nd permits one more target.
Delerium Blast. Action, 150 ft. Creatures in a 20-ft.-radius sphere make an Intelligence save. Failure deals 10d6 psychic damage and Incapacitates until the end of the target's next turn. Success halves damage and prevents Incapacitated. Add 2d6 per slot level above 4th.
Conjure the Deep Haze. Action, 120 ft., concentrate up to 10 minutes. A 20-ft.-radius sphere spreads around corners and is heavily obscured until it ends or strong wind clears it. First entry on a turn or starting a turn there forces a Constitution save. Failure deals 8d6 necrotic and one level of Contamination. Success halves damage without Contamination. Holding breath does not help.
Octarine Spray. Action, 60-ft. cone. Each creature makes a Constitution save. Roll a d8 for each creature. On rolls of 1–5, deal 20d6 psychic, necrotic, force, radiant, or thunder damage respectively, half on success. On a failed save, 6 compels the target to spend its movement approaching the nearest visible creature and use its action to attack a random creature in reach, with a Wisdom save at each turn's end to stop. A 7 causes a level of Contamination at each turn's start, with a Constitution save at each turn's end to stop. An 8 adds two rolls and can repeat.
Each spell above consumes a 100 gp delerium fragment and gives its caster one level of Contamination.
Purge Contamination. One hour, touch. Consume 100 gp of alchemical fluids or holy water to clear a humanoid's Contamination and mutations. It gains one Exhaustion level per level removed.
Forced Evolution. Eight hours, touch. Consume a 250 gp alchemical mixture to replace one mutation with one selected by the GM or rolled randomly.
Siphon Contamination. One hour, touch. Consume 500 gp of alchemical fluids and a 5,000 gp delerium geode. A second willing humanoid takes all Contamination removed from a first willing humanoid, whose mutations are also removed. A transformed former humanoid can instead return to their original form if the second willing humanoid has at least their transformed CR in levels or CR. The recipient then undergoes Monstrous Transformation. Preventing the transfer makes the spell fail.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Contaminating Touch. Melee spell attack +8, reach 10 ft., one target, 10 (3d6) necrotic. DC 16 Constitution save or one level of Contamination.
Infest the Flesh (recharge 6). Each creature within 30 ft. makes a DC 16 Dexterity save. Failure deals 22 (5d8) necrotic and Restrains the creature. It takes 22 (5d8) necrotic at the start of each of the Pale Man's turns. It repeats the save at the end of its own turns to end the effect.

gm.title: Legendary Actions
lines:
Three legendary actions per round. Use one option after another creature's turn and recover spent actions at the start of this creature's turn.
Cantrip. Cast a cantrip.
Slither (2 actions). Move up to speed without provoking opportunity attacks.
Contaminate (3 actions). Each target Restrained by Infest the Flesh makes a DC 16 Constitution save or gains one level of Contamination.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Appendix A, pp. 212–213. Setting spells, Appendix D, pp. 227–229.

gm.title: Delerium contamination
lines:
Printed source. Appendix C, pp. 222–223.
Add contamination levels from each exposure. A contaminated character rolls 1d20 at the end of each long rest and gains one level on a 1.
Symptoms are cumulative. Level 1 has no symptom. Level 2 halves healing from Hit Dice. Level 3 prevents HP recovery from a long rest. Level 4 halves damage the creature deals with weapon attacks and spells. Level 5 makes it Incapacitated. Level 6 triggers Monstrous Transformation.
After a character gains a level, roll 1d6. On a result at or below the current level, the GM chooses a new mutation or rolls on the printed mutations table. Replace or reroll duplicate mutations.
Contamination does not wear off. Purge Contamination can remove levels and causes Exhaustion. Heal removes all contamination and mutations. Each level removed also removes one random mutation. At level 0, all symptoms and mutations end.
A contaminated humanoid rises as a Haze Husk 24 hours after death. It rises as a Haze Wight if it had at least six class levels or Hit Dice. Raising a creature from the dead reduces its contamination by one level.
Monstrous Transformation. At level 6 or higher, the creature transforms after one round. Replace its statistics, hit points, and Hit Dice with those of a monster the GM chooses. Contamination resets to 0, and the GM controls the transformed creature.
Wish or similar magic can restore one transformed creature, clearing its madness and contamination. Using Wish this way gives the caster a 33 percent chance of losing the ability to cast it again.

lines: Contaminating Touch and Infest the Flesh use their printed attack bonus and save DC. These differ from the general Spellcasting numbers.
The stat block lists Siphon Contamination among the 5th-level slots, but Appendix D defines it as a 6th-level spell. Table ruling. Use the Appendix D level when casting it.

gm.title: Description
lines: An infestation creates a problem to diagnose or survive, with a cure that can drive an adventure.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Rare, one infestation. Mindless, no treasure or magic resistance. Parasites neither gain Legacies nor become Afflicted.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Use one infestation procedure below. Parasites have no regular attacks. Award 15 XP for surviving a nonfatal infestation or 65 XP for surviving a potentially fatal one.

gm.title: Inheritor lice
lines: Roll d100 for the degree of infestation. Increase the host’s cinnabryl use by the same percentage, doubling it at 100%. Up to three times per day the lice can trigger Displace and move their host 10 feet in a random direction to evade an incoming physical hit. They sometimes do so at random. Cinnabryl ointment removes them. Saragón lyra birds eat them.

gm.title: Powder moth
lines: Use detect invisibility to see the moths. Roll d100 for the percentage of smokepowder spoiled. While the moths remain, anyone moving the keg saves vs. paralysis or sets it off. A full keg deals 10d6+10 damage within 10 feet and half damage out to 20 feet. Scale damage by the unspoiled fraction, then halve it on a successful save vs. breath weapon. Inheritors within 20 feet lose one week of cinnabryl protection per full 8 points of damage suffered.

gm.title: Jibarú pest
lines: Choose a local pest. A moth’s powder makes victims believe they can fly, and the moth can supply medicine for the Fly Affliction. A brown leech drains several HP of blood per week while preventing the Strength Affliction. A green territorial wasp’s sting kills on a failed save vs. poison. Its nest supplies an ointment that cures vermilia.

gm.title: Lupin plague
lines: Infested grapes or wine transmit the plague. The host saves vs. poison at −3 at the end of each day or dies. Medication or magical healing can end it.

gm.title: Cardinal tick
lines: Roll d100 for the starting infestation and use that percentage as the chance a Legacy fails. Participants in melee against an infested carrier acquire a 5% infestation. Each attempted Legacy use increases infestation by 15 percentage points. Nonhumanoids cap at 50%. Other Red Curse effects still apply. Cinnabryl ointment removes the ticks. Scratching them off costs 1 HP per percentage point removed without rare Jibarú medicine. Saragón lyra birds eat them.

gm.title: Vermilia
lines: Physical contact transmits the infection. Living creatures save vs. poison to avoid it. Undead catch it automatically. Damage starts at 1 on day one and doubles each day. Undead can avoid the day’s damage with a save vs. death magic at the end of that day, with a penalty equal to that day’s damage. All victims take an additional −1 on related saves per Legacy. Infection counts as a +2 weapon for damaging undead or magical creatures. Cure disease, heal or a remedy from vulturehound blood or a suitable Jibarú pest ends the infection. Fire cleanses infested remains.

gm.title: Description
lines: An elder fire elemental shaped like a vast bird. When freed from the Inner Planes, it travels from place to place setting fires.

gm.title: Damage resistances
lines: Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.

gm.title: Condition immunities
lines: Exhaustion, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained, stunned.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Fiery Death and Rebirth. When the phoenix dies, each creature in a 60-ft.-radius sphere centered on it makes a DC 20 Dexterity save, taking 22 (4d10) fire damage on a failure or half on a success. The blast ignites flammable objects that no one is wearing or carrying and destroys the phoenix's body.
The blast leaves a 5-pound, egg-shaped cinder immune to all damage. A creature that touches it takes 21 (6d6) fire damage at most once per round. A new phoenix hatches after 1d6 days.
Fire Form. Move through gaps as narrow as 1 inch without squeezing. A creature that touches the phoenix or hits it with a melee attack while within 5 ft. takes 5 (1d10) fire damage. The phoenix can enter a hostile creature's space and stop there. The first time it enters a creature's space on a turn, that creature takes 5 (1d10) fire damage. The phoenix can also ignite flammable objects it touches if they are unworn and uncarried. This takes no action.
Flyby. Flying out of an enemy's reach provokes no opportunity attacks.
Illumination. Shed bright light in a 60-ft. radius and dim light for another 30 ft.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). When the phoenix fails a save, it can spend a use to succeed.
Siege Monster. Deal double damage to objects and structures.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Beak attack and one Fiery Talons attack.
Beak. Melee weapon attack, +13 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 15 (2d6 + 8) fire damage.
Fiery Talons. Melee weapon attack, +13 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 17 (2d8 + 8) fire damage.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
The phoenix has 3 legendary actions and regains them at the start of its turn. Spend the stated cost on one option immediately after another creature's turn. It cannot use them while incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. If surprised, it must finish its first turn before using one.
Move (1 action). Move up to its speed.
Peck (1 action). Make one Beak attack.
Swoop (2 actions). Move up to its speed and make one Fiery Talons attack.

gm.title: Heraldic servant rules
lines:
Printed source. Heraldic Servant, General, pp. 44–46.
A heraldic servant has an inactive form on its coat of arms and two active forms, one natural and one humanoid. The rightful bearer can summon one servant at any time. It must touch the coat of arms to return to it or transfer to another coat of arms.
Use the same hit points in either active form. Unless the entry gives an exception, use the same Armor Class and magical powers as well. Weapons and movement may depend on form. An active servant automatically defends its bearer unless ordered otherwise. It can only be killed while active.
An active servant and its bearer can share thoughts and senses telepathically within one mile. While linked, the bearer counts as one experience level higher and shares the servant's spell immunities and magic resistance. While the servant is inactive, personally carrying its coat of arms grants the extra level and magic resistance. Check the individual entry for additional benefits.
The servant's death removes all benefits and permanently costs its bearer two levels. The servant can return at the bearer's deathbed if a new generation takes over. Three consecutive unworthy generations lose its service until two consecutive generations prove worthy.
A heraldic servant needs neither food nor sleep and earns no XP. It remains neutral or takes its bearer's alignment. The Red Curse cannot give it Legacies or Affliction.

gm.title: Traits
lines:

gm.title: Actions
lines:

A summoned devil departs early if it or the summoner dies or the summoner uses an action to dismiss it.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A tiny verminlike demon with green eyes and wiry tendrils, whose shape resembles local pests.

gm.title: Classification
lines: Tiny Fiend (Demon, Category 1), typically chaotic evil

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Poison damage immunity. Immune to Poisoned. Darkvision 60 ft., Soulsight 10 ft., passive Perception 8. Language Abyssal.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Horrid Stench. An enemy that starts its turn within 10 ft. of at least three pitlings becomes Poisoned until the start of its next turn.
Minion. An attack or failed save that deals damage drops the pitling to 0 HP. Other damage kills it if it deals at least 11 damage. It ignores smaller amounts from such effects.
Soul Feast. When the pitling reduces a creature other than a Construct or Undead to 0 HP, or deals damage to a dying creature, that creature makes a DC 11 Wisdom save. On failure it dies, its soul is consumed and the pitling becomes a Category 2 demon of the GM’s choice with 1 soul. Only Wish can restore the victim to life. If a group attack brought the victim to 0 HP, the GM picks one participating pitling to consume the soul.
Soulsight. The pitling can sense creatures within 10 ft. except Constructs and Undead. This counts as sight for features that require it. Physical objects, total cover, and supernatural effects do not block this sense unless a rule says they do.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Spit (Group Attack). Melee or ranged weapon attack +4, reach 5 ft. or range 15/30 ft., one target. Hit 4 poison damage.

gm.title: Minion rules
lines:
Group attack. Two to five pitlings on the same turn can each use an action to attack a target in reach or range of all of them. A single roll gets +4 plus the number joining. On a hit, deal 4 poison damage per pitling. A lone pitling uses +4. Advantage or disadvantage applies if every participant has it. Split attackers into separate rolls when cover or concealment differs. The target chooses which participant is affected by a response that can affect just one attacker.
Group opportunity attack. If the target provokes from multiple pitlings at once, each can use its reaction to join the melee Spit attack. Pitlings have no Hit Dice and cannot score critical hits.
Overkill. A weapon hit dealing more than 11 damage leaves surplus that can drop another eligible pitling for every 11 points of surplus damage or part thereof. Melee targets must be in reach. Ranged targets must lie on the line from the attacker through the original target within the weapon’s short range. Opportunity attacks cannot deal overkill damage.

lines:

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Forceful Slam. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit 10 (3d6) force damage.
Telekinetic Thrust. Choose one Medium or smaller creature or unattended object of up to 150 lb. within 30 ft. Against a creature, contest the poltergeist's Charisma check with the target's Strength check. If the poltergeist wins, it hurls the creature up to 30 ft. in any direction, including up. If the creature then hits a hard surface or heavy object, it takes 1d6 damage per 10 ft. moved. The text leaves the damage type unspecified. An object nobody is wearing or carrying can be hurled up to 30 ft. in any direction without a check. The poltergeist can use that object to make a ranged attack at +4 against one creature in its path, dealing 5 (2d4) bludgeoning damage on a hit.

lines: The poltergeist is Invisible. Replace Life Drain with Forceful Slam and Telekinetic Thrust.

An unattended object can be hurled up to 30 ft. without a contest. It can hit one creature along its path with a ranged attack at +4 for 5 (2d4) bludgeoning damage.

lines: The World Eater is an incarnation of the hydra’s eternal form. Its return portends strife among the gods and danger for Theros.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Acidic Blood. After Polukranos takes piercing or slashing damage, each creature within 5 ft. of it takes 10 (3d6) acid damage.
Hold Breath. Polukranos can go without a breath for up to 1 hour.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). Polukranos can turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Multiple Heads. Polukranos starts with five heads. While it has more than one, it has advantage on saves against being blinded, charmed, deafened, frightened, stunned, or knocked unconscious. Taking 40 or more damage during a single turn kills one head. Losing every head kills Polukranos. At the end of its own turn, it grows two heads for each head lost since its last turn, unless it has taken at least 40 fire damage since its last turn. It heals 20 HP for each head it regrows.
Reactive Heads. Each head beyond the first grants an extra reaction for opportunity attacks only.
Siege Monster. Polukranos deals double damage to objects and structures.
Wakeful. At least one head remains awake when Polukranos sleeps.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack per living head.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +13 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 18 (2d10 + 7) piercing damage.

Tail. Melee weapon attack, +13 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 18 (2d10 + 7) bludgeoning damage. A creature hit must pass a DC 21 Strength save or be pushed up to 20 ft. away from Polukranos.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:

Detect (1 action). Make a Wisdom (Perception) check.

Trampling Charge (3 actions). Move up to 50 ft. in a straight line. Polukranos can pass through spaces occupied by Huge or smaller creatures. The first time Polukranos enters each creature’s space during this move, it can make a Stomp attack against that creature.

lines:

lines: Breastplate and shield. Saving throws Dex +5, Wis +10, Cha +8. Deception +8, Insight +10, Persuasion +8, Religion +3. Immune to psychic damage and to Charmed and Frightened. Darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 17. Speaks Common and Elvish.

Elf Glamour (1/day). When a creature targets Ellan with an attack, power, or spell, it makes a DC 18 Wisdom save or becomes Charmed by him through the end of his next turn. No action required.
Resolute Aura. While Ellan is conscious, he and any allies within 20 ft. who can see him are immune to Charmed and Frightened.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Bladed Scepter attacks.
Bladed Scepter. Melee weapon attack +10, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 11 (1d8 + 7) bludgeoning plus 10 (3d6) poison damage. The target makes a DC 18 Constitution save or is Poisoned for 1 minute. It can save again at the end of each turn.
Command (2nd-level spell). Speak a one-word order to up to two visible creatures within 60 ft. On a failed DC 18 Wisdom save, a target follows the order on its next turn. The spell has no effect on Undead, targets who understand neither Common nor Elvish, or those who would be directly harmed by obeying. It ends if the target cannot comply. Approach makes the target advance by the shortest route and end its turn when within 5 ft. Drop makes it release held objects and end its turn. Flee makes it spend its turn getting away as quickly as possible. Grovel makes it fall Prone and end its turn. Halt forbids movement and actions.
Unholy Flame (3rd-level spell). A visible creature within 60 ft. makes a DC 18 Dexterity save. Failure deals 27 (6d8) fire damage and envelops the creature in flame. While enveloped it takes 7 (2d6) fire damage at the start of its turns and can save to end the effect at the end of each turn. Success on the initial save halves the damage and avoids the ongoing flames.

gm.title: Villain Party Action
lines:
Soulbinders. The party can use one villain party action per round, after an enemy's turn. Each action is available once per encounter, in any order. The member taking it must be present and able to act.
Action 1, Battle Cry. Enemies who hear Ellan within 60 ft. make DC 18 Wisdom saves. On a failure, they have disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls through the end of their next turns.

gm.title: Recoverable Magic Item
lines:
Crown of Majesty. Very rare. Attunement required. The wearer resists psychic damage and is immune to Charmed and Frightened. The crown holds 3 charges. Spend an action and 1 charge to cast Command or Charm Person, DC 18. It regains 1d3 spent charges at dawn.
Cursed Sentience. The item uses its Soulbinder's alignment, mental ability scores, and languages. It hears and sees in darkness within 60 ft. and can speak to its wearer telepathically. Break attunement with Remove Curse or equivalent magic. After seven days attuned and every 24 hours after that, make a DC 18 Wisdom save. Each failure reduces Wisdom by 1 while attuned. On the third failure, the Soulbinder takes control and changes the wearer's body, statistics, and equipment to match its own. The wearer remains aware. Breaking attunement restores the body and control. The Soulbinder returns to the item when attunement ends or the body dies. After 1d6 + 12 months of possession, the victim's soul and body are destroyed. The full group ritual for permanently lifting the curse is on p. 382.

lines: A pseudodragon willing to form a familiar bond with a companion.

gm.title: Senses
lines: Blindsight 10 ft., darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 13.

gm.title: Languages
lines: Understands Common and Draconic. It can't speak.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Keen Senses. It has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that use sight, hearing, or smell.
Magic Resistance. It has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Limited Telepathy. It can magically send simple thoughts, feelings, or images to a creature within 100 ft. that understands a language.
Familiar. The pseudodragon forms a magical telepathic bond with a willing creature. The companion can share the pseudodragon's senses while they are within 1 mile of each other and gains the benefit of Magic Resistance while within 10 ft. The pseudodragon may end its service and the bond at any time.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage.
Sting. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage. The target makes a DC 11 Constitution save or is Poisoned for 1 hour. On a failure by 5 or more, it also falls Unconscious for the same duration. Damage or another creature using an action to shake it awake ends the Unconscious condition early.

gm.title: Encounter context
lines: Psurlons return from the Deep Astral about once a century for the seven-year Feast of Worlds. They infiltrate settlements and sometimes partner with a Mind Flayer that consumes their victims’ brains. Githyanki raid their astral strongholds because of this alliance. A Psurlon Leader can oversee a raid and a Psurlon Ringer can infiltrate a settlement.

gm.title: Life cycle
lines: Other psurlons hide the corpse of one of their own and lay eggs in it. Tiny worms hatch after 24 hours and feed on the corpse and one another. After seven days, the lone survivor emerges as an adult.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Spelljammer: Adventures in Space, Boo's Astral Menagerie, p. 44.

gm.title: Description

lines: A Psurlon must eat the specific Medium Humanoid it wants to imitate, then spend 8 hours in a psionic trance. It takes the victim’s appearance, memories and languages. The victim’s class features and other abilities do not transfer. The ringer is still an Aberration, and other psurlons recognize it. Only Wish can reverse the permanent transformation.

lines: A gray, liquid creature easily mistaken for wet stone. This variety can attack with its mind.

lines: Uses the Gray Ooze base profile with Intelligence 6 and the additional Psychic Crush action.

gm.title: Condition immunities
lines: Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Exhaustion, Frightened, Prone.

gm.title: Senses
lines: Blindsight 60 ft. It is blind beyond that radius. Passive Perception 8.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Amorphous. The ooze can pass through a gap as narrow as 1 inch without squeezing.
Corrode Metal. After a hit from a nonmagical metal weapon, that weapon permanently loses 1 from its damage rolls. Penalties stack and destroy it at −5. Nonmagical metal ammunition is destroyed after it hits and deals damage. The ooze can eat through 2 inches of nonmagical metal in one round.
False Appearance. A motionless ooze looks like an oily puddle or wet rock.
Ooze Nature. It needs no sleep.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Pseudopod. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 4 (1d6 + 1) bludgeoning plus 7 (2d6) acid damage. Nonmagical metal armor worn by the target takes a permanent, stacking −1 penalty to the AC it offers. The armor breaks once its AC drops to 10.

lines: Set Intelligence to 6. Add Psychic Crush, recharge 5–6. One sensed target within 60 feet attempts a DC 10 Intelligence save. It takes 3d6 psychic on failure, or half on success.

gm.title: Description
lines: A column of funeral flame scatters sparks from charred bones. It sets corpses alight and sends them careening through the fight.

gm.title: Classification
lines: Medium Elemental (Fire, Mists). Medium size tier shown in header.

gm.title: Medium size tier
lines:
Medium elemental (Fire, Mists). CR 3. 26 HP (4d8 + 8). Initiative +7. Speed 50 ft..
AC 16, touch 13, flat-footed 13. Base attack +3, grapple +4. Space 5 ft., reach 5 ft.
Attack Slam +6 melee (1d6 + 1 plus 1d6 fire). Full attack Slam +6 melee (1d6 + 1 plus 1d6 fire).
Fort +3, Ref +7, Will +1. Str 12, Dex 17, Con 14, Int 5, Wis 11, Cha 11. Listen +5, Spot +5.
Feats include Improved Initiative, Weapon Finesse. Advancement 5–7 HD, Medium.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Slam. Make one melee slam, or use the full-attack count in the chosen tier. Each slam deals the indicated bludgeoning and fire damage.
Burn (Ex). A creature hit by the slam makes a Reflex save or burns for 1d4 rounds. Use DC 10 + half the elemental’s HD + its Dexterity modifier. A burning creature can put out the fire with a move action. A creature that hits the elemental with a natural weapon or unarmed strike first takes the slam’s fire damage, then makes the same save to avoid catching fire.
Dance of Death (Su). As a free action, touch a corpse of a formerly living corporeal creature within reach. It rises as a skeleton or zombie according to the corpse’s condition, rushes about attacking creatures and setting fires at random, and adds the effect of a direct hit with alchemist’s fire to its own attacks. That adds 1d6 fire on impact and another 1d6 the following round. A burning target can use a full-round action and a DC 15 Reflex save to extinguish it before that second damage roll. The animated body itself takes 1d3 fire each round until consumed.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Darkvision 60 ft. Immune to poison, sleep, paralysis, stunning, critical hits, and flanking. Does not eat, sleep, or breathe. It cannot be raised or resurrected, though limited wish, wish, miracle, or true resurrection can restore it. The fire subtype grants fire immunity and cold vulnerability, increasing cold damage by 50%. A pyre belonging to an exceptionally evil person can bring forth an elemental of the next larger size tier even if the caster cannot control it.

gm.title: Other size tiers
lines: Small, Large, Huge, Greater, and Elder are listed below. Each uses the same actions and traits with its own statistics.

lines: Solitary, always neutral evil, no treasure. May appear in any environment.

gm.title: Dread elemental rules
lines:
Printed source. Elemental, Dread, p. 63, and Mists subtype, pp. 7–8.
In Ravenloft, calling a standard elemental has a 20% chance of producing a dread elemental. Summoning magic always produces the dread form. Accidental dread elementals are uncontrolled, and the Dark Powers supply the matching materials. Intentional conjuring requires the matching material and uses the usual chance for the elemental to break control.
Dread elementals understand speech but do not communicate. Their Mists subtype makes them native throughout Ravenloft and allows them to be summoned in any domain. A dismissed dread elemental returns to Ravenloft itself, so the realm's restrictions on calling do not break the calling pact.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: Burn’s explicit DC formula uses Dexterity. The next sentence calls it Constitution-based. Use the explicit formula at the table. The DCs are 12, 15, 19, 25, 28, and 31 in size-tier order. Using Constitution instead gives 11, 14, 17, 22, 24, and 26.

Burn does not state ongoing damage. Use the core 3.5 catching-on-fire damage of 1d6 fire per round until the printed 1d4-round duration ends or the victim extinguishes it. The listed Greater slam damage of 1d8 + 7 is intentional here.

gm.title: Description
lines: A towering skeleton burns from within with blue fire. Its flames can shrink to a candle-sized flicker when it has stood idle for 48 hours.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Initiative +5. AC 16 (−1 size, +1 Dex, +6 natural), touch 10, flat-footed 15. Base attack +2, grapple +6. Space 5 ft., reach 10 ft. Fort +1, Ref +2, Will +4. Alertness, Improved Initiative. Any land or underground. Any organization. No treasure. Always neutral. Advancement 6–15 HD (Huge), 16–25 HD (Gargantuan).

lines:
Attack. Claw +6 melee (1d6+4).
Full attack. Two claws +5 melee (1d6+4 each) or huge scythe +7 melee (2d6+6).
Fireball (Su), 1/hour. Cast an 8d6 fireball, Reflex DC 14 half.
Keen Edge (Su). Its flame applies keen edge to slashing weapons it holds. A nonmagical weapon it holds slowly becomes a huge bone scythe over a few months. This power leaves the claw attacks unchanged.

gm.title: Traits

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Evasion. For a Dexterity save that would halve damage, Qar takes none on a success and half on a failure.
Exploit Opening (3/day). Gain advantage on an attack roll Qar makes.
Supernatural Resistance. Qar has advantage on saves against powers, spells, and other supernatural effects.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three Unarmed Strikes. If the same creature is hit by all three, it is Dazed until the end of its next turn.
Unarmed Strike. Melee weapon attack +7, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 8 (1d6 + 5) bludgeoning damage.
Iron Ring (2/day). Teleport to the Cyst. From inside the Cyst, teleport to somewhere Qar has visited.

gm.title: Reactions
lines:
No Survivors. When a visible enemy within 40 ft. drops to 0 HP, move up to Qar's speed. If he ends that move within 5 ft. of an enemy, he can make an Unarmed Strike against that enemy.
Voice Stealer (3/day). When an enemy within 30 ft. that Qar can hear finishes casting a spell with a verbal component, it must pass a DC 15 Intelligence save or lose the ability to speak for 1 minute, with an end-of-turn save.

gm.title: Villain Party Action
lines:
Black Iron Pact. The party may use one villain party action per round after an enemy's turn. Each action is available once per encounter, in any order, and requires its performer to be present and able to act.
Action 1. Party Tactics. Qar and each ally within 60 ft. who can see or hear him can move up to their speed.

gm.title: Dazed (MCDM)
lines: On its turn a Dazed creature can move, take an action, or take a bonus action. It chooses one. Becoming Dazed during its turn ends the turn. Extra actions from effects such as Haste or Action Surge are still available. Cure Ailment, Lesser Restoration, and Greater Restoration can remove Dazed.

gm.title: Description
lines: An Emerald Enclave guide based at Fort Beluarian who travels with the vegepygmy Kupalué. He deliberately takes routes through undead territory to help drive the undead out of Chult.

4th-level druid, Wisdom, save DC 12, +4 to hit with spell attacks. Treat him as a druid for magic item use and attunement requirements.

1st level (4 slots). Entangle, Longstrider, Speak with Animals, Thunderwave.
2nd level (3 slots). Animal Messenger, Barkskin.

gm.title: Actions

gm.title: Guide

He recommends buying an exploration charter before leaving Fort Beluarian because the Flaming Fist mistreats unlicensed explorers.

gm.title: Description
lines: The Silent Decay uses acid and living shadows and wants to blot out the sun.

gm.title: Other statistics
